This revises §58A's "v1 is frozen with VC-7-02's implementation … every later change … is a new version" for `DE_CASH_TIMING@1` only. `DE_CATEGORY_DEFAULTS@1` stays frozen as it is.

**Why a section of its own, after §58E:** VC-X-39 is a backlog item of its own and changes a Phase-7 rule (§58A) that §58C and §58E read. It belongs with the Phase-7 sections, so it is §58F and comes after §58E, not as a §59 letter: §59 to §59F are Phase 8. §58A, §58C and §58E keep their statements, and this section names where each one changes.

### As the code stands (main, before VC-X-39)

- **The assumption is made in `rentTiming`.** Without a due day for the term, the term's first day is the due date, with `dueDateSource: 'PERIOD_START'` and `periodGuessed: false` (`domains/taxation/cash-timing.ts:68–79`). The comment there (`:73–77`) justifies it with § 556b Abs. 1 BGB: rent is due "at the latest by the 3rd working day".
  - A term has no due day in three cases: no RentalContractReference for the Tenant, an empty list, or a term before the first entry (`dueDayOn`, `domains/rental-contract-reference/reference.ts:51–59`).
  - The rent's timing is read in `infrastructure/postgres/tax-source-facts.ts:186–214` (`dueDays.get(…) ?? null`, `:213`).
- **The assumption moves the year.** `attributeTaxYear` (`cash-timing.ts:217–263`) works in four steps:
  - it pushes `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` for any `PERIOD_START` (`:233–234`);
  - it moves the year when the economic year lies across the year-end and the due date lies in the same window (`:235–236`);
  - only a guessed period stops the move. That is Hausgeld's `ECONOMIC_PERIOD_ASSUMED` (`:238–242`);
  - every other timing sets `moves = true` with `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (`:244–248`), and `taxYear` becomes the economic year (`:254`).

  So a rent's `PERIOD_START` moves the year exactly as a recorded day does.
- **The assumption can only move rent forward.** The first day of a December term (1 December) never lies in the window, which starts on 22 December. The first day of a January term does. So the assumption moves exactly one case: a January rent (or advance) paid from 22 to 31 December, which goes to the following year. It never moves a December rent paid late back into December's year. That move needs a recorded day from 22 to 31.
- **Hausgeld is already as the report wants.** `hausgeldTiming` sets `periodGuessed: true` always (`cash-timing.ts:94–113`), and `PERIOD_START` when the plan has no `advanceDueDay` (`:110`). It never moves, and the user decides with `taxYear`.
- **Loan interest moves on its schedule's payment date** (`LOAN_SCHEDULE`, `:121–139`). That is a recorded fact (§41.4), not an assumption. *(Since VC-X-53, §58O rule 8: the schedule pays every `paymentIntervalMonths` months, and the plan's first entry's period runs over its interval; the due date is the nearest entry of the contract plan, never the rebased one; `DE_CASH_TIMING@1` unchanged; whether intervals above 1 are „regelmäßig wiederkehrend“ is open with the Steuerberater, `beratungsfragen.md` §3, unconfirmed until answered.)*
- **The review closes the flags with any confirmed classification.** `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` and `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` are in `CONFIRMABLE` (`domains/taxation/tax-year-review.ts:13–20`). Each is open until a classification in `USER_CONFIRMED` or `ADVISOR_CONFIRMED` stands for the item (`:54`).
  - A create defaults to `USER_CONFIRMED` (§56).
  - So a classification of the rent's treatment, made for any reason and without `taxYear`, closes both and accepts the moved year.
- **The rule has no parameter for it.** `DE_CASH_TIMING@1` has `windowDays` and `recurringCategories` only (`domains/taxation/rules/de-cash-timing.ts:18–30`). Which due-date sources may move a year is code (`cash-timing.ts:238–244`), not the rule's (AGENTS.md §16).
- **`DE_CASH_TIMING@1` is not pinned, and nothing stores it.**
  - Pins: `infrastructure/hashing/frozen-rules.test.ts:16–28` pins `DE_CATEGORY_DEFAULTS@1` and the three AfA versions only, although §58A calls `@1` frozen.
  - Classifications: they store `rule` (`DE_CATEGORY_DEFAULTS`) and `treatmentRule` (§56, `domains/taxation/classification-checks.ts:157–200`), never the cash rule.
  - The derived attribution: it names `DE_CASH_TIMING@1` only on read (`tax-year-review.ts:110–113`).
  - Recorded versions: they store AfA rules only (§60).

  So no stored hash and no start check (`infrastructure/postgres/tax-rule-check.ts:27–53`) depends on it. Its hash today (`ruleVersionHash`, on main 92e2d22) is `b7fa5cf1648fb12179487933fd305f895983853021362877ff6c4c38a74487f8`.
- **The derived year feeds two further places.** The first is §58E's history: `attributionChanges` computes each candidate's year under the list before and after each amendment with `attributeTaxYear(…, rentTiming(term, list), override, registry)` (`domains/taxation/attribution-changes.ts:106–137`, `:121`). A reference's `CREATED` record is only the base of that history and is never a change (`:87–100`). The second is the classification create's `refundOfYear` bound without `taxYear` (`infrastructure/postgres/tax-classification-store.ts:207–208`, `domains/taxation/classification-checks.ts:194–195`).
- **Tests that assert the move under the assumption:**
  - `cash-timing.test.ts:51–60`;
  - `infrastructure/postgres/tax-year-repository.test.ts:63–72`;
  - `tax-year.e2e.test.ts:228–231`.

  The flag levels are asserted in `tax-year-view.test.ts:772–785`.

### The rule (§58A, amended)

The exception of §58A applies when **all four** hold. The fourth condition is new:
1. the booking date is in the window;
2. the due date is in the same window;
3. the economic year differs from the booking year;
4. **the due date is recorded:** its `dueDateSource` is one of the rule's `dueDate.recordedSources`, and the period is not guessed.

Conditions 1–3 decide the **proposal**. Condition 4 decides whether the proposal is **applied**:

| Case (1–3 hold) | `taxYear` | `attribution.proposedYear` | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|
| recorded due date (`RENTAL_CONTRACT_REFERENCE`, `LOAN_SCHEDULE`), period known | economic year | economic year | `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (unchanged) |
| period guessed (Hausgeld; any due-date source) | booking year | guessed year | `ECONOMIC_PERIOD_ASSUMED` (unchanged), and `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` before it when `PERIOD_START` |
| **due date not recorded (`PERIOD_START`), period known (rent)** | **booking year** | economic year | `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED`, then the new **`PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`** |
| any of the above with a classification's `taxYear` | `taxYear` | as above | as above; `overridden: true` |

- **When 1–3 do not hold**, nothing changes. A rent in the window whose term starts its own year (paid 2 January for January) carries `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` alone, informative as today. So does a December rent paid late without a due day: its assumed due date, 1 December, lies outside the window, so there is no proposal, and it is never moved back on an assumed due date (decided by the owner on 2026-11-02, open question 4).
- **`PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`** is the rent's counterpart of `ECONOMIC_PERIOD_ASSUMED`: "the rule would move this split if its due date were the one assumed". Its `details` are `{ bookingDate, dueDate, economicPeriod, dueDateSource, proposedYear }`: the keys of `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` plus `proposedYear`. A new code, not a new meaning for an existing one (decided by the owner on 2026-11-02, open question 1).
- **What the person can do:** two ways decide the year. A third way does not.
  - **Record the due day** (`rentDueDays` on the Tenant's RentalContractReference, §58A). Day 1–10 then applies the proposal for every term the entry covers, flagged `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`. Day 11–31 keeps the booking year without a flag. Both of the Transaction's rent splits follow (`RENT_BASE` and `RENT_OPERATING_COST_ADVANCE`).
    - **The entry suffices technically** (decided by the owner on 2026-11-02, open question 3): it is the person's statement from the lease. It may carry an optional **`evidenceReference`** (trimmed, 1–500: the lease or its clause, e.g. „Mietvertrag § 4 Abs. 1 (synthetisch)“), which the UI offers and recommends. An entry without one is not refused and moves the year all the same.
    - The item's `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE.details` gain `dueDateEvidence` (the entry's `evidenceReference`, or `null`), so a reviewer sees which due dates rest on a named document. The reference's `sourceReferences` stay as they are.
  - **Set `taxYear`** on the split's classification, either the booking year or the proposed year. This decides one split. The advance split needs its own classification.
  - **Confirming a classification without `taxYear` decides nothing** (decided by the owner on 2026-11-02, open question 2): only an explicit, confirmed tax-year decision or a recorded due date closes the proposal; a general confirmation of the classification does not.
- **Unchanged for Hausgeld:** a recorded `advanceDueDay` still never moves it (the period is guessed). The table's second row decides before condition 4 is read.
- **Unchanged for Loan interest:** `LOAN_SCHEDULE` is a recorded source. VC-X-40 changes how interest is allocated, not its year.

### The parameter, in place (the owner's decision of 2026-11-01)

| Rule | Parameter | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `DE_CASH_TIMING@1` | `dueDate` (new) | `{ recordedSources: ["RENTAL_CONTRACT_REFERENCE", "ECONOMIC_PLAN", "LOAN_SCHEDULE"], legalBasis: "§ 11 Abs. 1 S. 2, Abs. 2 S. 2 EStG", source: "Prüfbericht 2026-11-01, Frage 18 (mündlich bestätigt durch den Steuerberater, laut Projektinhaber am 2026-11-01)" }` |

- **What stays and what changes:** `windowDays` 10, `recurringCategories`, `title`, `legalBasis` and `effectiveFrom` 2000-01-01 are unchanged. The rule's `source` gains the change note "VC-X-39 in place: Prüfbericht 2026-11-01, Frage 18 (mündlich bestätigt durch den Steuerberater, laut Projektinhaber am 2026-11-01); owner decision 2026-11-01, api-design §58F".
- **Code:** `attributeTaxYear` reads `rule.parameters.dueDate.recordedSources`, never a constant.
  - `ECONOMIC_PLAN` is listed because a recorded `advanceDueDay` is a recorded due date. Hausgeld still does not move, because its period is guessed.
  - The type is `readonly string[]`, as `recurringCategories` is. `rules/` does not import `DueDateSource` from `cash-timing.ts`, which imports the rule.
  - A registry test asserts that every listed value is a `DueDateSource` and that `PERIOD_START` is not among them.
- **`GET /tax-rules`** shows the new parameter. That is the only visible change to a route besides the flag.
- **Pinned hash:** `frozen-rules.test.ts` gains `['DE_CASH_TIMING', 1, <the hash after the change>]`, with a comment naming question 18, the owner's decision and the hash before (`b7fa5cf1…87f8`, never pinned).
  - If §59D or §59F lands first, its pin of `DE_ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE@1` sits beside this one. Neither change touches the other's rule.
  - From the documented go-live of the first productive installation on, a change of `DE_CASH_TIMING` is `@2`, and this literal is never updated again.
- **`DE_CATEGORY_DEFAULTS@1`, `DE_WEG_SPENDING@1`, `DE_82B_DISTRIBUTION@1`, `DE_ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE@1`** and the AfA rules are not changed.

### The review (§58C, amended)

| Flag | Level |
|---|---|
| `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (new; an item flag in the booking year and a year flag in the proposed year, decided 2026-11-02) | **open** until a current classification in `USER_CONFIRMED` or `ADVISOR_CONFIRMED` sets `taxYear` (`attribution.overridden: true`), whichever of the two years it names; then informative, at both places. A recorded due day removes the flag at both places, because the split is then attributed or stays in its booking year by a recorded date. Nothing else closes it. |
| `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` | unchanged (open while no confirmed classification stands for the item). The flag now says only that the due date is not recorded: it no longer moves anything. |
| `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`, `ECONOMIC_PERIOD_ASSUMED`, `NO_ECONOMIC_PERIOD` | unchanged |

- **`flagIsOpen`** (`tax-year-review.ts:51–56`) takes the item's `attribution.overridden` for the new code. A `NEEDS_REVIEW` classification with `taxYear` leaves it open, as for every confirmable flag.
- **Both years** (decided by the owner on 2026-11-02, open question 9): the open attribution is visible in both years it may belong to, and counted in one.
  - **The booking year** shows the split as an item, in its figures, with the open item flag. `review.open` counts it per item, as every item flag.
  - **The proposed year** does not list the split and does not count it (§58A's per-year list holds the splits whose tax year is Y). It carries the **year flag `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`**, open, `details: { items: [{ sourceId, bookingDate, bookingYear, proposedYear, amount }] }` sorted by `sourceId`. Its splits are those booked in the window at the proposed year's start whose proposal names that year; the view reads them in its snapshot with the windows it already reads for §58E's Part 1, so no second read range is added.
  - **No double counting:** the amount is in exactly one year's figures, the booking year's or the year a confirmed `taxYear` names. The other year shows it in the flag only.
  - **No unrestricted `final`:** while the proposal is open, neither year is `final`. Once a `taxYear` is confirmed or a due day recorded, the item counts in the decided year, the flag is informative (with `taxYear`) or gone (with a due day) at both places, and each year is judged by §58C's other conditions.
- **Owners:** the per-owner parts are unchanged, since the share date is the booking date (§58C). An assumed January rent now stays in its booking year, so it no longer carries `SHARE_DATE_OUTSIDE_TAX_YEAR` (informative).

### Texts for the user (German; proposals for the UI)

The UI texts live in `docs/development/ui-guide.md`, which this spec does not change. These are the proposals:

- `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`: „Für diese Miete ist keine Fälligkeit erfasst. Ohne nachgewiesene Fälligkeit bleibt das Zahlungsjahr {bookingYear} maßgeblich. Nach der Zehntageregel gehörte die Zahlung in {proposedYear}, wenn sie am {dueDate} fällig war. Bitte die Fälligkeit im Mietverhältnis erfassen oder das Steuerjahr festlegen.“
- `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` (revised): „Keine Fälligkeit erfasst. Der {dueDate} dient nur als Vorschlag; das Steuerjahr folgt der Zahlung.“
- `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` as the proposed year's year flag: „{count} Mietzahlung(en) aus {bookingYear} könnten nach der Zehntageregel zu {proposedYear} gehören. Ohne nachgewiesene Fälligkeit zählen sie in {bookingYear}. Das Jahr ist nicht abschließend, bis die Fälligkeit erfasst oder das Steuerjahr festgelegt ist.“
- The due-day entry's evidence field: „Beleg der Fälligkeit (empfohlen)“, with the hint „z. B. Mietvertrag mit der Klausel zur Fälligkeit“.

### Effect on existing data, §58E, ACC7 and the stages

- **Existing data, no backfill** (decided by the owner on 2026-11-02, open question 6). Nothing is stored per split, so every assumed January rent paid in late December returns to its booking year on the first read after the deployment, flagged `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`.
  - **Classifications with `taxYear`** are unchanged: the override wins, and the flag is informative once confirmed.
  - **Confirmed classifications without `taxYear`** do not change the year. Under the old rule they closed `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` on the moved year. Now they leave `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` open: the person confirmed a year that the rule no longer proposes as the tax year, so the year is shown again for a decision, never kept silently.
  - **No AuditRecord marks the deployment.** It is a change of the rule, not of an input, so §58E does not flag it. That is acceptable only because no productive installation exists: the Phase-7 freeze point is its documented go-live. After it, a change is `@2`, and the item names it as `RULE_SUPERSEDED` does today.
- **The `refundOfYear` bound** without `taxYear` follows the derived year (`classification-checks.ts:194–195`). For an assumed January rent paid in December that is now the booking year, so a `refundOfYear` of the following year is `422 REFUND_YEAR_OUT_OF_RANGE` without `taxYear`. The database guard (booking year + 1) is unchanged.
- **§58E (VC-X-28, specified, not implemented):** Part 1 computes "before" and "after" with the rule as it now stands. This changes which amendments flag a year:
  - **An amendment from no due day to a day 1–10** for a January term paid in late December now moves the rent from the booking year to January's year. Recorded after the end of a year it touches, it raises `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED` in that year, and in both years when it is recorded after both have ended. Under the old rule it moved nothing, because the assumption gave the same year. The reverse amendment moves the rent back and is flagged the same way.
  - **An amendment from a day 11–31 to no due day** no longer moves anything (booking year under both). Today it moves the rent forward and is flagged.
  - **A reconciliation confirmed late without a due day** (§58E open question 5) now moves nothing: `NO_ECONOMIC_PERIOD` before and `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` after both give the booking year. With a recorded day it moves and is flagged, as proposed there.
  - **The `CREATED` record of a reference.** From VC-X-39 on, creating a reference after the year end with a day 1–10 moves such a rent out of a closed year. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02 (open question 7):** §58E counts that record as a change (kind `RENT_DUE_DAYS_CREATED`, §58E Part 1), so the move is flagged like an amendment. Until VC-X-28 is implemented, the moved item carries `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (open until confirmed) and the closed year gets no year flag; VC-X-28 closes that gap.
  - **Fingerprints:** an acknowledgement covers `items` with `yearBefore`/`yearAfter`. If §58E is implemented before VC-X-39, a change whose years VC-X-39 alters gets another fingerprint and opens again, as §58E intends.
- **ACC7** (`phase-7-acceptance.e2e.test.ts`) has **no figure change**.
  - Its one rent in a window is December's, paid 2028-01-04 (`:327–336`), and its RentalContractReference records day 31 from the start of the tenancy (`:337–338`). The due date 2027-12-31 is recorded, so the rent still moves to 2027 with `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (`:580–585`).
  - The totals stay as they are, for example `einnahmen` 13,284.01 with `RENT` 10,800.00.
  - Its Hausgeld (the 15th) and interest (the 20th) lie outside every window.
  - **ACC8** books its rents on the 15th and is not touched either (`phase-8-acceptance.e2e.test.ts:93`). It stays unchanged: the decision on open question 8 names ACC7 only.
- **ACC7 gains a case without a due date and its explicit resolution** (decided by the owner on 2026-11-02, open question 8). It runs on a PropertyReference and Tenant of its own, without a RentalContractReference, so the figures ACC7 asserts today stay as they are; the step's amounts are asserted on their own, and a changed existing figure is a finding to explain, not to adjust:
  - a January rent paid on 29 December of a year Y stays in Y with `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` and `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` open, Y + 1 carries the year flag, and neither year is `final` through it;
  - a general confirmation of the classification without `taxYear` leaves both open;
  - the explicit resolution, a confirmed classification with `taxYear` (or, in a variant, the Tenant's `rentDueDays` recorded with its `evidenceReference`), closes it, and the amount counts in exactly one year.
- **VC-X-45 and the AfA:** the tax-year view is not the AfA recording. No AfA component reads a rent's tax year. The only cash years §59B reads are those of capitalised sources (§58A), and §59E's interest keeps its schedule's year. So VC-X-39 changes no AfA figure, no `inputFingerprint`, no recorded version and no stage of VC-X-45. `DEPRECIATION_RECORDING_ENABLED` is not read. VC-X-39 is a prerequisite of the Phase-7 go-live, not of recording stage 1.

### Tests the implementation must have

- **Domain** (`cash-timing.test.ts`, replacing `:51–60`). Synthetic figures, window 2026/27:
  - **A January rent paid on 2026-12-29 without a due day** stays in 2026. Its flags are exactly `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` and `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (`dueDate` 2027-01-01, `dueDateSource` `PERIOD_START`, `proposedYear` 2027). Its `attribution` is `{ bookingYear: 2026, proposedYear: 2027, overridden: false }`.
  - **With `rentDueDays` day 1** it moves to 2027, `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` alone with `dueDateSource` `RENTAL_CONTRACT_REFERENCE`. Day 3 does the same. Day 15 keeps 2026 without a flag.
  - **A term before the first entry** behaves as with no due day.
  - **The same split with `taxYear` 2027** goes to 2027 with `overridden: true`, and `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` stays in its flags. With `taxYear` 2026: 2026, `overridden: true`.
  - **A December rent paid on 2027-01-05, due on 1 December** (recorded day 1) stays in 2027 without a flag. Its due date lies outside the window. **Without a due day:** 2027, `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` alone, no proposal.
  - **`RENT_OPERATING_COST_ADVANCE`** behaves as `RENT_BASE` in each case above.
  - **Non-recurring categories never move:** `MAINTENANCE` and `OTHER_INCOME` booked 2026-12-29 stay in 2026 without a flag, whatever the timing passed.
  - **Unchanged:** Hausgeld (`advanceDueDay` 1 and `null`) and interest, as today (`:105–180`).
  - **The parameter is read:**
    - a test registry whose copy of `@1` adds `PERIOD_START` to `recordedSources` moves the assumed rent again (`ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`);
    - a copy without `RENTAL_CONTRACT_REFERENCE` leaves the day-3 rent in 2026 with `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`;
    - a copy with `ECONOMIC_PLAN` removed changes nothing for Hausgeld.
- **Review** (`tax-year-view.test.ts`, beside `:772–785`): `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` is open on a `DEFAULT` item, open with a `USER_CONFIRMED` classification without `taxYear`, informative with `USER_CONFIRMED` or `ADVISOR_CONFIRMED` and `taxYear` (either year), and open with `NEEDS_REVIEW` and `taxYear`. A year with it open is not `final`, and `review.open` counts it per item.
- **Both years** (`tax-year-view.test.ts`, decided 2026-11-02): the January rent paid on 2026-12-29 without a due day counts in 2026's figures only; 2027 carries the year flag with the split's id and amount, does not count it, and is not `final`; with a confirmed `taxYear` 2027 the split counts in 2027 only and the flag is informative in both years; with day 3 recorded the flag is gone in both. Counter-check: the two years' `RENT` sum to the splits' sum (no double counting).
- **The evidence reference:** a `rentDueDays` entry with and without `evidenceReference` moves the year alike; `dueDateEvidence` names it or is `null`; its field errors (`400`: empty after trimming, over 500 characters); the reference's create and amend round-trip it.
- **ACC7:** the new step ("Effect on existing data").
- **§58E's history** (`tax-year-view.test.ts`, `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`):
  - an amendment from `[]` to day 1, recorded 2029-02-01, of a January 2028 rent paid 2027-12-29 is flagged with `yearBefore` 2027 and `yearAfter` 2028 in both views;
  - the same recorded on 2027-12-30 raises nothing (31-December rule);
  - a reference **created** on 2029-02-01 with day 1 flags both years (`RENT_DUE_DAYS_CREATED`; with VC-X-28);
  - day 15 → `[]` raises nothing;
  - the existing day 3 → 15 tests stay unchanged.
- **Rule and pin:**
  - the registry test of the parameter;
  - `frozen-rules.test.ts` with the new pin. Its counter-check on a copy of the cash rule: `recordedSources` with `PERIOD_START` added changes the hash, and `effectiveTo` does not;
  - `GET /tax-rules` lists `dueDate`.
- **Repository** (`tax-year-repository.test.ts:63–80`): the assumed January rent is in 2026's list, not in 2027's, with both flags. After the reference with day 3 it is in 2027's list with `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`.
- **End to end** (`tax-year.e2e.test.ts:222–261`): the example below, steps 1–3, through the routes. Step 2b goes through `POST /tax-classifications` with `taxYear` and is then read back. Realm isolation is unchanged.
- **Existing tests** that assert the move under the assumption (listed above) are rewritten to the new outcome. None is deleted, and none is weakened. The Hausgeld, interest and day-3/15/28 tests stay literally as they are.

### Counter-checks and mutations

**Counter-checks:**
- no year is moved on `PERIOD_START`;
- no proposal is lost: `attribution.proposedYear` and the flag are always present when 1–3 hold;
- no recorded due day is ignored;
- no Hausgeld is moved;
- no interest year changes;
- no non-recurring category is touched;
- no confirmation without `taxYear` closes the proposal;
- no year is `final` while a proposal into it or out of it is open, and no amount counts in two years;
- no ACC7 figure changes.

**Mutations** (each alone, restored byte for byte):
- `moves = true` for `PERIOD_START` again (condition 4 dropped): the domain test, the repository test and the e2e test turn red;
- condition 4 hard-coded (`dueDateSource !== 'PERIOD_START'`) instead of read from `recordedSources`: the parameter counter-check turns red;
- `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` not raised, or `proposedYear` set to the booking year: the domain test turns red;
- `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` put into `CONFIRMABLE` (closed by any confirmed classification): the review test turns red;
- the proposed year's year flag dropped, or the split's amount added to the proposed year's figures: the both-years test turns red;
- `periodGuessed` checked after condition 4, so Hausgeld with `ECONOMIC_PLAN` would move: the Hausgeld test turns red;
- `RENT_OPERATING_COST_ADVANCE` left on the old path: the advance case turns red;
- `attributionChanges` computing "before" with a fixed `PERIOD_START` move: the §58E case turns red;
- the pinned literal not updated, or the parameter left out of the rule: `frozen-rules.test.ts` turns red.

### Example (synthetic)

One flat P, one owner A (`"1/1"`), one Tenant T. Rent 850.00 (`RENT_BASE`) and advance 150.00 (`RENT_OPERATING_COST_ADVANCE`), one Transaction per month, each matched to its term (`CONFIRMED` reconciliation). The rents of January to November 2026 are paid on the 15th. Window 2026-12-22 to 2027-01-10. Read on 2027-02-01.

| Transaction | Booked | Term | Before VC-X-39 (no reference) | §58F (no reference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-Jan…R-Nov | the 15th of each month 2026 | January–November 2026 | 2026, no flag (outside the windows) | the same |
| R1 | 2026-12-29 | January 2027 | **2027**, `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED`, `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` | **2026**, `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED`, `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (`proposedYear` 2027) |
| R2 | 2027-01-04 | December 2026 | 2027, `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` (1 December is outside the window) | the same |
| M | 2026-12-30, `MAINTENANCE` 300.00 | – | 2026, no flag | the same |

**1. Without a reference.**

| 2026 view | Before VC-X-39 | §58F |
|---|---|---|
| `RENT` | 11 × 850.00 = **9,350.00** | 9,350.00 + 850.00 = **10,200.00** |
| `OPERATING_COST_ADVANCES` | 11 × 150.00 = **1,650.00** | **1,800.00** |
| `review.open`, 10-day flags | none | `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` 2, `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` 2 (R1's two splits) |

- **The 2027 view** holds R1 and R2 before VC-X-39 (`RENT` 1,700.00, advances 300.00), and R2 alone under §58F (850.00 and 150.00). 2027 counts `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` 4 and `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` 2 before VC-X-39, and `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` 2 (R2's splits) under §58F. Under §58F 2027 also carries the year flag `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` naming R1's two splits (850.00 and 150.00, not in its figures), so neither 2026 nor 2027 is `final` (decided 2026-11-02).
- **The 10-day items of 2026 under §58F:** R1 counts in 2026, the year it was paid, as the report requires without a proven due date. Before VC-X-39, 2026 showed no open 10-day flag at all.

**2. The person decides.**
- **(a) Records `rentDueDays` `[{ validFrom: 2026-01-01, day: 3 }]`** (created on 2026-12-30, before the year end):
  - R1 is due on 2027-01-03, in the window, so it goes to **2027** with `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (`dueDateSource` `RENTAL_CONTRACT_REFERENCE`).
  - R2 is due on 2026-12-03, outside the window, so it stays in 2027 with no flag.
  - 2026: `RENT` 9,350.00, advances 1,650.00, the same totals as before VC-X-39, now on a recorded date. 2027: `RENT` 1,700.00, advances 300.00.
- **(b) Without a reference, classifies R1's `RENT_BASE` split** as `RENT`/`INCOME` with `taxYear` 2027 (`USER_CONFIRMED`):
  - that split goes to 2027 (`overridden: true`), and its `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` becomes informative;
  - R1's advance split stays in 2026 with the flag open;
  - 2026: `RENT` 9,350.00, advances 1,800.00. 2027: `RENT` 1,700.00, advances 150.00.

**3. Day 28 instead** (`[{ validFrom: 2026-01-01, day: 28 }]`):
- R2 is due on 2026-12-28, in the window, and paid on 2027-01-04. It moves back to **2026** with `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`.
- R1 is due on 2027-01-28, outside the window. It stays in **2026** with no flag.
- 2026: `RENT` 9,350.00 + 850.00 (R1) + 850.00 (R2) = **11,050.00**, advances 1,650.00 + 150.00 + 150.00 = **1,950.00**. 2027: `RENT` 0.00 from these Transactions.
- That is the law's outcome for a lease due on the 28th. The assumption (1st) could never reach it.

**4. §58E, with the amendment recorded after the year end.** The reference was created on 2026-12-30 with `[]` and amended to day 3 on 2027-03-01:
- under §58F, before `[]` gives R1 2026, and after day 3 gives 2027;
- `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED` appears in 2026's view with `items: [{ R1 rent, 2026 → 2027 }, { R1 advance, 2026 → 2027 }]`. 2027's view does not: the amendment was recorded on 2027-03-01, within 2027, so the 31-December rule keeps it out of that year;
- under the old rule both lists gave 2027, so nothing was flagged;
- **created instead of amended** (decided 2026-11-02): with the reference created only on 2027-03-01, directly with day 3, `RENT_DUE_DAYS_CREATED` flags 2026 with the same items, and 2027 again not.

M stays in 2026 in every step.

### Not in VC-X-39 (pointers)

- **Loan interest by periods of use:** VC-X-40 (question 22). The interest's tax year by its schedule's payment date is unchanged here.
- **Hausgeld:** already never moved on a guess (§58A). Maintenance paid from the Hausgeld in the 15 % check is VC-X-27, a separate matter.
- **Acknowledging a change:** VC-X-28 (§58E). This section only says what its Part 1 computes under the amended rule, and that a reference's `CREATED` counts (decided 2026-11-02, open question 7).
- **The due day from MRE:** MRE's lease has no due day (§58A). An import or a link of `rentalContractReferenceId` on splits is a later item.
- **A rent split of several terms** (`SEVERAL_TERMS`) or without a reconciliation (`NO_ECONOMIC_PERIOD`): unchanged, booking year.
- **The AfA, recording and VC-X-45's stages:** not affected (above).
- **Docs to align at implementation:**
  - `invariant-suite.md` (the cash-timing rows, `:815`);
  - `phase-7-plan.md` P7-D3 ("the start of the period serves as the due date");
  - `beratungsfragen.md` §3 ("Was die Software tut");
  - the report's gap row 18 (as a Nachtrag);
  - `ui-guide.md` for the texts.

### Open questions for review

1. **A new flag, or a new meaning for an existing one.** **Proposal:** a new item flag `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (with `proposedYear`) beside `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED`, parallel to `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`. A client then sees "proposed, not applied" by its code, and `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` keeps one meaning for rent and Hausgeld. **Alternative:** no new code. `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED.details` would gain `proposedYear` (`null` where nothing would move), with fewer codes but one code at two levels of urgency. Reusing `ECONOMIC_PERIOD_ASSUMED` is not proposed: the rent's period is known. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02: the proposal.** Without a recorded due date no automatic shift of the year; the proposal is shown separately as `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`.
2. **What closes the proposal.** **Proposal:** only a confirmed classification that sets `taxYear` (either year), or a recorded due day. The owner's words name exactly these two, and a create defaults to `USER_CONFIRMED`, so "any confirmed classification" would close it as a side effect of classifying the treatment. **Alternative:** as `ECONOMIC_PERIOD_ASSUMED`, any confirmed classification closes it (the booking year is then the accepted year). Fewer open items, but a classification made for another reason would decide the year. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02: the proposal.** Only an explicit, confirmed tax-year decision (`taxYear` on a confirmed classification) or a recorded due date closes the proposal; a general confirmation of the classification does not.
3. **What counts as a proven due date.** **Proposal:** a recorded `rentDueDays` entry covering the term. The person states it from the lease, and the reference's `sourceReferences` can name the lease. **Alternative:** the reference must carry at least one `sourceReference` (or a review state) before its due day moves a year, which needs a new field or rule for the reference and leaves existing references without evidence unproven. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02: the proposal, with an evidence reference made possible and recommended.** A recorded `rentDueDays` entry suffices technically as the person's statement; the entry gains the optional `evidenceReference`, which the UI recommends and the attribution names (`dueDateEvidence`). It is not required.
4. **A December rent paid late without a due day.** **Proposal:** no proposal. Its assumed due date (the 1st) lies outside the window, so the rule has nothing to propose. `DUE_DATE_ASSUMED` alone shows that a recorded day 22–31 could move it back. **Alternative:** propose the economic year whenever the term and the payment straddle the year end (`PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` with `dueDate: null`), so both directions are shown alike. This would hold more years open on a guess about the lease. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02: the proposal.** A December rent without a due date is never moved back on an assumed due date.
5. **The rule's shape.** **Proposal:** the parameter `dueDate.recordedSources` in place in `@1`, the hash pinned for the first time, the change note in `source`. The judgement is the rule's (AGENTS.md §16), and the hash changes visibly. **Alternative:** a code change only, with the note in `source`. The hash still changes, but the parameter list shows nothing of the condition, and a test registry cannot restore the old reading. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02: the proposal.** The parameter and the pinned hash are updated explicitly.
6. **Existing data: no backfill.** **Proposal:** none. Assumed rents return to their booking year on read, and confirmed classifications without `taxYear` show the open proposal again. This is acceptable because no productive installation exists (the Phase-7 freeze point is its go-live), and DE writes no classification (ADR-006, P7-D8). **Alternative:** a one-off migration writing `taxYear` = the previously moved year into confirmed classifications without one. DE would then write tax statements on the person's behalf, which the principle forbids. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02: the proposal.** No backfill.
7. **§58E: a reference's `CREATED` record as a change.** **Proposal:** in VC-X-28 (an amendment of §58E's Part 1, not done here), the `CREATED` record counts as a change against the empty list, as kind `RENT_DUE_DAYS_AMENDED` or a new `RENT_DUE_DAYS_CREATED`. From VC-X-39 on, recording a day 1–10 after the year end moves a January rent paid in December out of a closed year, whether by a create or an amend. **Alternative:** leave `CREATED` out as today. The moved item still carries `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` (open until confirmed), but the closed year gets no year flag. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02: the proposal.** `CREATED` counts as a change in §58E, as the kind `RENT_DUE_DAYS_CREATED` (§58E Part 1 and its open question 9); it is implemented with VC-X-28.
8. **ACC7 and ACC8.** **Proposal:** unchanged. Their window rent has a recorded due day, so no figure moves, and `tax-year.e2e.test.ts` carries the example above. **Alternative:** ACC7 gains a step for a January rent paid in December without a reference (on a second Tenant, so the existing totals stay), showing the proposal and its decision in the phase's acceptance test. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02: the alternative for ACC7.** ACC7 gains a case without a due date and its explicit resolution ("Effect on existing data"). ACC8 is not named by the decision and stays unchanged as proposed.
9. **The proposed year's view.** **Proposal:** the proposal is shown on the item in its booking year only. The proposed year neither lists it nor is held open by it, as for Hausgeld's `ECONOMIC_PERIOD_ASSUMED` today. **Alternative:** the proposed year carries a year flag `PROPOSED_ITEMS_ELSEWHERE` naming the splits that may belong to it, so a person reviewing only that year sees them too. This would be a new year flag and a second read range. **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-02, replacing the proposal:** the open attribution is visible in both potentially affected years, without double counting, and neither year is unrestrictedly `final`. The proposed year carries `PROPOSED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` as a year flag (one code at both places, not the alternative's `PROPOSED_ITEMS_ELSEWHERE`), read from the windows the view already reads, so no second read range is added ("The review").

**Still open (owner):** whether ACC8 should gain a step as well (it stays unchanged, as proposed; the decision names ACC7 only). The UI texts above are proposals for `ui-guide.md`, which this section does not change (VC-X-47).

# 58G. Backdated Allocation Sets in the Tax-Year View (VC-X-48, spec)

**Status:** implemented (VC-X-48, migration 0063; "As implemented (VC-X-48)" at the end of this section). **Open questions 1–6 decided by the owner on 2026-11-03** (chat; "Decided by the owner on 2026-11-03 (chat)" under "Open questions (decided)" at the end of this section): each as proposed (the code `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED`; §58E's routes and `tax_year_acknowledgement` row with a second item table and a shape guard; every step that changes P's summed part flagged, `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NONE` not; the optional `kind` with `409 CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS`; VC-X-48 first with its own migration, VC-X-49 after it with its own; VC-X-48's own e2e test, ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged). Backlog VC-X-48, created by the owner's decision on §58E open question 4 („Rückdatierte Allocation-Sets: eigene Backlog-Zeile, nicht in VC-X-28. Sie verschieben den Anteil, nicht das Jahr, und brächten eine zweite Form in den Flag-Eintrag. VC-X-28 bleibt „was das Jahr verschiebt“.“; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-01). **Migration: the next free number at implementation** (0060 is VC-X-28's, 0061 VC-X-41 Part 2's; Kysely's Migrator refuses a migration whose name sorts before one already applied, so the number is fixed only by the merge order). Productive AfA recording stays disabled; nothing here touches it. It amends §58D (open question 3, "How the code's reality shapes", decision 1) and §58E (the acknowledgement's routes, tables and item shape, additively). `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`, its kinds and its item shape are **unchanged**: VC-X-28 stays "what moves the year". Placement, signs, the per-owner arithmetic, the attribution of Loan interest (§58D decisions 1–7), § 82b, VC-8-05's AfA and the rule for `final` are unchanged.

**Why a section of its own, after §58F:** VC-X-48 is a backlog item of its own (the owner's decision above). §58D and §58E keep their statements and point here.

**What it is about.** §41.3 lets a Loan's allocation set be appended with a `validFrom` in the past (it only has to lie after the last `VALID` set's) and lets the last set be voided, which extends the previous one, or leaves the Loan unallocated from the voided set's `validFrom` when there is none. Both corrections re-attribute interest already booked in the period they cover (§58D "How the code's reality shapes", decision 1: the set **as now recorded** on the booking date). They move a split's **property part** between the views of the PropertyReferences of the two sets, never its tax year (§58D decision 4: the year follows §58A, whatever the allocation). Today this happens silently: a year that was `final` and possibly filed shows other Loan interest figures afterwards, with no flag. VC-X-48 makes such a change visible as a flag of its own shape, `partBefore`/`partAfter` with the year unchanged, and lets a person acknowledge it with §58E's mechanism.

DE still writes no cash, no split, no classification and no allocation (ADR-006, P7-D8). The view stays a read that stores nothing. The acknowledgement command writes only its migration's tables and AuditRecords.

### As the code stands (main, after VC-X-28)

- **The sets in the view:** `allocatedLoanInterest` (`infrastructure/postgres/tax-year-reads.ts`) reads the candidate Loans (a `VALID` set names the PropertyReference), their counting `LOAN_INTEREST` splits of `year` and, by `setsOfLoans`, every set of those Loans (`VALID` and `VOID`) with `validUntil` over the `VALID` ones. `loanInterestOf` (`domains/taxation/tax-year-loan-interest.ts`) takes the set covering each booking date (`setOn`) as recorded now and distributes the split by `distribute`. Nothing reads the sets' AuditRecords.
- **The AuditRecords exist:** `loan-allocation-repository.ts` writes `CREATED` (basis, `validFrom`, every entry) and `VOIDED` (the reason) on the entity `LoanAllocationSet`, in the transaction that writes the set.
- **VC-X-28's history** (`attribution-history.ts`, `attribution-reads.ts`) replays `LoanTerms`, `RentPaymentReconciliation` and `RentalContractReference` records only, and its candidates are the splits in the windows at `year`'s edges, since only there can a year move. `ChangeItem` is `{ sourceId, yearBefore, yearAfter }`; migration 0060's `tax_year_acknowledgement_item` has `CHECK (year_before <> year_after)` and `change_kind` / `change_entity_type` CHECKs listing exactly VC-X-28's six kinds and three entity types (`tax_year_acknowledgement_kind_entity` binds them).
- **The flag of the price key** (`LOAN_ALLOCATION_BY_PURCHASE_PRICE_TO_VERIFY`, §58E Part 3) is per set and is not a change flag: a backdated multi-entry `PURCHASE_PRICE` set raises it on its items (open until confirmed), a backdated `MANUAL` set raises nothing.

### Routes

**No new route.** The acknowledgement routes of §58E serve both flags:

```text
POST /api/v1/property-references/{id}/tax-years/{year}/acknowledgements                                (§58E; VC-X-48: the part kinds, the optional `kind`)
GET  /api/v1/property-references/{id}/tax-years/{year}/acknowledgements[?status=]                      (§58E; VC-X-48: `change.items` of the part shape)
POST /api/v1/property-references/{id}/tax-years/{year}/acknowledgements/{acknowledgementId}/withdraw   (§58E, unchanged)
```

`GET /api/v1/property-references/{id}/tax-years/{year}` (§58C) gains the year and item flag `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` (below), additively. Whether a part change takes these routes and the existing table, or its own, is open question 2.

### The model: a part change

**One rule, the year rule's sibling.** A *part change* is one AuditRecord of an input of the attribution to PropertyReferences. For each candidate item, P's **part** of it is computed twice, with the input as it stood just **before** and just **after** that record, everything else as read now (§58E Part 1, "each change is judged alone"). The year `year` of P is flagged when

1. the item's tax year (§58A, derived now; it is the same on both sides) is `year`;
2. P's part differs between the two sides (below: the state or the amount);
3. the record's `occurred_at` lies after 31 December of `year` (Europe/Berlin; §58E's 31-December rule, `recordedAfter`).

**P's part of an item** is one of three states, with an amount:

| State | When (§58D's three cases, seen from P) | `part` |
|---|---|---|
| `ATTRIBUTED` | a usable set covers the booking date and has an entry for P (**since VC-X-40, §58L:** usable sets cover every day of the split's interest period and P has a weight) | P's part by `distribute` (non-negative Money, as `loanAllocation.propertyPart`; since VC-X-40 one `distribute` over the period's weights, the view's own function) |
| `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` | no usable set covers the booking date, and P is among the `VALID` sets' PropertyReferences of that side (`candidates`) | `null` (listed in `notAttributed`, never summed) |
| `NONE` | a usable set covers the booking date without an entry for P, or no `VALID` set of that side names P | `null` (nothing in P's view) |

- **"Differs"** means: the states differ, or both are `ATTRIBUTED` and the amounts differ. **Proposal:** a step between `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` and `NONE` is not a part change (no figure of P moves; the not attributed side held the year open with `LOAN_INTEREST_NOT_ATTRIBUTED` anyway), and a step between `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` and `ATTRIBUTED` is one (open question 3).
- **A set with the same share for P** can still change P's part by a cent (`distribute`'s remainder goes over the whole set). That is a part change: the figure moved.
- **The owners' parts** follow P's part (§58D step 4); they are not compared separately. The flag is the property's, shown unfiltered at the owner level, as `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED` is (§58E open question 3, decided).

**The kinds** (open question 1 for the code's name):

| `kind` | AuditRecords read | Candidate items | The input before / after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_ADDED` | `LoanAllocationSet` `CREATED` | the counting `LOAN_INTEREST` splits with a `loanId` of a Loan **any** of whose sets (`VALID` or `VOID`) names P, whose tax year is `year` (the whole year and the windows, as §58D's selection; not only the windows, since a part can move anywhere in the year) | the Loan's `VALID` sets, with `validUntil` derived over them (§41.3), replayed from the sets' records in `(occurred_at, id)` order |
| `LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_VOIDED` | `LoanAllocationSet` `VOIDED` | as above | as above |
| `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED` (§58P, VC-X-54) | `LoanTerms` `CREATED` | as above | the Loan's `VALID` terms just before and after the record (the closing as now), each side's contract plan giving the split's interest period (§58L rule 1, §58O); the sets as now; only splits whose year is `year` on both sides |
| `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED` (§58P) | `LoanTerms` `VOIDED` | as above | as above |
| `LOAN_CLOSED_PART` (§58P) | `Loan` `CLOSED` | as above | the terms as now, the Loan without and with the closing (§41.7) |

- **Why `VOID` sets count for the candidates:** after a void, P may no longer be named by any `VALID` set, so §58D's selection would not read the Loan, while the void is exactly what took the interest out of P's view.
- **The history** is §58E's: a set's records replayed from "not there" (`CREATED` on, `VOIDED` off); a history that does not end in the set's current status makes the set `ATTRIBUTION_HISTORY_INCONSISTENT` with `{ entityType: "LoanAllocationSet", entityId }`, its records unused and its current status held (open, as today). The sets of one Loan are walked together (as the terms of one Loan are), so "before" and "after" are the Loan's `VALID` sets just around the record.
- **What the record time is:** the AuditRecord's `occurred_at`, as for every §58E kind, so the change has an `auditRecordId` to acknowledge (§58D open question 3 had named the set's `created_at` and `voided_at`; they are written in the same transaction and agree with it).
- **Not a part change:** a set appended with a `validFrom` after every booked split (it covers no booked interest; **since VC-X-40, §58L:** after the end of every booked split's interest period); a recorded `interestPeriod` (§58L open question 4, a person's statement on the split, like a `taxYear` override); a set appended or voided before 31 December of the item's year (the 31-December rule); a `taxYear` override (it moves the year, not the part, and no set changes it); a Loan voided (§41.1: only without splits). A Loan's closing changes no set (§41.7: the last set stays open-ended) and is §58H's.
- **Confirmation and acknowledgement are independent.** A backdated multi-entry `PURCHASE_PRICE` set carries `LOAN_ALLOCATION_BY_PURCHASE_PRICE_TO_VERIFY` on its items (§58E Part 3) **and** raises a part change. Confirming the set clears only the price flag; acknowledging the part change clears only the part flag (§58E, decided 2026-11-02: a statement clears exactly its own flag).

### The flag `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED`

A **new code**, not a new form of `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED` (the owner's decision: a second form in the flag's entry is what VC-X-28 does not take). Year flag, plus an item flag of the same code on an item now in P's view of `year` (attributed, or listed in `notAttributed`) that a change moved. Its `details` mirror `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`'s array, one entry per change, ordered by `amendedAt`, then `auditRecordId`:

```text
{
  kind, entityType, entityId, auditRecordId, amendedAt,
  loanId, allocationSetId, validFrom,                     // the kind's own keys (the set's)
  items: [{ sourceType: "TRANSACTION_SPLIT", sourceId, taxYear,
            stateBefore, partBefore, stateAfter, partAfter }],
  changeFingerprint,
  acknowledgement: { acknowledgementId, acknowledgedAt, acknowledgedBy } | null
}
```

- **`items` are sorted by `sourceType`, then `sourceId`.** `taxYear` is the item's (always `year`; it is there so the entry reads alone). `partBefore`/`partAfter` are Money or `null` as the table above.
- **The level by state** (§58E open question 6, decided: the code kept, the level by state): **open** while at least one entry has `acknowledgement: null`; **informative** once every entry is acknowledged. The item flag the same way over the changes that moved the item. Clients filter by level, not by code.
- **The figures do not depend on it:** the view's parts are those of the sets as now recorded (§58D decision 1, unchanged). The flag only says that they differ from what they were before a record made after the year's end.
- **`ATTRIBUTION_HISTORY_INCONSISTENT`** stays the one inconsistency flag; it gains the entity type `LoanAllocationSet`. It cannot be acknowledged (§58E).
- **The review table of §58C** gains `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` with the rule "open while an entry is not acknowledged; then informative".

### The fingerprint

As §58E Part 2: SHA-256 (hex) of the canonical JSON (`shared/canonical-json.ts`) of `{ propertyReferenceId, year, auditRecordId, kind, items }`, `items` sorted as above. **It covers the parts as well as the ids**, unlike `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`'s (ids and years): the part is what moved, so what is acknowledged is exactly what the person saw. For one split and one set history the parts cannot change without a new id or a new record, so in practice the fingerprint changes when an item joins or leaves the year (a `taxYear` override set or removed, a split corrected into a new one), and the change is then open again. Money as `centsText` (exact cents, no float).

### Acknowledging a part change (§58E Part 2, reused)

`POST …/tax-years/{year}/acknowledgements` with §58E's body, gaining **`kind`** (optional; one of the kinds of §58E Part 1, of this section and of §58H; open question 4):

```json
{
  "auditRecordId": "6f1c2a9e-0000-4000-8000-000000000481",
  "kind": "LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_ADDED",
  "expectedFingerprint": "3c0e9a7b5d1f2e4c6a8b0d9f7e5c3a1b2d4f6e8a0c9b7d5f3e1a2c4b6d8f0e9a",
  "reason": "Erklärung 2027 noch nicht abgegeben; Aufteilung ab Juli 50/50 nachgetragen (synthetisch)"
}
```

**Order of checks** (§58E's, with step 3 widened; nothing else changes):

1. `400`, all field errors at once (`kind` an unknown value: `INVALID_FORMAT`);
2. the PropertyReference unknown or of another Realm → `404`;
3. **the year's changes of both flags, derived in the command's own snapshot** (§58E Part 1 and this section, for this PropertyReference and `year`), taken with `auditRecordId` and, when given, `kind`:
   - none → `409 CONFLICT` with `reason = "CHANGE_NOT_FLAGGED"` (`details: { auditRecordId, year }`, plus `kind` when given);
   - more than one and no `kind` → `409 CONFLICT` with `reason = "CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS"` and `details: { auditRecordId, year, kinds }` (one AuditRecord can be two changes: §58H's reconciliation moving a rent's year and a deposit's PropertyReference);
4. the change's fingerprint ≠ `expectedFingerprint` → `412 ATTRIBUTION_CHANGE_DIFFERS` (§58E; the message "moves other items than when it was read" fits a part change too);
5. the no-op: an `ACTIVE` acknowledgement with the same PropertyReference, year, `auditRecordId` and fingerprint → `200` with it;
6. `201`: the acknowledgement with its items in the part shape, AuditRecord `ACKNOWLEDGED` (`items` in the part shape).

- **Idempotency, `If-Match`, one change per request, withdraw** (with a reason, audited; §58E open question 2, decided): unchanged. A withdrawn acknowledgement re-opens the part change.
- **The response** (`GET` and the commands): `change.items` is `[{ sourceType, sourceId, taxYear, stateBefore, partBefore, stateAfter, partAfter }]` for a part kind and `[{ sourceId, yearBefore, yearAfter }]` for a year kind; `change.kind` tells which. A client that read only the year shape must accept the part shape.
- **Locks and concurrency:** §58E's (one `REPEATABLE READ` read-write transaction; the PropertyReference row written first; no input locked). A set appended or voided after the snapshot is a new `auditRecordId` (not acknowledged) or changes the fingerprint: the next read shows it open.

### In the database (migration: the next free number at implementation)

**Proposal** (open question 2): the acknowledgement stays one row of `tax_year_acknowledgement` (its subject, key and re-opening rule are a year change's: PropertyReference, year, AuditRecord, fingerprint; §58E open question 1's reason for two tables does not divide them), and the part items get a table of their own, since `tax_year_acknowledgement_item` holds years and refuses equal ones.

- **`tax_year_acknowledgement`:** `change_kind`'s CHECK gains `LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_ADDED`, `LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_VOIDED`; `change_entity_type`'s gains `LoanAllocationSet`; `tax_year_acknowledgement_kind_entity` gains `(change_entity_type = 'LoanAllocationSet') = (change_kind IN ('LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_ADDED', 'LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_VOIDED'))`. The `ACTIVE` unique index, the frozen guard (`tax_statement_frozen`), the insert guard and `down`'s refusal are unchanged.
- **`tax_year_acknowledgement_part_item`** (new): `acknowledgement_id`, `mre_realm_id` (composite foreign key to the acknowledgement), `source_type` (CHECK `TRANSACTION_SPLIT`; §58H adds `DEPOSIT_CLOSING`), `source_id` (`uuid`, as a value), `tax_year` (CHECK 2000–2100), `state_before`, `state_after` (CHECK `ATTRIBUTED`, `NOT_ATTRIBUTED`, `NONE`), `part_before`, `part_after` (`numeric`, scale ≤ 2, ≥ 0); key `(acknowledgement_id, source_type, source_id)`. CHECKs: a part is set exactly on `ATTRIBUTED` (`(state_x = 'ATTRIBUTED') = (part_x IS NOT NULL)`, both sides); **the part moved**: `(state_before, part_before) IS DISTINCT FROM (state_after, part_after)`; the step `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NONE` refused (open question 3's proposal; dropped if decided otherwise).
- **Guards** (triggers, as 0060's):
  - `tax_year_acknowledgement_part_item_append_only`: inserted only in its acknowledgement's transaction (`created_txid`), never updated or deleted (as `tax_year_acknowledgement_item_append_only`);
  - **the shape matches the kind** (both item tables, one function): a part item only under a part kind, a year item only under a year kind (`change_kind` read from the acknowledgement); refused otherwise.
- **`down`:** drops the new table and restores the CHECKs; with an acknowledgement of a new kind or a part item present it **refuses** (a person's statement is never dropped silently, as 0060).
- **Not in the database:** whether a change is flagged, its parts and its fingerprint (derived over Financing and Taxation, checked by the command and re-checked by every read).
- **No column** on `loan_allocation_set`, `loan_allocation`, `loan` or any ledger table.
- **Since VC-X-54 (§58P, migration 0071):** `change_kind` gains `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`, `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED`, `LOAN_CLOSED_PART`; the `Loan` clause of `tax_year_acknowledgement_kind_entity` binds `Loan` to `LOAN_CLOSED` and `LOAN_CLOSED_PART`, the terms kinds are bound to `LoanTerms` by elimination; the shape guard admits `TRANSACTION_SPLIT` part items under the three kinds.

### AuditRecords

`TaxYearAcknowledgement` `ACKNOWLEDGED` as §58E, with `items` in the part shape for a part kind; `WITHDRAWN` unchanged. No AuditRecord on the set, the Loan or the PropertyReference. These records are not inputs of any kind.

### Error answers (`api/error-answers.ts`)

| Error | Answer | `details` |
|---|---|---|
| `AttributionChangeAmbiguousError` (new) | `409 CONFLICT`, "The record is more than one change of this year; name its kind." | `{ reason: "CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS", auditRecordId, year, kinds }` |

Reused: `AttributionChangeNotFlaggedError` (`details` gain `kind` when given), `AttributionChangeDiffersError`, `TaxYearAcknowledgementNotFoundError`, `PropertyReferenceNotFoundError`, `IdempotencyKeyConflictError`, `ConcurrentUpdateError`.

### Example (synthetic)

§58D's setup: P1 < P2; P1 owned by A and B `"1/2"` each, P2 by C; Loan L, `debtFrom` 2027-01-01, monthly payments due on the last day of each month. One set at first: **S1** `MANUAL` from 2027-02-01 (P1 `"3/5"`, P2 `"2/5"`), recorded on 2027-02-01. Confirmed interest debits with L's `loanId`:

| Debit | Booking date | Interest | Tax year (§58A) |
|---|---|---|---|
| d1 | 2027-03-31 | 450.01 | 2027 |
| d2 | 2027-07-30 | 449.99 | 2027 |
| d3 | 2028-01-03 | 448.00 | 2027 (10-day rule: due 2027-12-31) |
| d4 | 2028-06-30 | 446.00 | 2028 |

**Step 1, a backdated set.** On **2028-03-01** **S2** `MANUAL` from 2027-07-01 (P1 `"1/2"`, P2 `"1/2"`) is appended (allowed: after S1's `validFrom`). It covers d2, d3 and d4.

| Debit | Under S1 (before): P1 / P2 | Under S2 (after): P1 / P2 |
|---|---|---|
| d1 | 270.01 / 180.00 | unchanged (S1) |
| d2 | 269.99 / 180.00 (44,999 × 3/5 = 26,999.4, × 2/5 = 17,999.6: the cent to P2) | 225.00 / 224.99 (the tie by `propertyReferenceId`) |
| d3 | 268.80 / 179.20 | 224.00 / 224.00 |
| d4 | 267.60 / 178.40 | 223.00 / 223.00 |

- **2027** (recorded after 31 December 2027): P1's `LOAN_INTEREST` line moves from 808.80 to **719.01**, P2's from 539.20 to **628.99** (both sum to 1,348.00, the three debits). Both views carry `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED`, open, with one entry `LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_ADDED` (S2): P1's items d2 `ATTRIBUTED` 269.99 → `ATTRIBUTED` 225.00 and d3 268.80 → 224.00; P2's d2 180.00 → 224.99 and d3 179.20 → 224.00. d1 is in neither entry. Each of d2 and d3 carries the item flag. 2027 is not `final` in either view.
- **2028:** the record is not after 31 December 2028: no flag for d4 in 2028.
- **No year moved:** d3 stays in 2027 under both sides; `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED` is not raised by S2.
- **Acknowledged in P1's 2027** (`kind` `LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_ADDED`, the entry's fingerprint): P1's flag informative; P2's 2027 still open (one acknowledgement per PropertyReference, year and change; §58E open question 3, decided).

**Step 2, the set voided.** On **2029-02-01** S2 is voided; S1 covers everything again. A new change `LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_VOIDED`, recorded after both years' ends:

- **2027:** both views gain a second entry (P1: d2 225.00 → 269.99, d3 224.00 → 268.80; P2 the reverse), open. The `ADDED` entry stays (each change judged alone, §58E) and keeps P1's acknowledgement, since its fingerprint is unchanged. P1's line is 808.80 again.
- **2028:** d4 223.00 → 267.60 (P1) and 223.00 → 178.40 (P2): both 2028 views flagged, open.
- **Over-flagging only keeps a year open until acknowledged; it never hides a move** (§58E).

**Variant, a first set backdated.** Were S1 itself appended only on 2028-03-01, d1–d3 would go from `NONE` (before S1 no `VALID` set names P1 or P2, so neither view reads L and nothing is listed; the state table above) to `ATTRIBUTED`: under open question 3 (decided as proposed) both 2027 views carry a part change for them, since a step to `ATTRIBUTED` changes P's summed part. (Corrected with VC-X-49 on the owner's answer to the VC-X-48 PR, 2026-11-03: the text read `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` → `ATTRIBUTED`, which neither the state table nor the code gives; "As implemented (VC-X-48)" 6.)

### The effect on `final`, ACC7 and ACC8

- **The rule stays §58C's** (`final` only when `review.open` is empty). A year with a part change after its end is not final until each change is acknowledged with its current fingerprint; it stops being final when a change is new, moves another part, or its acknowledgement is withdrawn. This can turn a `final: true` of today into `false` after deployment: the intended correction.
- **What an acknowledgement does not replace** (§58E, decided 2026-11-02): it clears only its own flag; it confirms no set (the price flag stays open until its own confirmation), supplies no allocation (`LOAN_INTEREST_NOT_ATTRIBUTED` stays), changes no figure and no stage of §60A, and is no evidence for a VERIFY point (checklist A1).
- **§59E:** a part change of an attributed `CAPITALIZED` interest item makes its component's basis differ from P's part; `LOAN_INTEREST_CAPITALIZED_NOT_IN_BASIS` then shows `BASIS_MISMATCH` (§59E, unchanged). Acknowledging the part change does not drop it.
- **ACC7 and ACC8 expect no change:** their Loans' sets are `MANUAL` `1/1` and recorded before the end of the years they cover (as the tests' clock runs), so no set record lies after 31 December of a year whose part it moves. Both run unchanged; **a flag appearing there is a finding to report and explain, not to suppress.** No acceptance step is added (open question 6).

### Performance

- **Candidates:** the view already reads the candidate Loans' interest splits of `year` and all their sets (`setsOfLoans`); the selection of Loans widens from "a `VALID` set names P" to "any set names P" (`loan_allocation_property_reference_idx`, 0026). One AuditRecord query for the sets' records by `audit_record_entity_idx` (`entity_type = 'LoanAllocationSet'`, `entity_id IN …`), after the sets are selected in the Realm.
- **The derivation:** per record, `distribute` over two sets for the Loan's splits of `year` (about 12 a year per Loan, at most 50 entries per set). A handful of records per Loan.
- **The command** derives both flags' changes for the PropertyReference and year, not the view. A repository test reads the plan of the set-record query inside the view's snapshot.

### The code that changes (pointers)

- **`domains/taxation/`:** a pure `partChanges` (new file, e.g. `attribution-parts.ts`) replays the sets' records per Loan with `walk`/`replay` of `attribution-history.ts`, computes P's part per side with `loanInterestOf`'s case logic (`setOn`, `sumsToOne`, `distribute`), and returns entries with the part items and `changeFingerprint`; `attribution-rule.ts` gains the part kinds (or a sibling `PART_CHANGE_KINDS`, keeping `CHANGE_KINDS` the year kinds) and the entity type `LoanAllocationSet`; `tax-statements.ts` matches acknowledgements to both flags; `tax-year-review.ts`'s `flagIsOpen` decides `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` by its `details`, as `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`.
- **`infrastructure/postgres/`:** `attribution-reads.ts` reads the sets' records and the widened Loan selection in the view's snapshot; `tax-statement-repository.ts` writes and reads the part items; migration `<n>_tax_year_part_acknowledgements`.
- **`application/tax-statements.ts`, `api/tax-statements.ts`:** the optional `kind`, `CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS`, the part shape in the DTO. `docs/development/api-inventory.md` is unchanged (no route changes); `yarn api:inventory:check` stays green.
- **`architecture.test.ts`:** no new edge (Taxation → Financing exists; Financing never reads Taxation).

### Tests the implementation needs

- **Domain (pure):** the example literally (both steps, both views, both years, the 31-December rule for d4); each state step (`ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `ATTRIBUTED` with another amount, `ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NONE`, `ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NOT_ATTRIBUTED`, `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NONE` not flagged under the proposal); the same share for P with a one-cent move (flagged) and an identical part (not flagged); a set appended after every booked split (nothing); recorded on 31 December (nothing) and on 1 January (flagged); a 10-day-rule item whose booking date lies in the next year (the set by the booking date, the flag in the tax year); a `taxYear` override on a moved split (flagged in the overridden year); a Loan whose only set naming P was voided (still a candidate); an inconsistent set history (`ATTRIBUTION_HISTORY_INCONSISTENT` with `LoanAllocationSet`, history unused); the fingerprint stable over key and item order, different for another part, another state, another year, another `auditRecordId`; the levels (open with one unacknowledged entry, informative with all, open again after a withdraw or another fingerprint); the price flag and the part flag independent (each statement clears only its own); `final` true exactly when nothing else is open; owners' parts unchanged in their derivation (owners plus `NOT_OWNED` equal P's part, both sides).
- **Repository (PostgreSQL):** the order of checks with the new steps (`CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS`, `kind` narrowing, `CHANGE_NOT_FLAGGED` for a set record of a year it does not touch); idempotency; withdraw; one snapshot (a set appended between two statements of the view is not seen); **schema past the repository**, each with a counter-check: a part item with `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` and a part, `ATTRIBUTED` without one, an unmoved item, a `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NONE` item, a part item under a year kind and a year item under a part kind, a part item inserted after its acknowledgement's transaction, an update and a delete, a negative part, a part kind with another entity type; Realm isolation (another Realm's set records never read, its acknowledgements never seen, its Loan's ids `CHANGE_NOT_FLAGGED`); "no cash mutated" extended by the new table (rows and versions unchanged by views); the plans; the migration's `up`, `down`, and `down` refusing with a part item or a new kind present.
- **API:** every `400` (`kind`), the part DTO, `CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS`'s mapping.
- **End to end** (`tax-year-part-changes.e2e.test.ts`, synthetic values only, a settable clock): the example through the HTTP API (L, S1, the four debits, S2 appended on 2028-03-01, both views of 2027 and 2028 at both levels, the acknowledgement in P1, P2 still open, S2 voided on 2029-02-01, the second entries, 2028 flagged); **Realm isolation** and **no cash mutated** around it. ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged.

### Counter-checks and mutations

**Counter-checks:** no part moved after a year's end without the flag, in every view whose part moved; no year flag of `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED` raised by a set; no figure changed by an acknowledgement; no confirmation of a set by an acknowledgement, nor the reverse; nothing written by a view.

**Mutations** that must turn the tests red (each applied alone, restored byte for byte):

- the 31-December rule dropped, or applied to the booking date or to the set's `validFrom` instead of the record's `occurred_at`;
- the part compared as P's share instead of P's part (the one-cent case missed);
- the candidates restricted to Loans with a `VALID` set naming P (the void out of P's view missed);
- the candidates restricted to the windows (d2 missed);
- the sets taken as now for both sides (no change found);
- `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NONE` flagged, or `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` → `ATTRIBUTED` not flagged (under the decided variant of open question 3);
- an acknowledgement matched without the amounts in the fingerprint, or by `auditRecordId` alone across kinds (the `CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` case);
- `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` no longer raised once acknowledged (instead of informative), or still open when every entry is acknowledged;
- a part kind accepted into `tax_year_acknowledgement_item` (the shape guard dropped), each with its schema test;
- the Realm filter dropped from the set-record read.

### Invariant suite (with the implementation)

§44's table gains **no silent move of a part** (every set appended or voided after a year's end that moves P's part of an item of that year flags P's view of it, at both levels, until acknowledged; the parts always those of the sets as now recorded); the row "an acknowledgement covers what was seen" covers the part shape; the migration's guards.

### Open questions (decided)

1. **The flag's code.** **Decided (as proposed):** `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED`, one code for every input that moves a part between views without moving the year (here the sets; §58H proposes the deposit's PropertyReference under it). **Alternative (not taken):** `LOAN_ALLOCATION_CHANGED`, a Loan-only code, so each source has its own code (§58H's deposit would then need a third code).
2. **Where the acknowledgement lives.** **Decided (as proposed):** the same routes and the same `tax_year_acknowledgement` row, with a second item table for the part shape and a guard that the item shape matches the kind: the subject (PropertyReference, year, AuditRecord), the key, the fingerprint and the re-opening rule are a year change's, which is what §58E open question 1 (decided: two tables) divided by. **Alternative (not taken):** a table and routes of their own (`…/tax-years/{year}/part-acknowledgements`): no `kind` in the body and no shape guard, but a second set of routes, use cases and withdrawals doing the same thing.
3. **Steps from and to "not attributed".** **Decided (as proposed):** flag every step that changes P's part as summed in P's view, so `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` → `ATTRIBUTED` (a first set backdated) and `ATTRIBUTED` → `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` (the only set voided) are flagged, and `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NONE` is not (no figure of P moves). This follows §58E open question 5 (decided: flagged although the "before" state held the year open, since DE does not know whether the return was filed). **Alternative (not taken):** do not flag a step whose "before" side was `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` (that year could not have been `final` through this item); less noise, but it rests on the year's state as derived now.
4. **Two changes of one AuditRecord.** **Decided (as proposed):** the body gains an optional `kind`; without it, a record that is more than one change of the year answers `409 CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` naming the kinds, so the client sends the one it showed. **Alternative (not taken):** no `kind`: the command takes the change whose fingerprint equals `expectedFingerprint` among those of the record (the fingerprints differ, since `kind` is in them); a mismatch then answers `412` with every current fingerprint. Simpler for the client, but the `412` loses its one `currentFingerprint`. (Within this section a set record is only ever one change; the case arises with §58H's deposit kinds.)
5. **One implementation with VC-X-49, or two.** **Decided (as proposed):** VC-X-48 first, with its own migration (the part flag, the part item table, the `kind`), then VC-X-49 widening the kinds with its own migration. **Alternative (not taken):** one implementation and one migration for both.
6. **The acceptance tests.** **Decided (as proposed):** as the owner decided for VC-X-28 and VC-X-49 (§58E open question 8): VC-X-48's own e2e test, ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged, so the phase exit stays stable. **Alternative (not taken):** a step in ACC8 showing a backdated set holding a year open.

**Decided by the owner on 2026-11-03 (chat)** (verbatim; cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-03“; mapped to open questions 1–6 above; the owner's preamble for §58G and §58H: „Alle zehn: wie vorgeschlagen.“):
1. „wie vorgeschlagen. `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` als ein Code für alles, was den Anteil statt des Jahres verschiebt; die Quelle steht im `kind`.“ (the proposal)
2. „wie vorgeschlagen. Dieselben Routen und dieselbe Quittierungszeile mit zweiter Item-Tabelle und Form-Wächter. §58E Frage 1 hat nach Subjekt getrennt, und das Subjekt ist hier dasselbe.“ (the proposal)
3. „wie vorgeschlagen. Jeder Schritt, der den summierten Anteil von P ändert, wird geflaggt; `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NONE` nicht. Konsistent mit §58E Frage 5.“ (the proposal)
4. „wie vorgeschlagen. Optionales `kind`, bei Mehrdeutigkeit `409 CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS`. Das `412` behält seinen einen `currentFingerprint`.“ (the proposal)
5. „wie vorgeschlagen. VC-X-48 zuerst mit eigener Migration, VC-X-49 danach mit eigener.“ (the proposal)
6. „wie vorgeschlagen. Eigener E2E-Test, ACC7 und ACC8 unverändert.“ (the proposal)

**Still open (owner):** none. Open questions 1–6 are decided (2026-11-03, above), each as proposed, so the body's proposals are the decisions and the alternatives are not taken. VC-X-48 is implemented first, with its own migration; VC-X-49 follows with its own (§58H open question 4).

### As implemented (VC-X-48)

Implemented as specified, with the owner's decisions of 2026-11-03 (questions 1–6, each as proposed; „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-03“). Productive AfA recording stays disabled; nothing here touches it. `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`, its kinds and its year items are unchanged.

1. **Migration 0063** (`0063_tax_year_part_acknowledgements`, the next free number on main after 0062): `tax_year_acknowledgement`'s CHECKs `change_kind`, `change_entity_type` and `_kind_entity` widened by `LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_ADDED`, `LOAN_ALLOCATION_SET_VOIDED` and `LoanAllocationSet` (dropped and re-added under their names); the table `tax_year_acknowledgement_part_item` as "In the database" (key `(acknowledgement_id, source_type, source_id)`, `_part_on_attributed`, `_moved`, `_not_unattributed_step`, the parts `numeric` ≥ 0 with scale ≤ 2); the guards `tax_year_acknowledgement_part_item_append_only` (its own function, as 0060's for the year items) and `tax_year_acknowledgement_item_shape` (one function, a trigger on each item table). `down` refuses while a part item or an acknowledgement of a part kind exists, else drops the table and both functions and restores 0060's CHECKs. 0060's `down` test rolls 0063 back first (its table references 0060's).
2. **The currency of a part item** is not stored: the view's figures are EUR only (`buildTaxYearView`, data-model.md §17.4), so a part is read back as EUR. A second currency would need a column. **Confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-03** (answer to the VC-X-48 PR; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-03): EUR without a column suffices while the view knows only EUR; the same holds for §58H's deposit items.
3. **Domain** (`domains/taxation/attribution-parts.ts`): `partChanges` replays each Loan's sets with `replay`/`walk` of `attribution-history.ts` (now exported), `partOn` computes P's state and part per side (`withValidUntil` over that side's `VALID` sets, `setOn`, `sumsToOne`, `distribute` over the whole set, as `loanInterestOf`), `partMoved` is question 3's rule, `partChangeFingerprint` covers the parts (Money as exact cents by `canonicalJson`); `tax-year-view.ts` raises the year flag and the item flag (on attributed items and on items in `notAttributed`), `tax-year-review.ts` gives `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` the level by state of `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`; an inconsistent set history is `ATTRIBUTION_HISTORY_INCONSISTENT` with `LoanAllocationSet`. `planAcknowledgement` takes both flags' changes, narrows by the optional `kind` and answers `AMBIGUOUS` for a record that is more than one change without `kind`.
4. **Reads** (`infrastructure/postgres/part-reads.ts`, `tax-year-reads.ts`): `allocatedLoanInterest` reads, with `anySet`, the Loans any of whose sets (`VALID` or `VOID`) names P, once per view; §58D's figures take the Loans with a `VALID` set naming P out of that read (`ofValidSets`), so the figures are unchanged. The sets' `CREATED`/`VOIDED` records by `audit_record_entity_idx` after the sets were selected in the Realm. The command (`tax-statement-repository.ts`) reads both flags' inputs in its own snapshot and writes a part kind's items into the part table, a year kind's into 0060's; the `ACKNOWLEDGED` AuditRecord carries the items in the part shape (parts as `{ amount, currency }`).
5. **API:** `kind` optional in the body (any kind of both flags, else `400 INVALID_FORMAT`), part of the idempotency payload; `CHANGE_NOT_FLAGGED` names `kind` when given; `409 CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` with `{ reason, auditRecordId, year, kinds }`; the DTO's `change.items` in the part shape for a part kind. No route changed; `docs/development/api-inventory.md` unchanged.
6. **What a set record can reach** (found at implementation): §41.3 appends a set only after the last `VALID` one and voids only the last, so one set record never changes whether a booking date lies before the first `VALID` set. `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` → `ATTRIBUTED` and `ATTRIBUTED` → `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` therefore arise only in record orders §41.3 does not write (or with a set held at its status by an inconsistent history); the rule flags them (question 3), tested on synthetic histories. The example's variant "a first set backdated" is `NONE` → `ATTRIBUTED` by the table (before it no `VALID` set names P, and the view does not read the Loan), flagged all the same. **`CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` cannot arise from VC-X-48's data** (a set record is only ever a part change): it is tested on the pure plan, the use case with a stubbed snapshot and the API mapping; §58H's reconciliation will be the first real case.
7. **ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged** (question 6): both run unchanged and green; no `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` appears there. The example runs end to end in `tax-year-part-changes.e2e.test.ts`.
8. **Tests:** `attribution-parts.test.ts` and `attribution-parts-view.test.ts` (pure: the example with its numbers, each state step, the one-cent move, the 31-December rule, the 10-day item, a `taxYear` override, a Loan whose only set naming P was voided, an inconsistent history, the fingerprint, the order of checks with `kind`, the levels, `final`, the owners, the price flag independent), `tax-statement-kinds.test.ts` (the use case with both flags), `tax-statement-part-repository.test.ts` (the order of checks, idempotency with `kind`, withdrawal, step 2, one snapshot, Realm isolation past the composite keys, "no cash mutated", the plans), `tax-statement-part-schema.test.ts` (0063's CHECKs and guards with counter-checks, `up`/`down`), `api/tax-statements.test.ts` (the `kind` `400`s, the part DTO, `CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS`), `tax-year-part-changes.e2e.test.ts`. The mutations of "Counter-checks and mutations" each turn them red (the PR's table).
9. **Release note:** like VC-X-28's kinds, `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` can reopen tax years previously shown as `final` on existing data, where a set was appended or voided after the year's end and moved a part of its interest; acknowledging each change in each view clears it.
