# 58K. The Anschaffungsnahe Check Without `economicTransferDate` (VC-X-34, implemented: migration 0066)

**Status:** implemented (VC-X-34, migration 0066; below, "As implemented (VC-X-34)"). Open questions 1–6 decided by the owner on 2026-11-04 (below, "Open questions (decided)"; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04): 1–3, 5 and 6 as proposed, 4 both (the proposal's backlog row, now VC-X-52, and the alternative's refusal on `confirm`). VC-X-52 (recording the date later, requirement 0 in the database) is **implemented in §58N** (migration 0067; open questions 1–8 decided by the owner on 2026-11-04). Backlog VC-X-34 (follow-up of VC-X-33, review of #193; §59A "As implemented (VC-X-33)" 7: "the anschaffungsnahe check (§58B) still reads §27.1's `transferDate` … without a flag of its own; aligning it would be a separate item"). **Answered by the tax review of 2026-11-01** (`docs/germany/pruefbericht-2026-11-01.md`, questions 3 and 14; mündlich bestätigt durch den Steuerberater, laut Projektinhaber am 2026-11-01): the three-year window starts on the day of the transfer of economic ownership, and without that date the record is incomplete. So the check must not rest on the contract date; the report lists VC-X-34 **before enablement**. **Migration 0066** (the owner's order of 2026-11-04: „Reihenfolge: §58K zuerst, damit bekommt VC-X-34 die 0066; dann §58M, dann §58L.“), needed only for the guard of open question 3. Productive AfA recording stays disabled; nothing here touches it.

**What it amends:** §58B "The anschaffungsnahe check" (the window: "from the Acquisition's `transferDate` (§27.1: `economicTransferDate`, else `contractDate`)"), §58B's capitalisation on the check (`anschaffungsnaheAcquisitionId`, `422 ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_NOT_APPLICABLE`), §59F (the window's start, which §59F measures from "whatever start the check has", §59F "Not changed"), §58C's `acquisitions` and `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_NOT_FINAL`, and §59A "As implemented (VC-X-33)" 7 (the sentence above is closed by this section).

**Unchanged guarantees:** §27.1's `transferDate` (`economicTransferDate`, else `contractDate`, P2-D6) stays the day the buyers' Ownerships begin (§28.1's confirm, migration 0022's check 2, 0050), the default `effectiveDate` of a land/building allocation (`land-building-allocation-repository.ts:97`) and the listing of a purchase in a year (`tax-year-depreciation.ts:250-252`); none of these is the check's window. A check with `economicTransferDate` set is unchanged in every field, figure, flag and suggestion. `DE_ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE@1`'s parameters and pinned hash are unchanged (the window's start is code, not a parameter; open question 6). §59A's `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING` on the AfA (VC-X-33) is unchanged. The check stores nothing and changes no classification (§58B). Realm isolation and the order of checks of `GET /acquisitions/{id}/anschaffungsnahe-herstellungskosten` (`400` → `404` → `409 ACQUISITION_CANCELLED` → `200`) are unchanged.

**Why a section of its own, after §58J:** VC-X-34 is a backlog item of its own. §58B, §59A and §59F were corrected by the implementation (below, "The text that changes"); §28.1 gained requirement 0 (open question 4).

### As the code stands (main 1c03873, after VC-X-51, #262; paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`)

- **The check's date:** `acquisitionsOf` reads the Acquisition with `to_char(coalesce(economic_transfer_date, contract_date), 'YYYY-MM-DD')` as `transfer_date` (`infrastructure/postgres/tax-property-context.ts:216`) and passes it as `transferDate` (`:247`). Nothing tells the check whether that is the transfer of economic ownership or the contract date. (The tax review cites `:215`; the line moved by one since.)
- **The rule and the window from it:** `checkAnschaffungsnahe` (`domains/taxation/anschaffungsnahe.ts:245`) selects the rule version on that date (`anschaffungsnaheRuleOn`, `:207-209`, called at `:257`) and builds the window from it (`anschaffungsnaheWindow`, `:215-217`, called at `:262`): from the date to the same calendar day three years later. Without a rule the window is `null` and the check `NOT_COMPUTABLE` with `NO_APPLICABLE_RULE` (`:349`); that is the only way to a `null` window today. The response names the date as `transferDate` (`:450`); `CheckAcquisition.transferDate` and `AnschaffungsnaheCheck.transferDate` are non-null (`:62`, `:169`).
- **The read range:** `checkRange` (`tax-property-context.ts:277-292`) takes each check's outer bound from the same date, so the sources read for the check are chosen around the contract date too.
- **The capitalisation on the check:** `acquisitionFactsOf` (`infrastructure/postgres/tax-source-facts.ts:136-148`) reads the same `coalesce` (`:142`), and the create check of a classification with `anschaffungsnaheAcquisitionId` selects the rule and the window from it (`domains/taxation/classification-checks.ts:202-205`). The database repeats it literally: 0062's `tax_classification_anschaffungsnahe()` (`infrastructure/postgres/migrations/0062_classification_partial_treatment.ts:110-148`) reads `coalesce(economic_transfer_date, contract_date) AS transfer_date` (`:119`), `window_until := acq.transfer_date + interval '3 years'` (`:133`), and refuses work outside it (`:136-143`). 0062 is the latest definition of that function (0047 and 0058 defined it before).
- **In the tax-year view:** `buildTaxYearView` lists a check in `acquisitions` only when `c.window !== null` and the window overlaps `year` (`domains/taxation/tax-year-view.ts:255-268`, the filter at `:256`), and raises `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_NOT_FINAL` over the listed ones (`:269-270`). `TaxYearAcquisition.transferDate` and `.window` are non-null (`domains/taxation/tax-year-response.ts:200-208`).
- **The AfA beside it:** the purchase component without `economicTransferDate` has no start and is `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING` with `{ contractDate }` (`domains/depreciation/purchase-work.ts:87`, `:225`; VC-X-33); the recording stage treats a `NOT_COMPUTABLE` check as `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN` (`domains/depreciation/recording-stage.ts:75`).
- **No route sets the date later:** an Acquisition's dates are set on create (§27.1 `POST /acquisitions`); there is no amend, and `CONFIRMED` is final (§27, §28.1). A confirmed Acquisition without `economicTransferDate` keeps it unset for good (open question 4).
- **The silent case:** an Acquisition with `contractDate` 2026-02-01 and no `economicTransferDate` gets the window 2026-02-01 – 2029-02-01, is `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` or `NOT_ABOVE_THRESHOLD` by it, may be `final`, and a capitalisation on it is accepted for work in that window, with no flag naming the assumption. No test pins it as a gap (the check's tests always set a date, e.g. `infrastructure/postgres/tax-weg.test-support.ts:325`).

### The rule

**Without `economicTransferDate` the check has no window: it is `NOT_COMPUTABLE` with the reason `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING`, and nothing of the check is derived from the contract date** (open question 1). In detail:

- **The check's input:** `acquisitionsOf` reads `economic_transfer_date` and `contract_date` separately (no `coalesce`); `CheckAcquisition` gains `contractDate` and its `transferDate` becomes `economicTransferDate` (`BusinessDate | null`).
- **The order of the reasons:** `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING` first, before `NO_APPLICABLE_RULE` (the rule version is chosen on the transfer date, so without it no version is chosen), then the basis function's reasons as today. `NOT_COMPUTABLE_REASONS` gains it (`anschaffungsnahe.ts:74`).
- **The check's fields** (as for `NO_APPLICABLE_RULE` today, open question 2): `transferDate` `null`, `window`, `searchRange`, `outerBound` and `rule` `null`, `status` `NOT_COMPUTABLE`, `notComputableReason` `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING`, no source read or listed (`sources`, `excluded`, `unclassified`, `undetermined`, `outsideSearchRange` empty), `sum` and `sumUpper` 0.00, `attributableAmount`s 0.00, `threshold`, `thresholdWithUnclassified`, `percentOfBasis`s and `affectedYears` `null`, `basis` as far as known (the building's cost does not depend on the date). **`final: false`**, with the `NOT_FINAL` reason `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING` (`NotFinalReason` gains it), and the check flag `{ code: "TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING", details: { contractDate } }` (open; the same code and details as §59A's component reason). No source carries `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_HERSTELLUNGSKOSTEN` or a suggestion from it.
- **`checkRange`** skips such an Acquisition (no outer bound), as it skips one without a rule today.
- **In the tax-year view** (open question 2): the check is listed in `acquisitions` of **every year from the contract's year on** (the window cannot start before `contractDate`, 0020's `acquisition_transfer_dates`, so no earlier year can hold it; its end is unknown), with `transferDate` `null`, `window` `null`, `status` `NOT_COMPUTABLE`, `final` `false`, `notFinalReasons` `["TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING"]`; `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_NOT_FINAL` names it. `TaxYearAcquisition.transferDate` and `.window` become nullable (additive for a client that reads them only when set; a client must accept `null`). A `CANCELLED` Acquisition stays out (`:256`).
- **A capitalisation on the check** (`anschaffungsnaheAcquisitionId`) naming an Acquisition without `economicTransferDate` is refused (open question 3): `422 ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_NOT_APPLICABLE` with `reason = "TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING"` (a new reason of `AnschaffungsnaheNotApplicableReason`), checked after `ACQUISITION_NOT_CONFIRMED` and before `NO_APPLICABLE_RULE` (`classification-checks.ts:202-205`); `acquisitionFactsOf` reads the two dates separately. The database guard refuses the same row (below, "Database"). **Classifications stored before** keep their link (classifications are never updated); their source is not summed by a check that is not computable, and the year is held open by `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_NOT_FINAL`.
- **Nothing else changes:** an Acquisition with `economicTransferDate` (whatever its `contractDate`) gets exactly today's check; the 90-day strip, §59F's performance, §59D's cost classification, the bounds and 236-4 are unchanged.

### Example (synthetic)

PropertyReference P, owned by A `"1/1"`. Acquisition Q: `contractDate` **2026-02-01**, no `economicTransferDate`, price 300,000.00, a confirmed land/building allocation with building 240,000.00 of 300,000.00 (basis 240,000.00, 15 % = 36,000.00), `CONFIRMED`. A repair of 40,000.00 net, `MAINTENANCE` / `DEDUCTIBLE`, performed 2026-05-04 – 2026-06-30, booked 2026-07-10.

- **Today (main 1c03873):** window 2026-02-01 – 2029-02-01 from the contract date; 40,000.00 > 36,000.00: `ABOVE_THRESHOLD`, the repair flagged `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_HERSTELLUNGSKOSTEN` with a suggested `CAPITALIZED`; nothing says the window rests on the contract date. A capitalisation of the repair on Q is accepted.
- **Under §58K:** `NOT_COMPUTABLE`, `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING` (`details: { contractDate: "2026-02-01" }`), `final: false`, no source listed, no suggestion; P's views of 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029 and every later year list Q in `acquisitions` and carry `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_NOT_FINAL` `{ acquisitionIds: [Q] }`; 2025 does not. A capitalisation of the repair on Q answers `422 ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_NOT_APPLICABLE` (`TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING`). The repair stays `DEDUCTIBLE` on `MAINTENANCE` 40,000.00 in 2026; **no figure of any view moves** (the check never changes a figure, §58B).
- **Why the date matters here:** were the transfer 2026-06-01, the repair (performed from 2026-05-04) would straddle the window's start (`PERFORMANCE_STRADDLES_WINDOW`, `START`; a capitalisation refused `STRADDLES_START`, §59F); the contract date would have hidden that.
- **Counter-example:** Acquisition Q′ with `contractDate` 2026-02-01 and `economicTransferDate` 2026-03-15: window 2026-03-15 – 2029-03-15, `ABOVE_THRESHOLD`, exactly as today.

### Flags, reasons and the effect on `final`

| Code | Where | Level | Since |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING` (`notComputableReason`) | the check | — (a reason) | §58K |
| `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING` (`details: { contractDate }`) | the check's `flags` | open | §58K |
| `NOT_FINAL` with reason `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING` | the check's `flags` | open (as today's `NOT_FINAL`) | §58K |
| `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_NOT_FINAL` | the year, every year from the contract's year | open (unchanged code) | §58C |

- **The rule for `final` stays §58C's.** A year of P from the contract's year on is not final while one of its Acquisitions (not `CANCELLED`) lacks `economicTransferDate`. This can turn a `final: true` of today into `false` after deployment (a release note, as VC-X-51's "As implemented" 7). In practice the AfA already holds those years open (§59A's `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING`, VC-X-33).
- **Nothing clears it but the date** (open question 4): no acknowledgement (it is no change flag of §58E), no classification.
- **No interaction with VC-X-28/48/49/50/51's flags** (§58E, §58G–§58J): the check is not an input of a year or a part change; `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED` and `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` are unchanged. An `economicTransferDate` entered later (open question 4) would change the check, not a year or a part.

### Open questions (decided)

1. **How the check reads without the date.** **Proposal:** not computable, `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING` (with `contractDate` in the flag), `final: false`, no window, rule, source list or suggestion; as §59A decided for the AfA's start (2026-10-31, second set) and as the tax review answers (questions 3 and 14). **Alternative:** computed from the contract date with an open flag `TRANSFER_DATE_ASSUMED` on the check (the backlog row's first option): the outcome stays visible, but the check would rest on the contract date, which questions 3 and 14 exclude. **Decided (as proposed; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04, K1):** not computable, `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING`. The alternative is not taken.
2. **Where and how it shows.** **Proposal:** in every tax year of P from the contract's year on (the window can lie anywhere from `contractDate` on), with the fields as for `NO_APPLICABLE_RULE` today (sums 0.00 with no source listed, percentages and threshold `null`). **Alternative:** only in the contract's year up to the contract's year + 3 (a bounded guess at the window, wrong when the transfer comes later), and the sums `null` instead of 0.00 (a change of the check's DTO for one reason). **Decided (as proposed; K2):** in every year from the contract's year on, the fields as for `NO_APPLICABLE_RULE`. The alternative is not taken.
3. **A capitalisation on such an Acquisition.** **Proposal:** refused, `422 ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_NOT_APPLICABLE` with `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING`, in the create check and in the guard (the migration); stored ones keep their link. **Alternative:** accepted without a window check, and judged once the date exists; then the database no longer guarantees "only work performed in the window is capitalised on the check". **Decided (as proposed; K3):** refused in the create check and by 0066's guard; stored ones keep their link. The alternative is not taken.
4. **Entering the date later.** No route sets `economicTransferDate` on an Acquisition, and `CONFIRMED` is final (§27, §28.1); a confirmed Acquisition without it stays not computable for good. **Proposal:** not in VC-X-34; a new backlog row for recording the transfer of economic ownership on a confirmed Acquisition with its evidence (§27.1's `sourceReferences`, the tax review's „Eingabe mit Belegquelle“), which must also say what happens to Ownerships that began on the contract date (P2-D6). **Alternative:** in VC-X-34, `POST /acquisitions/{id}/confirm` refuses an Acquisition without `economicTransferDate` (`422`), so no new confirmed Acquisition lacks it; existing ones stay as above, and §28.1 and the Phase-2 acceptance tests change. **Decided: both (K4, a deviation from the proposal):** the alternative is implemented in VC-X-34 (`confirm` refuses an Acquisition without `economicTransferDate`, `422 CONFIRMATION_BLOCKED` with the violation `TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING`, §28.1 requirement 0; §28.1 and the Phase-2 fixtures carry a date), and the proposal's backlog row is created as **VC-X-52** (recording the transfer of economic ownership on a confirmed Acquisition with its evidence, including the rule for Ownerships that began on the contract date; specified there, not implemented).
5. **Order and tests.** **Proposal:** a small PR of its own, independent of VC-X-40, with the migration of the guard (the next free number), its own e2e test `tax-year-transfer-date.e2e.test.ts`; ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged (both date every Acquisition). **Alternative:** without the guard (open question 3's alternative), no migration. **Decided (as proposed; K5):** a PR of its own with migration 0066 and its own e2e test; ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged. The alternative is not taken.
6. **The rule version.** **Proposal:** `DE_ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE@1` unchanged, its pinned hash too: the start is not a parameter, and the rule's text already says "from the transfer date". **Alternative:** a note in `@1`'s `source` naming questions 3 and 14 (corrected in the same version, as decided for the Phase-7 rules on 2026-11-01), with the pin in `frozen-rules.test.ts` updated explicitly and a counter-check. **Decided (as proposed; K6):** `DE_ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE@1` and its pinned hash unchanged; the rule already said "from the transfer", the code was wrong ("As implemented (VC-X-34)" 8). The alternative is not taken.

**Decided by the owner on 2026-11-04 (chat)** (verbatim, the §58K part and the order; cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04“):

„Reihenfolge: §58K zuerst, damit bekommt VC-X-34 die 0066; dann §58M, dann §58L.“

„**§58K, VC-X-34: wie vorgeschlagen, außer K4**

- **K1 bis K3, K5, K6: wie vorgeschlagen.** Nicht berechenbar ohne Übergangsdatum, in jedem Jahr ab Vertragsjahr, Aktivierung abgelehnt mit Wächter, eigener PR. K6 bleibt unverändert mit stabilem Hash: die Regel sagte schon „ab Übergang“, falsch war der Code, und das gehört in „As implemented“, nicht in die Regel.
- **K4: beides.** In VC-X-34 lehnt `confirm` eine Anschaffung ohne `economicTransferDate` mit `422` ab; der Bericht nennt den Datensatz ohne das Datum unvollständig, und einen unvollständigen Datensatz bestätigt man nicht. §28.1 und die Phase-2-Fixtures bekommen ein Datum. Dazu die neue Backlog-Zeile für das Nachtragen an einer bestätigten Anschaffung mit Beleg, inklusive der Regel für Ownerships, die am Vertragsdatum begannen. Ohne die Zeile bliebe jeder Altbestand dauerhaft nicht final.“

**Deviations from the body:**

1. **`AnschaffungsnaheCheck.contractDate`:** the domain check carries the contract date (the view needs it for the years from the contract's year on); it is not part of the check's DTO (`api/tax-meanings.ts` lists the fields), which shows it only in the flag's `details`, as specified.

Owner to decide whether a later migration adds it.

# 58L. Loan Interest by Periods of Use, Not by the Booking Date (VC-X-40, implemented: migration 0069)

**Status:** **implemented** (VC-X-40, migration 0069, PR #270, not merged; below, "As implemented (VC-X-40)"); specified and decided 2026-11-04. **Open questions 1–12 decided by the owner on 2026-11-04** (chat; "Decided by the owner on 2026-11-04 (chat)" under "Open questions (decided)" at the end of this section; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04): each as proposed, open question 4 with an addition (§58D decision 1 amended; no flag for the deployment; the whole split not attributed where a day of its period lacks a set; the recorded `interestPeriod` on the classification, **plus the new backlog row VC-X-53**, `paymentIntervalMonths` on the Loan's terms; calendar days; the owners on the booking date; one `distribute` per split; `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` as proposed; §59E's case outside the basis with `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS`; terms and closings as part changes not here but **the new backlog row VC-X-54**; its own PR and e2e test, ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged; Financing unchanged). **Order (decided):** §58K (VC-X-34) first, which takes 0066; then §58M (VC-X-27); then §58L (VC-X-40); each migration takes the next free number at implementation. Backlog VC-X-40, created from the tax review of 2026-11-01 (`docs/germany/pruefbericht-2026-11-01.md`, question 22, „Muss geändert werden“; mündlich bestätigt durch den Steuerberater, laut Projektinhaber am 2026-11-01): the allocation follows the actual change of the economic connection; interest period, change of use and payment date are separate; an annual interest paid in December is not allocated by December's use; recommended: interest over periods of use, the payment decides the year. The report lists VC-X-40 **before enablement** (tax-year view, Phase 7; a prerequisite of the go-live of the first productive installation, „Was das für die Freischaltung bedeutet“). **It changes §58D decision 1, which is the owner's (2026-10-31): amended by the owner's decision on open question 1 (2026-11-04), with the tax review as the reason; §58D's text is corrected with the implementation.** **Migration:** none for the rule itself (the view derives on read); one for the recorded interest period (open question 4, decided); none for open questions 9 and 10 as decided. Its number is the next free one at implementation (by the decided order after §58K's 0066 and §58M's; Kysely's Migrator refuses a migration whose name sorts before one already applied). Productive AfA recording stays disabled; nothing here touches it.

**What it amends:** §58D decision 1 ("the `LoanAllocation` set valid on the booking date … nothing is pro-rated"), "How the code's reality shapes" (decision 1), "What the view reads" ("per split: the set covering its booking date"), "The arithmetic" step 2, the example, the item's `loanAllocation`, the flag details and "Cross-check with Financing"; §58G's `partOn` (P's part on one side of a part change) and its "Not a part change" list; §59E's Loan of a capitalised interest source (open question 9).

**Unchanged guarantees:** the tax year (§58A, §58D decision 4): the booking year, the 10-day rule with the schedule's due date (`DE_CASH_TIMING@1` and its pinned hash unchanged), the classification's `taxYear`; the interest period never moves a split between years. Decisions 2, 5, 6 (largest remainder, `distribute`), 7 and, under open question 6's proposal, 3 (the owners on the booking date). Placement, signs, § 82b, the cap, `LOAN_INTEREST_NOT_ATTRIBUTED`'s keys, `UNATTRIBUTED_ITEMS`, the rule for `final`, §58E's year changes and acknowledgements, VC-8-05's AfA. **For every split the parts over all views sum exactly to its amount** (§58D "The arithmetic" 5), and per Loan and year the attributed plus the not attributed interest is the Loan's interest of the year, as today: the change moves interest between PropertyReferences (and, where a period reaches days without a set, from attributed to not attributed), never in or out of the year. The view writes nothing and stores nothing (P7-D8).

**Why a section of its own, after §58K:** VC-X-40 is a backlog item of its own, and its first step is an owner decision on §58D's decision 1. §58D keeps its text until the implementation corrects it (the amendment decided by the owner on 2026-11-04, open question 1).

### As the code stands (main 1c03873; paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`)

- **The view's set per split:** `loanInterestOf` (`domains/taxation/tax-year-loan-interest.ts:74-109`) takes `setOn(loanSets, bookingDateOf(split.item))` (`:81`; `setOn`, `domains/financing/allocation.ts:80-82`: `VALID`, `validFrom ≤ day ≤ validUntil`), and P's part is `distribute(centsOf(amount), set.allocations)[index]` (`:95`; `distribute`, `domains/financing/debt.ts:92-102`, largest remainder over the whole set). Without a set or with a sum ≠ `1/1` the split is `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` (`:82-91`). Called once per view (`domains/taxation/tax-year-view.ts:171`). (The tax review cites `:76`; the lines moved since.)
- **The item's allocation** is one set: `TaxYearLoanAllocation` (`domains/taxation/tax-year-response.ts:153-163`: `allocationSetId`, `validFrom`, `validUntil`, `basis`, `share`, `propertyPart`, `taxConfirmation`); `LOAN_ALLOCATION_BY_PURCHASE_PRICE_TO_VERIFY` names that one set (`tax-year-loan-interest.ts:127-131`).
- **The interest period exists, but only for the 10-day rule:** `interestTiming` (`domains/taxation/cash-timing.ts:123-141`) takes the schedule entry nearest to the booking date and gives `economicPeriod` from the day after the previous entry (or one month before the first) to its payment date. `timingOf` computes it only for splits the rule could move (`needsTiming`: a recurring category booked in a window, `infrastructure/postgres/tax-source-facts.ts:183`), reading the Loan's `VALID` terms and `loanSchedule` (`:243-258`). Outside the windows no period is read.
- **The schedule is monthly only:** §41.4's schedule has monthly payments from `firstPaymentDate` (`domains/financing/terms.ts:5-9`, `:129`). An interest the lender debits quarterly or yearly has no schedule entry of its own; `interestTiming` gives it the one month before the nearest monthly entry. *(Since VC-X-53, §58O: the terms state `paymentIntervalMonths`, the plan pays every 1, 3, 6 or 12 months, and the first entry's period is its interval; the interval on the terms is the lasting source of a quarterly or yearly period, Example 2 with interval 12 needs no recorded period.)*
- **The read:** `allocatedLoanInterest` (`infrastructure/postgres/tax-year-reads.ts:243-281`) reads the candidate splits, their meanings (`meaningsOf`, with `timingOf` inside) and every set of their Loans with `validUntil` (`:278-279`). It does not read the Loan's terms or `debtFrom` for the view.
- **The part change (§58G) uses the same rule twice:** `partOn` (`domains/taxation/attribution-part-rule.ts:23-39`) takes the set on the candidate's booking date (`:29`) and `distribute` (`:33`); called by the set history (`domains/taxation/attribution-parts.ts:169`) and by the split corrections (`domains/taxation/attribution-corrections.ts:67`, §58I Part 2).
- **§59E's capitalised interest** carries one set: `CapitalizedSourceInput.loan` `{ loanId, set, propertyCents }` and `CapitalizedSourceLoan` `{ loanId, allocationSetId, share, propertyPart }` (`domains/taxation/capitalized-items.ts:25`, `:31-37`), stored in a recorded version's component as `loan_id`, `allocation_set_id`, `share_numerator`, `share_denominator`, all set or all null (0055, `infrastructure/postgres/migrations/0055_construction_period_interest.ts:274-286`).
- **Financing's per-property payments** use the booking date too: `paymentsInYear` (`domains/financing/debt.ts:211-242`) takes `setOn(sets, s.bookingDate)` (`:228`) and refuses the year with `LOAN_NOT_ALLOCATED` where none covers it (`:229`). §58D decision 6 makes the view's part of a split equal to Financing's.

### The rule (decided 2026-11-04, open question 1)

**Each attributed interest split is distributed over its interest period, by the allocation sets valid on each day of it; the payment still decides the year.**

1. **The interest period** of a split with a `loanId`: the recorded `interestPeriod` of its current classification where one is given (open question 4, decided; for the allocation only, never for the 10-day rule), else the schedule's `economicPeriod` of `interestTiming` (§58A; the nearest entry, the day after the previous one to its payment date), computed for **every** candidate interest split, not only in the windows, and **clipped at the Loan's `debtFrom`** (§41.1, `domains/financing/loan.ts:67`: no interest accrues before the debt). The 10-day rule keeps reading its own timing as today (`timingOf`); the period here is a second use of the same function, not a change of §58A.
2. **The days:** every calendar day of the period, both ends inclusive (open question 5). For each day d, the set covering d (`setOn(sets, d)`, as recorded now, §58D "How the code's reality shapes"). Consecutive days with the same set form a **segment** `(set, days)`.
3. **Covered:** every day has a usable set (a complete `VALID` set, `sumsToOne`). Otherwise the split is **not attributed** (open question 3), reason `NO_LOAN_ALLOCATION` (some day without a set) or `ALLOCATION_SUM_NOT_ONE` (defensive, as today), with the uncovered days in the entry.
4. **P's weight** in a covered split: `w_P = Σ over segments (days_k / D) × share_k(P)`, with D the period's days and `share_k(P)` P's share in the segment's set (0 without an entry): an exact fraction, reduced. The weights of all PropertyReferences named by the segments' sets sum to exactly `1/1`.
5. **The parts:** one call of the existing `distribute` over those weights (`distribute(A, [{ propertyReferenceId, share: w_P }])`, §41.6: largest remainder, ties by `propertyReferenceId`), **once per split** (open question 7). The parts sum exactly to A; every view computes the same parts, since each distributes over the whole union.
6. **Case per view:** `ATTRIBUTED` when `w_P > 0`; `ELSEWHERE` when the split is covered and `w_P = 0`; `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` as in 3, listed in the views of every PropertyReference named by a `VALID` set of the Loan (today's `candidates`, unchanged).
7. **A period in one set** (the common case: no set boundary inside it) gives `w_P` = P's share in that set, so the part is exactly today's `distribute` over that set. **Only a split whose period contains a set boundary, or a day before the first set, changes.**
8. **Without a period** (no `VALID` terms, `NO_SCHEDULE`; open question 8): the split is distributed by the set on its **booking date** (today's rule) and carries the item flag `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN`.
9. **The owners** of P's part: the participants on the **booking date** by §58C's `shareOut` (decision 3 unchanged; open question 6).
10. **The tax year** is untouched: an interest period reaching into the previous year (December's interest paid in January) is distributed by that December's sets, and the split stays in the year §58A gives it.

### Examples (synthetic)

PropertyReferences P1 and P2 (`propertyReferenceId` P1 < P2). P1 owned by A and B `"1/2"` each (A < B), P2 by C `"1/1"`, all from 2026-01-01. Confirmed `OUTFLOW` debits with a `LOAN_INTEREST` split carrying the Loan's `loanId`.

**1. A set change within an interest period.** Loan L: `debtFrom` 2027-01-01, terms with `firstPaymentDate` 2027-01-31 (monthly, due on the last day). Sets, `MANUAL`: S1 from 2027-01-01, P1 `"1/1"`; S2 from **2027-03-16**, P1 `"1/2"`, P2 `"1/2"`.

| Booking date | Interest | Period (schedule) | Segments | Today (set on the booking date) | §58L |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2027-03-31 | 310.00 | 2027-03-01 – 2027-03-31, 31 days | S1 15 days, S2 16 days | S2: P1 155.00, P2 155.00 | `w_P1` = 15/31 + 16/31 × 1/2 = **23/31**, `w_P2` = **8/31**: P1 **230.00**, P2 **80.00** |
| 2027-04-30 | 300.00 | 2027-04-01 – 2027-04-30 | S2 30 days | S2: 150.00, 150.00 | S2 alone: 150.00, 150.00 (unchanged) |

- **The owners:** P1's 230.00 → A 115.00, B 115.00; 150.00 → 75.00 each; P2's parts → C.
- **2027, sum across views unchanged:** today P1 305.00 + P2 305.00; under §58L P1 380.00 + P2 230.00; both **610.00**, exactly the two debits. Each split's parts sum to its amount in both.
- **Cent rounding via `distribute`** (had the 2027-03-31 interest been **100.00**): 10,000 cents × 23/31 = 7,419.35… and × 8/31 = 2,580.64…; the floors 7,419 and 2,580 leave one cent, which goes to the larger remainder (0.64…, P2): **P1 74.19, P2 25.81**, summing to 100.00. P1's 7,419 over A and B are 3,709.5 each: the cent by the lower `ownerPartyId`, **A 37.10, B 37.09**. (Rounded in two steps, open question 7's alternative: the segments 48.39 and 51.61 by days, then each by its set, P1 48.39 + 25.81 = 74.20 and P2 25.80; one cent apart.)

**2. Annual interest paid in December across a change of use.** Loan M: `debtFrom` 2026-01-01, `INTEREST_ONLY` terms with `firstPaymentDate` 2026-01-31 (DE's schedule is monthly); the lender debits the year's interest once, on **2027-12-30**: **3,650.00** for 2027-01-01 – 2027-12-31. Sets, `MANUAL`: T1 from 2026-01-01, P1 `"1/1"`; T2 from **2027-10-01**, P2 `"1/1"` (the funds' use changed on that day).

- **Today:** the set on 2027-12-30 is T2: **P2 3,650.00**, P1 nothing. This is the case question 22 names („Jahreszins im Dezember nicht nach Dezember-Verwendung aufteilen“).
- **§58L with the schedule's period alone:** the nearest entry is 2027-12-31, the period 2027-12-01 – 2027-12-31, wholly T2: **still P2 3,650.00**. The monthly schedule cannot say the interest is annual (open question 4; the payment interval on the terms is backlog VC-X-53).
- **§58L with the year as the interest period** (open question 4, decided: a recorded period 2027-01-01 – 2027-12-31): T1 273 days (January–September), T2 92 days, D = 365: P1 3,650.00 × 273/365 = **2,730.00** (A 1,365.00, B 1,365.00), P2 × 92/365 = **920.00** (C). Sum 3,650.00.
- **The year:** 2027 in every variant (booked in 2027; the schedule's due date 2027-12-31 lies in 2027). **Variant, paid 2028-01-05:** the 10-day rule (the schedule's due date 2027-12-31, in the window) puts it into 2027 with `ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE`, exactly as today; its parts are those above, and no set of 2028-01-05 is read for it.

**3. The first period and a day before the first set.** Loan N: `debtFrom` 2027-03-16, `firstPaymentDate` 2027-03-31; set U1 from 2027-03-16, P1 `"1/1"`; interest 81.00 booked 2027-03-31.

- The schedule's period would be 2027-03-01 – 2027-03-31 (one month before the first entry); **clipped at `debtFrom`** it is 2027-03-16 – 2027-03-31, wholly U1: P1 81.00, as today.
- **Variant, U1 from 2027-03-20:** the days 2027-03-16 – 2027-03-19 have no set. Today the booking date is covered: P1 81.00. Under §58L (open question 3, decided) the split is **not attributed**, `NO_LOAN_ALLOCATION` with `uncovered: [{ from: "2027-03-16", until: "2027-03-19" }]`, listed in P1's `notAttributed`, and P1's 2027 carries `LOAN_INTEREST_NOT_ATTRIBUTED` (`interestTotal` 81.00). Under the alternative (not taken): P1 60.75 (12 of 16 days) attributed, 20.25 not attributed.

### In the view (additive DTO changes)

- **`loanAllocation`** of an item gains `interestPeriod: { from, until, source }` (`source`: `LOAN_SCHEDULE`, or the recorded period (open question 4, decided); `null` under rule 8) and `segments: [{ from, until, allocationSetId, basis, share }]` (P's share in the segment's set, `null` where P has no entry), sorted by `from`. `share` is P's weight `w_P` (`"23/31"`); `allocationSetId`, `validFrom`, `validUntil` and `basis` name the set when one set covers the whole period, else `null`. `propertyPart` is P's part, as today.
- **A not attributed entry** gains the same `interestPeriod` and `uncovered: [{ from, until }]`; its `href` stays `/loans/{id}/allocations?asOf=<bookingDate>`.
- **`LOAN_ALLOCATION_BY_PURCHASE_PRICE_TO_VERIFY`:** one entry per multi-entry `PURCHASE_PRICE` set among the item's segments, each `{ loanId, allocationSetId, confirmation }` (§58E Part 3: confirming a set clears only its own entry; the item flag is informative once every one is confirmed).
- **New item flag `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN`** (rule 8): `details: { loanId, reason: "NO_SCHEDULE" }`; **open** when the Loan has more than one `VALID` set, **informative** with exactly one (open question 8).
- **No other code** is added or removed; `LOAN_INTEREST_NOT_ATTRIBUTED`'s keys (`loanIds`, `interestTotal`, `splitIds`) are unchanged.

### The effect on `final`

- **The rule for `final` stays §58C's.** A year can become not final (a period reaching a day before the Loan's first set, Example 3's variant; an `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` open) or final (interest booked before a set's `validFrom` whose whole period the set covers, e.g. paid early); figures of P1 and P2 move between them as in Example 1. **A release note** names both after deployment. No year is productively filed yet (the go-live of the first productive installation waits for VC-X-40, among others), so no flag is raised by the deployment itself (open question 2).
- **ACC7 and ACC8** (open question 11): ACC8's Loan (terms from 2026-07-31, set from 2026-10-01, interest booked 2026-09-20) has the period 2026-09-01 – 2026-09-30 without a set: not attributed, `NO_LOAN_ALLOCATION`, the year's flags exactly `["LOAN_INTEREST_NOT_ATTRIBUTED"]` as today. **ACC7's two Loans have no terms** (no schedule): both fall under rule 8, by the booking date as today (450.00 attributed `"1/1"`, 120.00 not attributed); the first carries `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` **informative** (one `VALID` set), which ACC7 does not assert against, and the second is listed as today. **So both run unchanged under the decisions** (open questions 8 and 11, as proposed).

### Interaction with VC-X-28/48/49/50/51 (§58E, §58G–§58J)

- **`ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED` (§58E, VC-X-28; §58H Part 1's `LOAN_CLOSED`):** unchanged. The interest period moves no year (rule 10), so no year kind gains or loses a change.
- **`PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` (§58G, VC-X-48) — does a changed distribution count?** **Yes, when a record moved it, by §58G's one rule unchanged:** `partOn` becomes the period distribution (the same function as the view), so a set added or voided after 31 December of the item's year is a part change whenever it changes P's part, now also when it covers only days inside a period. Example 1 with S2 recorded on **2028-02-10**: the debit of 2027-03-31 moves P1 310.00 → 230.00 (`ATTRIBUTED` → `ATTRIBUTED`) and P2 `NONE` → `ATTRIBUTED` 80.00 (today 310.00 → 155.00 and → 155.00): both 2027 views flagged, with the new parts in `items` and in the fingerprint. **§58G's "Not a part change: a set appended with a `validFrom` after every booked split"** narrows to "after the end of every booked split's interest period" (a debit booked 2027-03-28 for a period to 2027-03-31 and a set from 2027-03-30 is a part change under §58L, none today).
- **The deployment itself is no part change:** it is no AuditRecord, and §58G's rule compares two sides of one record with the code as it is. Figures that move by the new rule move without a flag (open question 2).
- **Terms and a closing move the period, not only the year:** a `LoanTerms` record (`LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`/`_VOIDED`) or a Loan's `CLOSED` record after the year's end changes the schedule's entries, so a split's period and with it P's part, also outside the windows and without a year change. Today those records are only year kinds (0065's `tax_year_acknowledgement_kind_entity` binds `LoanTerms` and `Loan` to the year shape, and the part-item trigger admits only the set, deposit and correction kinds, `0065_tax_year_deposit_and_correction_movers.ts:21-33`, `:59`). Open question 10, decided: not in VC-X-40 but backlog **VC-X-54**; until then a test pins that such a record after the year's end can move a part without a flag. **Done (VC-X-54, §58P, migration 0071):** such a record is a part change of kind `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`, `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED` or `LOAN_CLOSED_PART`; the pin is replaced by its inverse with a counter-check.
- **A recorded interest period** (open question 4, decided) is a person's statement on the split, like a `taxYear` override (§58G "Not a part change"): no part change.
- **§58H Part 2 (VC-X-49), §58I Part 1 (VC-X-50), §58J (VC-X-51):** deposits only; unaffected. **§58I Part 2's split corrections** compare P's parts with `partOn` (`attribution-corrections.ts:67`) and follow the new rule; a correction that changes an interest split's booking date can now move its period and so its part, which that rule already flags.
- **§58E Part 3's set confirmations:** per set, unchanged; an item spanning two multi-entry `PURCHASE_PRICE` sets needs both confirmed (above).

### Database

- **The rule itself: no migration.** Nothing is stored; the view, the part changes and §59E's matching derive on read.
- **Decided (2026-11-04): one migration,** for the recorded interest period (open question 4: `tax_classification.interest_period_from`/`_until`, both or neither, from ≤ until, only on a `LOAN_INTEREST` split with a `loanId`, guarded past the repository like §59F's performance), the next free number at implementation (after §58K's 0066 and §58M's, the decided order).
- **Not in VC-X-40:** the part kinds of terms and closings (open question 10: backlog VC-X-54, there `change_kind`, `kind_entity` and the part-item trigger of 0065 widened); a recorded §59E component without a single set (open question 9: not taken; `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS` instead, 0055 unchanged).
- **No route changes;** `docs/development/api-inventory.md` unchanged.

### Tests and mutations

- **Domain (pure), a new file** `domains/taxation/tax-year-loan-periods.test.ts` (`tax-year-loan-interest.test.ts` has 628 lines): Examples 1–3 at both levels with every figure above (the parts, the owners, 2027's lines, the cent case and its tie at the owner level); the period in one set equal to today's `distribute` (rule 7) for a property-based sample over seeded sets and periods; **unchanged money sums:** for every split the parts over all views sum to its amount, per Loan and year attributed + not attributed = the Loan's interest, and every non-interest line, section and `result` is the same as without the change; the year unchanged in every case, including the 10-day variant of Example 2 (`ATTRIBUTED_BY_10_DAY_RULE` as today); the clip at `debtFrom`; a period across 31 December allocated by December's sets and kept in its §58A year; `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` open and informative; `LOAN_ALLOCATION_BY_PURCHASE_PRICE_TO_VERIFY` per segment set; §58G's part change for Example 1 recorded after the year's end, and a set within the period after the booking date (a part change now); the recorded `interestPeriod` (open question 4): Example 2 with the recorded year (P1 2,730.00, P2 920.00), the 10-day rule ignoring it; a `LoanTerms` record after the year's end moving a part without a flag, pinned until VC-X-54.
- **Repository (PostgreSQL):** Example 1 through the real read (terms, sets, splits), the view's and `partOn`'s parts equal; **Realm isolation:** another Realm's Loan with the same dates and sets changes nothing here, every new query (terms, `debtFrom`) carries the Realm; the recorded period's guard past the repository with a counter-check (a raw insert with `from` > `until`, with one end only, on a split without `loanId`; each accepted for a valid row); **history:** the sets' and terms' AuditRecords as today, and reading the view writes no AuditRecord and no row ("no cash mutated").
- **End to end:** a new `tax-year-loan-periods.e2e.test.ts`: Example 1 and 3 through the HTTP API at both levels, the part change of S2 recorded after the year's end, Realm isolation. ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged (above; open question 11).

**Mutations** that must turn the tests red (each applied alone, restored byte for byte): the set taken on the booking date again (`setOn(…, bookingDate)` in the new function); the period's last day dropped (exclusive end); the clip at `debtFrom` removed; the weights distributed per segment and summed (two roundings, the cent case moves); an uncovered day ignored (Example 3's variant attributed); the view's function and `partOn` diverging (one of them on the booking date); the 10-day rule fed with the allocation period (a year moves); `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` always informative (as decided); the recorded `interestPeriod` ignored (Example 2 by December's use again) or fed to the 10-day rule (a year moves); the guard on the recorded period without its `from ≤ until` test.

### The text that changes with the implementation

- **§58D decision 1** (amended by the owner's decision of 2026-11-04, open question 1): „The allocation follows the periods of use: each interest split over its interest period by the sets valid on each day (§58L); the payment decides the year (§58A).“ The original wording stays quoted as the decision of 2026-10-31, amended on the owner's date. "How the code's reality shapes" (decision 1), "What the view reads" (per split), "The arithmetic" step 2, the example's set column and "Cross-check with Financing" point to §58L.
- **§58G** "P's part of an item" and "Not a part change" as above; **§59E**: the reason `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS` (open question 9, decided).
- **The invariant suite** (`docs/development/invariant-suite.md:867`, "Interest of an allocated Loan is never silent"): "where a usable set covers their booking date" becomes "where usable sets cover every day of their interest period".

### As implemented (VC-X-40)

Implemented as specified and decided (L1–L12, Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04), with **migration 0069** (the next free number after §58M's 0068; verified: 0068 was the last on main e7cb10e). Paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`.

**What was built:**

1. **One function for every reader** (`domains/taxation/loan-interest-periods.ts`): `interestPeriodOf` (rule 1: the classification's recorded period, else `interestTiming`'s schedule period clipped at `debtFrom`; `null` without payment dates) and `distributeOverPeriod` (rules 2–8: the `VALID` sets' segments over the period, calendar days both inclusive, `uncovered` days, `ALLOCATION_SUM_NOT_ONE` defensively, the exact weights `w_P` reduced, **one** `distribute` over them; without a period the booking date's set). `loanInterestOf` (the view), `partOn` (§58G, and through it §58I Part 2's `splitPartOn`) and §59E's `capitalizedLoanInterestOf` all call it, so they cannot drift.
2. **The read** (`infrastructure/postgres/loan-interest-periods.ts`, `loanPeriodFactsOf`): each candidate Loan's `debtFrom` and the payment dates of its `VALID` terms' schedule (`loanSchedule`, cut at a closing as Financing's), in the view's snapshot and **in the Realm** (`readLoanIn`; `periodsOf` gained an optional Realm filter). Used by `allocatedLoanInterest` (view, §58G's candidates), `capitalizedLoanInterestOf` (§59E) and `correctionHistoriesOf` (§58I Part 2: each split's period by its own booking date and classification). The 10-day rule's `timingOf` is unchanged and never sees the recorded period.
3. **The DTO** (additive): `loanAllocation.interestPeriod` (`{ from, until, source }`, `source` `LOAN_SCHEDULE` or `CLASSIFICATION`; `null` under rule 8) and `loanAllocation.segments` (`[{ from, until, allocationSetId, basis, share }]`, P's share in each set or `null`; `[]` under rule 8); `share` is `w_P`; `allocationSetId`, `validFrom`, `validUntil`, `basis` and `taxConfirmation` name the set only when one set covers the whole period (or, under rule 8, the booking date). A not attributed Loan entry gains `interestPeriod` and `uncovered` (in the API flattened beside `reason`, `candidates`, `href`).
4. **Flags:** `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` (item, rule 8) with `details: { loanId, reason: "NO_SCHEDULE", validAllocationSets }`, open with more than one `VALID` set, informative with one (`flagIsOpen`); `LOAN_ALLOCATION_BY_PURCHASE_PRICE_TO_VERIFY` once per multi-entry `PURCHASE_PRICE` set among the segments, each with its own `confirmation`; §59E's `LOAN_INTEREST_CAPITALIZED_NOT_IN_BASIS` and `capitalizedSourcesOf`'s `notSources` gain the reason `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS` (after the record's reasons, before the basis check).
5. **The recorded period (L4):** `POST /tax-classifications` takes `interestPeriod: { from, until }` (`until` not before `from`, else `400 OUT_OF_RANGE`; a source other than `TRANSACTION_SPLIT`: `400 NOT_SUPPORTED`); on a split without a `loanId` or not of category `LOAN_INTEREST` the create refuses with `400 NOT_SUPPORTED` at `interestPeriod` (the existing `FIELD_NOT_SUPPORTED`). Stored, in the response and in the `TAX_CLASSIFIED` AuditRecord's metadata only when given; the idempotency fingerprint gains it only when given (keys stored before replay). No route changes; `docs/development/api-inventory.md` unchanged (`yarn api:inventory:check` green).
6. **Migration 0069** (`0069_loan_interest_period.ts`): `tax_classification.interest_period_from`/`_until` (`date`); CHECK `tax_classification_interest_period` (both or neither, `from ≤ until`, only with `source_type` `TRANSACTION_SPLIT`); the before-insert guard `tax_classification_interest_period_split` (the split of the Realm has a `loan_id` and the category `LOAN_INTEREST`, else `INTEREST_PERIOD_NOT_ALLOWED`); 0068's frozen guard `tax_classification_weg_source_fixed` covers the two columns. No backfill; `down` refuses while a period is stated.

**Deviations and interpretations** (none changes a decided rule):

- (a) The recorded period's `source` is named `CLASSIFICATION` (the section left the value open; as `ofYearSource`).
- (b) `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN`'s `details` carry a third key, `validAllocationSets`, besides `loanId` and `reason`: the review decides open or informative from the flag itself (L8), as `LOAN_ALLOCATION_BY_PURCHASE_PRICE_TO_VERIFY` reads its `confirmation`.
- (c) The clip at `debtFrom` applies to the schedule's period only (rule 1 places it there); a recorded period is the lender's statement and is taken as recorded. No further bound (length, nearness to the booking date) is checked: none is specified.

**Release note** (open question 2, decided: no flag for the deployment): *From VC-X-40 on, the tax-year view distributes each Loan interest split over the days of its interest period by the allocation sets valid on each day, instead of by the set on its booking date (§58D decision 1 as amended by the owner on 2026-11-04). Figures move between PropertyReferences only where an interest period contains a set change (or a day before the first set, then the whole split is shown as not attributed); a year can become not final (a period reaching before the Loan's first set; `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` open for a Loan without terms and with several sets) or final (interest booked before a set's `validFrom` whose period the set covers). The tax year of every split, the totals per Loan and year, and Financing's payments read are unchanged. December's interest paid in January is distributed by December's sets. A period differing from the monthly schedule (annual or quarterly interest) can be recorded on the classification (`interestPeriod`); the payment interval on the terms follows with VC-X-53, terms and closings as part changes with VC-X-54. No year is productively filed yet, so no change flag is raised by the deployment.*

### Open questions (decided)

1. **Amend §58D decision 1** (the owner's, 2026-10-31), with the tax review's question 22 as the reason. **Decided (as proposed):** amend it to the rule above: each interest split over its interest period by the sets valid on each day, the payment still deciding the year, nothing else of §58D changed. **Alternative (not taken):** keep decision 1 (the booking date) and raise an open item flag on each interest item whose interest period contains a set boundary, figures unchanged and the year not final, until a person states the split; this stays „abweichend“ against question 22.
2. **No flag for the deployment.** **Decided (as proposed):** the figures that move by the new rule move without a change flag (a code change is no record, and no year is productively filed before the go-live this item is a prerequisite of), with a release note. **Alternative (not taken):** a one-time informative year flag `ALLOCATION_RULE_CHANGED` on each year whose interest parts differ from the booking-date rule, which needs the old rule kept beside the new one.
3. **A period with days without a set.** **Decided (as proposed):** the whole split not attributed (`NO_LOAN_ALLOCATION` with `uncovered`), never estimated, as decision 5 says for a booking date without a set. **Alternative (not taken):** the covered days' part attributed and the rest listed as not attributed, one split in two places (`lineAmount` and a not attributed remainder), more precise but a new shape of `notAttributed`.
4. **Where the interest period comes from.** DE's schedule is monthly only, so the schedule alone never gives an annual or quarterly period, and Example 2 stays allocated by December's use. **Decided (as proposed, with an addition):** an optional recorded interest period on the split's classification (`interestPeriod: { from, until }`, evidence from the lender's statement, as §59F's performance; migration), which wins over the schedule's for the allocation only, never for the 10-day rule. **Addition (the owner's):** a new backlog row, **VC-X-53**: `paymentIntervalMonths` on the Loan's terms, the lasting place of the fact (an annually paying Loan has a wrong schedule and a wrong remaining debt today too); once it exists, a recorded `interestPeriod` that deviates from the schedule is flagged. **Alternative (not taken in VC-X-40; it becomes VC-X-53):** a payment interval on the Loan's terms (§41.2, `paymentIntervalMonths` 1/3/6/12), which changes §41.4's schedule, the remaining debt and the payments read too.
5. **Counting the days.** **Decided (as proposed):** calendar days, both ends inclusive (taggenau, as the use changes on a day). **Alternative (not taken):** 30/360, as the schedule computes interest (`terms.ts:8`): a February day weighs more, a 31st nothing.
6. **The owners of P's part.** **Decided (as proposed):** unchanged, the owners on the booking date (decision 3, §58C's one share date for every item; question 22 speaks of the Loan's use, not of the owners). **Alternative (not taken):** the owners per day of the interest period as well, a second distribution with its own rounding and a second share date only for interest.
7. **Rounding.** **Decided (as proposed):** one `distribute` per split over the exact weights (one rounding, the parts sum exactly, §58D decision 6's "once per step"). **Alternative (not taken):** two steps, the split by days over the segments, then each segment over its set (each segment reads like a split of its own; one cent apart in Example 1's cent case).
8. **No schedule.** **Decided (as proposed):** by the booking date's set, with `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN`, open when the Loan has more than one `VALID` set and informative with one (ACC7 unchanged). **Alternative (a, not taken):** always open: ACC7's 2027 gains an open `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` (count 1; ACC7's assertions still pass, 2027 is not final anyway, but `review.open` changes). **Alternative (b, not taken):** not attributed: ACC7's 450.00 leaves `LOAN_INTEREST` (2,899.48 → 2,449.48) and ACC7 must change.
9. **§59E's capitalised interest across a set change.** A recorded component stores one `allocation_set_id` and share (0055). **Decided (as proposed):** a capitalised interest split whose period spans more than one set keeps `LOAN_INTEREST_CAPITALIZED_NOT_IN_BASIS` open with a new reason `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS` and enters no basis (Bauzeitzinsen with a change of use in the period are rare); recording stays disabled anyway. **Alternative (not taken):** the component stores the weight with `allocation_set_id` `NULL` (0055's CHECK relaxed, migration).
10. **Terms and closings as part changes.** **Decided (as proposed):** not in VC-X-40; a new backlog row (**VC-X-54**, created) for `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` kinds of `LoanTerms` and `Loan` `CLOSED` records (migration), as VC-X-49 left VC-X-50; until then a test pins that such a record after the year's end can move a part without a flag. **Alternative (not taken):** in VC-X-40, new part kinds (e.g. `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`, `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED`, `LOAN_CLOSED_PART`) with 0065's CHECKs and trigger widened; one AuditRecord can then be a year and a part change (`CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS`, §58G open question 4).
11. **Order, tests, ACC7 and ACC8.** **Decided (as proposed):** after the owner's decision on 1, a PR of its own (no migration unless 4, 9 or 10 need one; as decided, 4 needs one, 9 and 10 none), its own e2e test `tax-year-loan-periods.e2e.test.ts`; ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged (above). **Alternative (not taken):** Example 1 added to ACC7 (a second set in 2027), which changes ACC7's 2027 figures.
12. **Financing's per-property payments.** **Decided (as proposed):** unchanged (`paymentsInYear` by the booking date's set: a payments and debt read by ADR-038's one key on the day, not a tax figure); §58D's cross-check narrowed to splits whose period lies in one set, and the difference documented. **Alternative (not taken):** Financing distributes interest by periods too, so the two reads agree again; a change of §41.6 and its tests.

**Decided by the owner on 2026-11-04 (chat)** (verbatim; cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04“; the owner's preamble for §58K, §58L and §58M, then the part on §58L; L1–L12 are open questions 1–12 above; the part on §58K is recorded with VC-X-34, the part on §58M in §58M):

> Ich lese die drei Abschnitte §58K, §58L und §58M auf `main` mit ihren offenen Fragen.
>
> Hier die 29 Entscheidungen. Abweichungen vom Vorschlag: K4 (beides), L4 (Vorschlag plus Backlog-Zeile), M3 (Alternative). Reihenfolge: §58K zuerst, damit bekommt VC-X-34 die 0066; dann §58M, dann §58L.
>
> **§58L, VC-X-40: wie vorgeschlagen, L4 mit Zusatz**
>
> - **L1: §58D Entscheidung 1 wird geändert**, wie vorgeschlagen. Frage 22 sagt „muss geändert werden“; die Alternative bliebe abweichend und würde das Go-live blockieren. Nur die Zuordnung des Zinses über den Zinszeitraum, die Zahlung entscheidet weiter das Jahr.
> - **L2, L3, L5 bis L12: wie vorgeschlagen.** Kein Deployment-Flag, ganzer Split nicht zugeordnet bei Lücken, Kalendertage, Eigentümer am Buchungstag, eine Verteilung je Split, `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` wie vorgeschlagen, §59E-Fall bleibt mit `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS` außerhalb der Basis, Konditionen und Schließungen als neue Zeile, eigener E2E-Test, Financing bleibt operativ.
> - **L4: wie vorgeschlagen, plus eine Backlog-Zeile.** Der erfasste `interestPeriod` an der Klassifikation macht das Dezember-Beispiel abbildbar und ist verhältnismäßig, weil deutsche Annuitätendarlehen fast immer monatlich zahlen. Der dauerhaft richtige Ort des Fakts ist aber das Zahlungsintervall in den Konditionen, denn ein jährlich zahlendes Darlehen hat heute auch einen falschen Plan und eine falsche Restschuld. Also neue Zeile `paymentIntervalMonths` an den Terms; sobald sie da ist, wird ein erfasster Zeitraum, der vom Plan abweicht, geflaggt.
