# 58O. Payment Interval on the Loan's Terms (VC-X-53, implemented: migration 0070)

**Status:** **implemented** (VC-X-53, migration 0070; below, "As implemented (VC-X-53)"); **open questions 1–12 decided by the owner on 2026-11-05**, all as proposed, 8 and 12 with additions (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05; below, "Open questions (decided)"). Specified as: backlog VC-X-53, created by the owner's decision on §58L open question 4 (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04). **Migration:** one, the next free number at implementation (0070 at the time of writing: main 10709ad ends at 0069). Productive AfA recording stays disabled; nothing here touches it, and no unconfirmed tax assumption reads as released by it (open question 8 names the one tax question this item raises).

**What it amends:** §41.2 (the field `paymentIntervalMonths`, its order of checks, the annuity check 7, "In the database"; the bullet "`paymentFrequency`: unknown key; Phase 3 is monthly only" and P3-D2's "monthly only"), §41.4 (payment dates, interest, the 600-payment cap), §41.5's proposal and §41.6's planned remaining debt (through the schedule only), §41.7's cut schedule (unchanged rule, new dates), §58A's due date of a Loan interest split (`interestTiming`'s first period), §58L rule 1 (the schedule's period now follows the interval) and its "As implemented (VC-X-40)" (the new item flag for a recorded `interestPeriod` that deviates from the plan); data-model §21/§22 (`paymentFrequency` "not stored" becomes `paymentIntervalMonths`, stored).

**Unchanged guarantees:** with `paymentIntervalMonths = 1`, the value of every existing terms period (no backfill, the column's default), **every derived figure is the same as today, cent for cent and byte for byte apart from the new DTO key**: the schedule, the planned remaining debt and its per-property parts, the payment proposal, the payments read (open question 12's proposal changes the schedule's later rows, `planned`, `difference` and `fixedRateEnd` only where the bookings deviate from the plan, and the proposal only where a purpose text states the split), §58A's years and due dates, §58L's periods and parts, §59E's sources, ACC7 and ACC8. Terms stay appended, never edited, only the last one voidable (P3-D2). The ledger stays the truth (ADR-015): the interval changes only the plan, never a split, a classification or cash. §58L's rules 2–10 (calendar days, one `distribute` per split, uncovered days, rule 8 without a schedule, the owners on the booking date, the year by payment) are unchanged; the recorded `interestPeriod` is never read by the 10-day rule; its precedence against the plan is "Precedence of the plan and the recorded `interestPeriod`" below (open question 11). `DE_CASH_TIMING@1` and its pinned hash are unchanged (the hash covers the rule's parameters, `infrastructure/hashing/frozen-rules.test.ts:85`, not the schedule). Realm isolation, idempotency and the locks of P3-D8 are unchanged. Financing's `paymentsInYear` (§41.6) stays by the booking date's set (§58L decision 12).

**Why a section of its own, after §58N:** VC-X-53 is a backlog item of its own; §58L created it and left the payment interval out of VC-X-40, so its number is the next free letter (verified: §58N is the last §58 letter on main 10709ad).

### The decided fact (verbatim)

Cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04“ (the owner's answer on §58L open question 4, L4; recorded in full in §58L "Decided by the owner on 2026-11-04 (chat)"):

> - **L4: wie vorgeschlagen, plus eine Backlog-Zeile.** Der erfasste `interestPeriod` an der Klassifikation macht das Dezember-Beispiel abbildbar und ist verhältnismäßig, weil deutsche Annuitätendarlehen fast immer monatlich zahlen. Der dauerhaft richtige Ort des Fakts ist aber das Zahlungsintervall in den Konditionen, denn ein jährlich zahlendes Darlehen hat heute auch einen falschen Plan und eine falsche Restschuld. Also neue Zeile `paymentIntervalMonths` an den Terms; sobald sie da ist, wird ein erfasster Zeitraum, der vom Plan abweicht, geflaggt.

So two things are decided: **the field** (`paymentIntervalMonths` on the terms, the lasting place of the fact) and **the flag** (once the field exists, a recorded `interestPeriod` that deviates from the plan is flagged). Everything else below (the values, the derivation, the flag's name and level, the precedence of the plan over the recorded period, the first payment's reconciliation with the real bookings, the migration) is this section's proposal and open to the owner (open questions 1–12). The name of the field is the owner's; data-model §21's `paymentFrequency` (an enum, "fixed to `MONTHLY`" by P3-D2) is not used.

### As the code stands (main 10709ad; paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`)

- **The terms have no interval:** `LoanTermsData` (`domains/financing/terms.ts:23-37`) has no such field; the module's doc states "monthly payments from `firstPaymentDate`" (`:5-10`). The create body is strict (`api/loan-terms.ts:32-45`), so `paymentFrequency` and any other key are `400` (pinned by `api/loan-terms.test.ts:151` and `api/loans.test.ts:160`). The response (`api/loan-terms.ts:266-286`), the `CREATED` AuditRecord's metadata (`infrastructure/postgres/loan-terms-repository.ts:135-149`) and the idempotency fingerprint (`terms.ts:308-322`) carry no interval.
- **The schedule is monthly:** `walkSchedule` (`terms.ts:116-149`) takes `addMonths(period.firstPaymentDate, k)` for k = 0, 1, 2, … (`:129`), stops at the next `VALID` period's `validFrom`, after `maturityDate`, at a balance of 0 and at `MAX_PAYMENTS = 600` entries in all (`:93-94`, `:128`), and charges `monthlyInterest(balance, rate)` = `round_half_up(balance × rate / 100 / 12)` (`:75-80`, `:131`). `addMonths` counts from the original date and clamps to the month's last day (`shared/business-date.ts:43-58`). The annuity check 7 of §41.2 compares `scheduledPayment` with one month's interest (`terms.ts:348-353`).
- **Everything else reads that one schedule:** the planned remaining debt `plannedBalanceOn` (`terms.ts:274-285`) and `debtOn` (`domains/financing/debt.ts:67-86`); `fixedRateEnd` (`terms.ts:222-232`); the cut at a closing `closedSchedule`/`loanSchedule` (`terms.ts:238-263`); the payment proposal's `nearestEntry` (`domains/financing/payment-proposal.ts:46-57`); the 10-day rule's timing (`infrastructure/postgres/tax-source-facts.ts:243-258`); §58L's period facts (`infrastructure/postgres/loan-interest-periods.ts:14-23`, used by the view, §58G's `partOn`, §58I Part 2 and §59E); §58E's `LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`/`_VOIDED` and §58H's `LOAN_CLOSED` year changes (`domains/taxation/attribution-history.ts:204-208`, `:240-246`). Every one of them reads the terms through `periodsOf`/`toTerms` (`loan-terms-repository.ts:279-291`, `:300`), so one new column reaches them all.
- **The interest period of an entry:** `interestTiming` (`domains/taxation/cash-timing.ts:117-141`) takes the entry nearest to the booking date and the period from the day after the previous entry to its payment date; **the first entry's period is one month long** (`addMonths(due, -1)`, `:131`). §58L's `interestPeriodOf` (`domains/taxation/loan-interest-periods.ts:44-56`) clips it at `debtFrom`.
- **So a non-monthly Loan is wrong in three places today:** its plan has a payment every month (twelve where the lender debits four or one), its planned remaining debt falls monthly, and its interest periods are one month long, so an annual or quarterly interest is distributed by the last month's sets (§58L Example 2). VC-X-40's recorded `interestPeriod` on the classification (`tax_classification.interest_period_from`/`_until`, migration 0069) repairs the third for one split at a time; nothing compares it with the plan.
- **The database:** `loan_terms` (`infrastructure/postgres/migrations/0025_loan_terms.ts:20-45`) with `loan_terms_append` (`:52-88`) and `loan_terms_frozen` (`:89-126`), whose `IS DISTINCT FROM` lists every data column by name (`:97-103`), so a new column is not frozen until that list names it.
- **The flags:** §58L's `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` (`domains/taxation/tax-year-loan-interest.ts:154-157`; its level `domains/taxation/tax-year-review.ts:91-92`) is the only flag about the interest period; no flag reads the recorded period.

### The rule

1. **The field.** Each terms period has `paymentIntervalMonths`, an integer in **{1, 3, 6, 12}** (monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, yearly; open question 1): the months between two planned payments of that period. **Default 1**: a create without the key is a monthly period, exactly as today; every existing period is 1 (the column's default, no backfill, no AuditRecord).
2. **Payment dates** (§41.4): a period's k-th payment falls on `addMonths(firstPaymentDate, k × paymentIntervalMonths)`, k = 0, 1, 2, …, always counted from `firstPaymentDate` and clamped to the month's last day (open question 2: the anchor is `firstPaymentDate`, not the calendar). Quarterly from 2027-01-31: 2027-04-30, 2027-07-31, 2027-10-31, 2028-01-31; quarterly from 2027-11-30: 2028-02-29, 2028-05-30, 2028-08-30; half-yearly from 2027-08-31: 2028-02-29, 2028-08-31; yearly from 2028-02-29: 2029-02-28, 2030-02-28, 2031-02-28, 2032-02-29. With 1 this is today's formula.
3. **Where a period's payments stop:** unchanged (before the next `VALID` period's `validFrom`, never after `maturityDate`, once the balance is 0), and **the cap is 50 years of intervals**: the plan ends with `PAYMENT_CAP` once the sum of the entries' intervals reaches 600 months (600 monthly, 200 quarterly, 100 half-yearly, 50 yearly payments; open question 9). With 1 this is today's 600 payments.
4. **Interest per entry:** `round_half_up(balanceBefore × rate × paymentIntervalMonths / 100 / 12)` to the cent, the same 30/360 convention, in integer arithmetic (`monthlyInterest` becomes `periodInterest(balance, rate, months)`; with 1 the same function). **Every entry charges its full interval**, the first entry of a period too, as today's first monthly entry charges a full month whatever the days since `debtFrom` or `validFrom` (open question 3).
5. **Principal, payment, balance:** unchanged formulas per entry (`ANNUITY`: `min(scheduledPayment − interest, balanceBefore)`; `INTEREST_ONLY`: 0). `scheduledPayment` is the payment **per interval**, as on the contract (a quarterly rate of 1 800.00 is entered as 1 800.00).
6. **The annuity check** (§41.2 check 7): `scheduledPayment` must exceed the first entry's interest **over the period's interval** (rule 4); `details.firstInterest` is that amount. With 1, unchanged.
7. **Successive terms** may have different intervals (an Anschlussfinanzierung may change it; open question 4). Each period's entries follow its own interval from its own `firstPaymentDate`; the balance carries over as today.
8. **The interest period of an entry** (§58A's `economicPeriod`, §58L rule 1): from the day after the previous entry of the plan (whatever its period) to the entry's payment date, as today; **the first entry of the plan runs from `addMonths(paymentDate, −paymentIntervalMonths)` + 1 day**, the interval of its own period instead of one month (`cash-timing.ts:131`), clipped at `debtFrom` by §58L rule 1 as today. So the entry's period and its interest (rule 4) are the same interval, except for a first entry after `debtFrom` or a follow-up period starting off the previous rhythm (open question 3).
9. **A closing** (§41.7): unchanged: entries after `closingDate` are omitted, `endReason = CLOSED` when one was. A closing inside an interval leaves the days from the last kept entry to the closing without an entry, as today a closing inside a month does (open question 5).

### The first payment: the simple rule plus reconciliation with the real bookings (open question 12; issue #121, case A)

Open question 12 by the owner's request („Ja, 25.09. war die Auszahlung, nimm es als Frage 12 auf“; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05, for its place as question 12 of this section only; its content is open). It comes from the real-data run's finding F9 (`docs/development/real-data-run.md`, step 2; #121), which the first real debit answered (amounts stay out of this document):

- the total debit equals the planned payment (the annuity is fixed);
- the lender charged interest for **36 days** by 30/360 (exactly 1.2 times one month's interest), from the payout to the end of the first payment's period, and the **principal share is reduced by the difference**: #121's **case A** (Teilzinsen inside the first payment), not a separate debit;
- so the plan (§41.4, rule 4 above: a full interval on the first entry) overstates the first principal share; every later balance, the planned remaining debt and `summary.fixedRateEnd` deviate by that difference (growing by its interest); and §58L's interest period of the first payment is payout – end of the first period, not one month.

**The owner's direction for question 12** (chat, 2026-11-05; quoted as direction, the substance stays open question 12): „Warum machen wir es nicht so, dass die einfach Regel gilt und dann die Daten immer mit dem echten Upload abgeglichen und bei Abweichungen auf die Echtwelt Daten korrigiert werden“ (and, asked whether question 12 is to be rewritten accordingly: „Ja“).

**What the code does today** (main 10709ad; checked for this rewrite):

- **The schedule never looks at the ledger.** `walkSchedule` starts from `principalOriginal` (`domains/financing/terms.ts:122`) and only a terms period's `principalAtStart` restarts the balance (`:125`); its inputs are the Loan and its terms (`application/loan-terms.ts:143`, `loanSchedule(inputs.loan, inputs.periods)`). So the plan is computed from the contract start for its whole length, whatever was booked.
- **The planned remaining debt is the contract plan too:** `debtOn`'s `planned` is `plannedBalanceOn(principalOriginal, maturityDate, periods, d + 1)` (`domains/financing/debt.ts:84`), again from the contract start (`terms.ts:274-285`); `summary.fixedRateEnd` the same (`terms.ts:222-232`). Only **`actual`** reads the ledger: `principalOriginal` − the counted `LOAN_PRINCIPAL` splits up to `d` (`debt.ts:46-59`, `:74`, `:80`), and `difference = actual − planned` is therefore **cumulative**: one stub difference, special repayment or missed payment stays in every later `difference`, and every later planned row keeps the contract's balance.
- **The payment proposal takes the plan's split:** `proposePayment` (`domains/financing/payment-proposal.ts:62-78`) proposes `min(entry.interest, amount)` as interest and the rest as principal for the nearest entry (`:66-71`); the only deviation it states is `AMOUNT_DIFFERS_FROM_SCHEDULE` for the total (`:73`). It reads no purpose text: `ProposalTransaction` has no description (`:11-20`), although the Transaction has one (`ledger_transaction.description`, `infrastructure/postgres/schema.ts:573`; the rent suggestion already reads months from it, `domains/rent-reconciliation/suggestion.ts:97`).
- **Tax figures use only booked splits:** the tax-year view's Loan interest is the counted `LOAN_INTEREST` splits (`infrastructure/postgres/tax-year-reads.ts:239-281`, the category filter `:260`); the plan contributes **dates only** (§58A's due date through `interestTiming`, `tax-source-facts.ts:243-258`; §58L's interest period, `loan-interest-periods.ts:14-23`), never an amount. Principal is no tax figure.

**Proposal** (open question 12): **the simple rule stays** (rule 4: a full interval on every entry, the first one too; no new terms field), **and the plan is reconciled with the real bookings**:

- **(a) The split from the bank's purpose text.** The payment proposal (§41.5) reads the Transaction's purpose text (`description`) and, where it states the split, proposes **that** split: the BBBank form `RECHN.ZINS <interest> TILG./ENTG. <principal> TILGUNG PER <date>` (`<interest>`, `<principal>` German amounts such as `1.234,56`; `<date>` `DD.MM.YYYY`; spaces between the tokens tolerant, case as the bank writes it). The parsed split is used only when `<interest> + <principal>` equals the debit's amount exactly; otherwise, and for any other text or bank format, **no parsed proposal**: the plan's split as today (the fallback), with the flag `PURPOSE_SPLIT_NOT_MATCHING` (informative) only when the pattern was found but did not add up. The plan's split is always computed beside it as the counter-check: the response gains `source` (`PURPOSE_TEXT` | `SCHEDULE`) and `scheduleSplit: { interest, principal }`, and a parsed split that differs from the plan's carries `SPLIT_DIFFERS_FROM_SCHEDULE` (informative, with both splits). The pattern is code (one parser per bank format, versioned by its name, e.g. `BBBANK_LOAN_DEBIT`); other formats are added when real data shows them. A person still confirms the splits (§41.5; DE never writes splits on its own, ADR-015).
- **(b) The plan re-anchored on the actual remaining debt ("rebased").** The schedule (§41.4) and the planned remaining debt (§41.6) read the Loan's counted splits (§41.5's counting rule, in the same snapshot). The **last booked payment** is the latest booking date of a counted split of the Loan. A regular debit (one with a `LOAN_INTEREST` split) is matched to its nearest entry (§41.5's `nearestEntry`) and counts as that entry paid; a principal-only payment (a special repayment) matches no entry. **The rebase starts with the first entry after the matched entry, or, for a principal-only payment, with the first entry after its booking date**: that entry and every later one are computed from the actual remaining debt on the last booked payment's date (§41.6's `actual`), with the same rules (rule 4, the annuity, the interval, the stops); every earlier entry stays the contract's plan. So a stub difference, a special repayment or a missed principal changes the following rows once and does not propagate as a difference: `planned` and `difference` (§41.6) and `summary.fixedRateEnd` read the rebased plan. The contract plan stays visible beside it: the schedule's response gains `rebasedOn: { bookingDate, entryNumber, actualBalance }` (or `null` without a booked payment, then the plan is exactly today's), and the remaining-debt read gains `plannedAsContracted` and `differenceAsContracted` (today's `planned` and `difference`, cumulative). **Taxation keeps reading the plan as contracted** (its payment dates; `loanSchedule` unchanged for `tax-source-facts.ts`, `loan-interest-periods.ts`, `attribution-history.ts`), so a rebase that ends a plan earlier (after a special repayment) moves no due date and no interest period, and no tax figure changes.
- **(c) A deviation flagged once, on its payment.** Where a booked payment's split differs from its matched entry's (interest or principal; the total is `AMOUNT_DIFFERS_FROM_SCHEDULE`'s, unchanged), the schedule's entry carries `BOOKED_SPLIT_DIFFERS_FROM_PLAN` with `{ transactionId, booked: { interest, principal }, planned: { interest, principal } }`, **informative**: it changes no tax figure (the booked splits are what counts, above) and no later entry repeats it, since the rows after it are rebased. It is shown in the schedule's items and in the remaining-debt read's `rebasedOn`; not in the tax-year view.
- **§58L's first interest period** (payout to the end of the first period) is **not** derived: it matters only when an allocation set changes inside that stub, and then the recorded `interestPeriod` of VC-X-40 (the fallback of "Precedence of the plan and the recorded `interestPeriod`" above) states it, flagged by `INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE` as any deviation (open where the parts differ).
- **No migration** for question 12 under this proposal (the parser and the rebase are code; the purpose text and the splits exist).
- **Unchanged for a Loan without a booked payment, or booked exactly as planned:** the rebased plan equals the contract plan cent for cent, so ACC7 and ACC8 (no terms or monthly terms; tax figures from splits) stay unchanged. **Changed by design:** `planned`, `difference` and `fixedRateEnd` of a Loan whose bookings deviated from the plan (e.g. §41.6's tests of a special repayment, which then assert `differenceAsContracted` for the cumulative figure).

**Example (synthetic).** Loan F: `principalOriginal` 120 000.00, paid out (`disbursementDate`) 2027-04-25, one `ANNUITY` period from 2027-04-25 at `"3.000"`, `scheduledPayment` 600.00, `firstPaymentDate` 2027-05-31, monthly. The plan's first entry: 300.00 / 300.00 / 119 700.00. The bank debits 600.00 on 2027-05-31 with the purpose text `RECHN.ZINS 360,00 TILG./ENTG. 240,00 TILGUNG PER 31.05.2027` (36 days of interest, synthetic figures).

- **(a)** The proposal: `source = PURPOSE_TEXT`, interest **360.00**, principal **240.00** (360.00 + 240.00 = 600.00, the debit); `scheduleSplit` 300.00 / 300.00; `SPLIT_DIFFERS_FROM_SCHEDULE`. With the text `RECHN.ZINS 360,00 TILG./ENTG. 250,00 TILGUNG PER 31.05.2027` (610.00 ≠ 600.00): no parsed proposal, the plan's 300.00 / 300.00 with `PURPOSE_SPLIT_NOT_MATCHING`. With another bank's text: the plan's split, no flag.
- **(b)** Once the splits 360.00 / 240.00 are confirmed: `actual` 119 760.00; `rebasedOn` { 2027-05-31, entry 1, 119 760.00 }; the next entries from it: 2027-06-30 **299.40 / 300.60 / 119 459.40**, 2027-07-31 **298.65 / 301.35 / 119 158.05** (the contract plan: 299.25 / 300.75 / 119 399.25 and 298.50 / 301.50 / 119 097.75). On 2027-06-15: `planned` 119 760.00, `difference` **0.00**; `plannedAsContracted` 119 700.00, `differenceAsContracted` **+60.00**.
- **(c)** Entry 1 carries `BOOKED_SPLIT_DIFFERS_FROM_PLAN` (booked 360.00 / 240.00, planned 300.00 / 300.00), informative; entry 2, booked as rebased (299.40 / 300.60), carries none.
- **After a special repayment** (Loan M of the example below: entry 1 on 2027-01-31 booked as planned, then a principal-only `LOAN_PRINCIPAL` split of 5 000.00 booked 2027-02-15): `actual` 114 700.00; the special repayment matches no entry (it would otherwise be nearest to entry 2, 13 days against 15, and swallow it), so the rebase starts with entry 2, the first after 2027-02-15: entry 2 (2027-02-28) **286.75 / 313.25 / 114 386.75**, entry 3 285.97 (285.966875) / 314.03 / 114 072.72 (the contract plan: 299.25 / 300.75 / 119 399.25). On 2027-02-20: `planned` 114 700.00, `difference` 0.00; `differenceAsContracted` −5 000.00.
- **The tax-year view:** the 2027-05-31 debit's interest is 360.00 by its split (as today); its §58L period is the plan's 2027-05-01 – 2027-05-31 unless a recorded `interestPeriod` states 2027-04-25 – 2027-05-31.

**Alternative (a) of question 12, kept from the earlier versions of this section: `firstInterestFrom` on the terms** (with its figures; under this alternative in the same migration as `paymentIntervalMonths`):

- **The field:** `firstInterestFrom` (business date, optional, `null` by default) on a terms period: the day interest starts to accrue for the first entry. Only on a Loan's **first** terms period (`422 FIRST_INTEREST_FROM_NOT_ON_FIRST_TERMS` otherwise, the mirror of `PRINCIPAL_AT_START_ON_FIRST_TERMS`); not before the Loan's `debtFrom` (`422 FIRST_INTEREST_BEFORE_DEBT` with `details.debtFrom`); **not after the first entry's period start** `addMonths(firstPaymentDate, −paymentIntervalMonths) + 1 day` (`400 AFTER_PERIOD_START`).
- **The first entry's interest** (review round 1 on #272: equality with rule 4 by construction): rule 4's full interval **plus the extra days before the period start**, in one rounding: `round_half_up(balanceBefore × rate × (n × 30 + extraDays) / 100 / 360)` to the cent, where `periodStart = addMonths(firstPaymentDate, −n) + 1 day` and `extraDays = days30/360(firstInterestFrom − 1 day, periodStart − 1 day)`, the days from `firstInterestFrom` up to and including the day before the period start. `days30/360(a, b) = (Y2 − Y1) × 360 + (M2 − M1) × 30 + (D2 − D1)`, D1 = 31 → 30, D2 = 31 → 30 only when D1 ≥ 30 (the 30/360 "bond basis"). Since `n × 30 / 360 = n / 12`, **`firstInterestFrom` = `periodStart` gives `extraDays` = 0 and exactly rule 4's interest for every month and quarter** (a period start on 30 March, 1 March, 1 April, a due date on the 29th, February or a quarter ending in June alike). The real case (a payout on the 25th of a 30-day month, the period starting on the 1st of the next month): `extraDays` = 30 − 24 = 6, 30 + 6 = **36**, the lender's figure. (A plain bond count from `firstInterestFrom` to the payment date would not reduce to rule 4: a period start of 1 April with the payment on 29 April counts 28, not 30.)
- **Annuity unchanged:** `scheduledPayment` stays the payment; `principal = min(scheduledPayment − interest, balanceBefore)`, so the stub's extra interest lowers the first principal share and every later balance follows. `INTEREST_ONLY`: the first payment is the stub's interest. Check 7 (§41.2) compares `scheduledPayment` with this first interest.
- **§58L / §58A:** the first entry's interest period starts at `firstInterestFrom` (rule 8 above; the clip at `debtFrom` then changes nothing). The 10-day rule's `economicPeriod` of that entry is the same period (one function); its due date is unchanged.
- **`null`:** today's behaviour (rule 4 and rule 8 above), byte for byte; every existing period is `null` (no backfill), so ACC7 and ACC8 are unchanged.
- **API, database:** the create body gains `firstInterestFrom` (optional), the response gains it (`null`), the AuditRecord's metadata and the fingerprint only when not `null`; in **the same migration** as `paymentIntervalMonths`: `first_interest_from date NULL`, CHECK `first_interest_from IS NULL OR first_interest_from <= first_payment_date`, `loan_terms_append` refusing it on a period that is not the Loan's first `VALID` one and before `debtFrom`, `loan_terms_frozen` with the column in its list, `down` refusing while a value is stated.

**Its example (synthetic; recomputed in review round 1 on #272).** Loan F: `principalOriginal` 120 000.00, paid out (`disbursementDate`) **2027-04-25**, one `ANNUITY` period from 2027-04-25 at `"3.000"`, `scheduledPayment` 600.00, `firstPaymentDate` 2027-05-31, monthly. The first entry's period starts 2027-05-01; `firstInterestFrom` 2027-04-25 gives `extraDays` = days30/360(2027-04-24, 2027-04-30) = **6**, so 30 + 6 = **36 days**.

| # | paymentDate | `firstInterestFrom` `null` (today): interest / principal / balanceAfter | `firstInterestFrom` 2027-04-25: interest / principal / balanceAfter |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2027-05-31 | 300.00 / 300.00 / 119 700.00 | **360.00** (120 000.00 × 3 % × 36/360, 1.2 × 300.00) / **240.00** / **119 760.00** |
| 2 | 2027-06-30 | 299.25 / 300.75 / 119 399.25 | 299.40 / 300.60 / 119 459.40 |
| 3 | 2027-07-31 | 298.50 / 301.50 / 119 097.75 | 298.65 / 301.35 / 119 158.05 |

- The payment is 600.00 in both; the balances differ by 60.00, 60.15, 60.30, …; `planned` (§41.6) and `fixedRateEnd` follow the right column.
- The figures are those of the first version of this example; only the dates moved (from a February payout to an April one), since the new count gives 36 days only for a 30-day month.
- §58L: the debit of 2027-05-31 has the interest period **2027-04-25 – 2027-05-31** (37 calendar days, §58L rule 2 counts calendar days; the extra days are 30/360 only for the interest) instead of 2027-05-01 – 2027-05-31.
- **February variant** (paid out and `firstInterestFrom` 2027-02-25, `firstPaymentDate` 2027-03-31, period start 2027-03-01): `extraDays` = days30/360(2027-02-24, 2027-02-28) = **4**, 34 days: interest **340.00**, principal **260.00**, balance **119 740.00** (the plain bond count from 2027-02-25 to 2027-03-31 would give 36 and 360.00; open question 12 names the choice).
- **With interval 3** (Loan F quarterly, `scheduledPayment` 1 800.00, `firstPaymentDate` 2027-03-31, period start 2027-01-01, paid out and `firstInterestFrom` **2026-12-25**): `extraDays` = days30/360(2026-12-24, 2026-12-31) = **7** (D2 = 31 stays, D1 = 24 < 30), 90 + 7 = **97 days**: interest **970.00**, principal **830.00**, balance **119 170.00**; the second entry (2027-06-30) 893.78 (893.775) / 906.22 / 118 263.78; the first interest period 2026-12-25 – 2027-03-31. (The first version had 96 days and 960.00 by the plain count.)

### Effects

- **Schedule (§41.4):** the entries and the summary follow rules 2–5; `number`, the window and `endReason` work as today. `fixedRateEnd` reads the planned balance as today, so it follows the interval.
- **Remaining debt (§41.6):** `planned` is the balance after the last entry on or before `d` (unchanged definition): for a quarterly Loan it steps once a quarter, so a Loan the lender debits quarterly no longer shows a positive `difference` in the months between. `actual`, `difference`, the per-property distribution (largest remainder, ties by `propertyReferenceId`) and `LOAN_NOT_ALLOCATED` are unchanged. `MATURITY` and `PAYMENT_CAP` keep their meaning.
- **Payment proposal (§41.5):** proposes from the nearest entry of the interval's plan; its interest is the interval's (rule 4). Refusals unchanged.
- **Payments read (§41.6):** unchanged (by the booking date, from the ledger).
- **Closings (§41.7):** the cut is unchanged; `settledAmount`, `SPLITS_AFTER_CLOSING` and `REMAINING_DEBT_NOT_ZERO` read the ledger and are unchanged. The schedule's `balanceDue` after a cut is the omitted entry's `balanceBefore`, as today.
- **§58A's 10-day rule:** the due date of a Loan interest split is the nearest entry of the interval's plan (source `LOAN_SCHEDULE`, unchanged); its window, its "payment and due date in the window" test (§58F) and `DE_CASH_TIMING@1` are unchanged (open question 8). A split's year can move only where the nearest entry of the interval's plan differs from the monthly one's, e.g. a quarterly Loan due on the 5th of February, May, August and November (`firstPaymentDate` 2027-02-05) with a debit booked 2028-01-03: the same terms without the interval (monthly from 2027-02-05), whose nearest entry 2028-01-05 lies in the window (2027 by the 10-day rule), the quarterly plan's nearest entry 2028-02-05 (33 days, against 59 to 2027-11-05) does not (2028, the booking year). Such a move is caused by a `LoanTerms` record and is flagged as today by §58E's year kinds `LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`/`_VOIDED` (`attribution-history.ts:204-208`, which reads the same `loanSchedule`).
- **§58L's interest periods:** rule 8 above makes the schedule's period the interval, so a quarterly or yearly Loan's interest is distributed over the quarter or the year by the sets valid on each day, **without a recorded `interestPeriod`** (§58L Example 2 with `paymentIntervalMonths = 12` and `firstPaymentDate` 2026-12-31, entries 2026-12-31, 2027-12-31, …: the debit of 2027-12-30 is nearest to 2027-12-31, its period 2027-01-01 – 2027-12-31, P1 2,730.00, P2 920.00, as with the recorded period). A recorded period still wins (§58L rule 1).
- **§59E's capitalised interest** reads the same period (`loanPeriodFactsOf`): a quarterly construction-period interest spanning a set change now meets `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS` where a monthly period did not; the rule is unchanged.
- **The new flag** (below) is the only new code in the tax-year view.

### The deviation flag (the owner's decision; its form open questions 6 and 7)

- **Name:** `INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE`, an **item flag** on the Loan interest item of a split whose current classification records an `interestPeriod` (VC-X-40) **and** whose Loan has a schedule (at least one entry, so not §58L rule 8).
- **When:** the recorded `{ from, until }` differs from the schedule's period of the split (rule 8 above: `interestTiming` over the interval's plan, nearest entry to the booking date, clipped at `debtFrom`) in either end. Equal periods raise nothing; under open question 5's proposal a recorded period from the day after a `CLOSED` Loan's last kept entry to its `closingDate` counts as equal. A Loan without terms has no plan to deviate from (no flag; rule 8 of §58L does not apply either, the recorded period wins).
- **Level (open question 6, proposal): open when the deviation matters, informative otherwise.** The view distributes the split once by the recorded period (as today) and once by the schedule's (§58L rules 2–5); **open** when the two give different parts for some PropertyReference (or one is covered and the other not), **informative** when every part is the same (e.g. a recorded 2027-04-02 – 2027-07-01 against the schedule's 2027-04-01 – 2027-06-30, both in one set). The level is the same in every view, since it compares the whole distribution. An open flag makes the year not final (§58C's rule for `final`); it clears when the terms state the right interval (a new or re-entered terms period, §41.2) or the classification is superseded by one with a matching or no `interestPeriod`; there is no acknowledgement for it.
- **`details`:** `{ loanId, recorded: { from, until }, schedule: { from, until }, termsId, paymentIntervalMonths, partsDiffer }` (`termsId` and `paymentIntervalMonths` of the period of the nearest entry; `partsDiffer` decides the level, as `validAllocationSets` does for `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN`, `tax-year-review.ts:91-92`).
- **Where it shows:** on the item in the PropertyReference and owner views of every PropertyReference the split is attributed to, counted in the year's `review` like every item flag; on a not attributed entry (§58L rule 3) it is listed informative (the year is open by `LOAN_INTEREST_NOT_ATTRIBUTED` anyway, as VC-X-40's deviation (d) keeps `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` off such entries). Not in Financing's reads (the plan is Financing's, the classification is Taxation's).
- **Not a change flag:** it is no `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED` or `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` kind; it appears and disappears with the inputs, like `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN`.
- **After the deployment** every recorded `interestPeriod` on a Loan whose terms keep the default 1 is compared with a monthly plan, so a recorded quarter or year is flagged at once (open question 7, proposal: as the owner's decision says, no exemption). No year is productively filed yet, so this is a release note, not a deployment flag (as §58L open question 2).

### Precedence of the plan and the recorded `interestPeriod` (open question 11)

Owner's context of 2026-11-05 (chat; context, not a decision on the open questions): the interval on the terms is the lasting place of the fact; once it exists, the plan itself gives the interest period, and VC-X-40's recorded `interestPeriod` per split (§58L L4, migration 0069) shrinks to the fallback for "interval missing / plan does not match" or becomes secondary. L4 itself (the recorded period wins over the schedule's for the allocation) is a decision of 2026-11-04; changing its precedence is an amendment the owner makes with open question 11.

- **Primary source: the plan with its interval.** For a Loan with a schedule (at least one `VALID` terms period), the interest period of a split is the schedule's (rule 8 above, §58L rule 1's `interestTiming` clipped at `debtFrom`). Entering the right interval on the terms is the intended way to get a quarterly or yearly period; the release note and the flag point there.
- **The recorded `interestPeriod` only where** (proposal, open question 11):
  1. the Loan has **no schedule** (no `VALID` terms; §58L rule 8 would otherwise apply): the recorded period is the only source, and no flag is raised (there is no plan to deviate from);
  2. the recorded period **deviates from the plan**: it stays in effect for the allocation (L4 unchanged in effect), and the split carries `INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE` (open where the parts differ). So the deviation is never silent, and it is resolved by putting the interval on the terms or superseding the classification;
  3. the recorded period **equals the plan's**: it changes nothing (the same parts), no flag; it is redundant and may stay.
- **The 10-day rule** never reads the recorded period (L4, unchanged); it reads the plan's due date.
- **Existing recorded periods** (0069's `tax_classification.interest_period_from`/`_until`) are **kept as they are**: no migration touches, moves or deletes them (0069's frozen guard stays), no AuditRecord is written for them. From the deployment on, each is compared with its Loan's plan and flagged when it deviates (open question 7: also on Loans still at interval 1). A person resolves a flag by entering the interval on the terms (the recorded period then equals the plan and the flag disappears) or by superseding the classification without `interestPeriod`.
- **New recorded periods:** `POST /tax-classifications` keeps accepting `interestPeriod` (VC-X-40's checks unchanged) under the proposal; under alternative (b) of open question 11 it is refused on a split whose Loan has a schedule.
- **In the view:** `loanAllocation.interestPeriod.source` stays `LOAN_SCHEDULE` or `CLASSIFICATION` (VC-X-40's values); with the proposal, `CLASSIFICATION` appears only in cases 1 and 2 above (in case 3 the source reads `LOAN_SCHEDULE`, the recorded period being redundant), so a `CLASSIFICATION` source on a Loan with a schedule always comes with the flag.

### API

- **`POST /api/v1/loans/{loanId}/terms`** (§41.2): the body gains `paymentIntervalMonths` (optional, a JSON integer in {1, 3, 6, 12}, default 1). A string, a fraction or `null` → `400 INVALID_FORMAT`; another integer → `400 OUT_OF_RANGE`. `paymentFrequency` stays an unknown key (`400`). Its place in the order of checks is step 1 (`400`); check 7 uses it (rule 6).
- **Idempotency (§15):** the fingerprint gains the interval **only when it is not 1**, so a key stored before the deployment replays (an omitted key and an explicit 1 are the same request).
- **AuditRecord `CREATED`** on `LoanTerms`: the metadata gains `paymentIntervalMonths` (always, from the deployment on); readers treat its absence in older records as 1.
- **`POST …/terms/{termsId}/void`:** unchanged (no body change; a period is never edited, so the interval of a wrong period is corrected by void and re-append while it is the last one, P3-D2).
- **Responses (additive):** every terms period (`POST`, `GET …/terms`, the void's `200`) gains `paymentIntervalMonths` (integer, never `null`). The schedule's items and summary, the remaining debt and the proposal keep their shapes (their figures follow the rule). The tax-year view gains only the new flag code.
- **No route changes;** `docs/development/api-inventory.md` unchanged (`yarn api:inventory:check`).

### Migration (the next free number at implementation; 0070 at the time of writing)

- `ALTER TABLE loan_terms ADD COLUMN payment_interval_months smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`, with `CONSTRAINT loan_terms_payment_interval CHECK (payment_interval_months IN (1, 3, 6, 12))`. Existing rows read 1 (a constant default; no `UPDATE`, so `loan_terms_frozen` does not fire and writes no version, and no AuditRecord is written: **no backfill**).
- **Frozen:** `loan_terms_frozen` is replaced (`CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`) with `payment_interval_months` added to both rows of its `IS DISTINCT FROM` (`0025_loan_terms.ts:97-103`); everything else of 0025's function stays word for word (the Loan write, `TERMS_NOT_LAST`, the `VALID` → `VOID` step with `version` + 1, never deleted).
- **`loan_terms_append`:** unchanged (the CHECK covers the values; the append rules do not read the interval).
- **`first_interest_from`** only under open question 12's alternative (a): in this migration as well, as described under "The first payment" (the column, its CHECK, the append rule, the frozen list, `down`). Open question 12's proposal needs no migration.
- **Not in the database:** the annuity check (needs the derivation, as today), the `400` codes, the flag (derived on read).
- **`down`:** refuses (`RAISE EXCEPTION`, naming the first such terms id) while any row has `payment_interval_months <> 1`, since dropping it would turn a quarterly plan silently monthly; otherwise restores 0025's `loan_terms_frozen` verbatim and drops the column (and with it the CHECK). The down tests of earlier migrations that run later `down`s first run this one first too.

### Interaction with VC-X-54 and the change flags (§58E, §58G, §58H)

- **Setting the interval on an existing Loan** is a terms record: void the last period and append it again with the interval (P3-D2), or append a follow-up period. Both are `LoanTerms` AuditRecords (`CREATED`/`VOIDED`).
- **A year that moves** by such a record (the 10-day case above) is flagged as today: `LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`/`_VOIDED` are §58E's year kinds (0064, 0065) and read the schedule through `loanSchedule`, which then carries the interval.
- **A part that moves** (Loan Q's March debit: P1 450.00 → 745.00, P2 450.00 → 155.00 when the interval is entered after 2027's end) is **not flagged** until VC-X-54 makes terms records `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` kinds (**done: VC-X-54, §58P, migration 0071; flagged as `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED` from then on, the pin inverted**); VC-X-40's pinning test ("a `LoanTerms` record after the year's end can move a part without a flag") stays, and VC-X-53 adds the interval case to it. Today's §58L already has the same gap for `firstPaymentDate` and terms changes; the interval makes it more frequent, since entering it on an existing non-monthly Loan is the expected step (open question 10).
- **The deviation flag** itself is no change kind (above); it may appear or disappear with such a record, which is visible in `review`, not acknowledged.
- **§58G, §58I Part 2, §59E:** follow the period through the one shared function (`distributeOverPeriod`, `loanPeriodFactsOf`); no rule of theirs changes.

### Release note (proposal; the release note as implemented is under "As implemented (VC-X-53)")

*From VC-X-53 on, a Loan's terms period states its payment interval (`paymentIntervalMonths`: 1, 3, 6 or 12; default 1). Every existing period is monthly, as before, and every figure of a monthly Loan is unchanged. For a Loan entered with another interval, the schedule pays every 3, 6 or 12 months with that interval's interest, the planned remaining debt steps accordingly, and the tax-year view distributes each interest debit over the whole quarter, half-year or year by the allocation sets valid on each day, without a recorded interest period. To correct an existing non-monthly Loan, void its last terms period and enter it again with the interval, or append a follow-up period; a year it moves is flagged as before (`LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`/`_VOIDED`), a part it moves is not yet (VC-X-54; flagged from VC-X-54 on, §58P). A recorded interest period on a classification that differs from the Loan's plan is now flagged (`INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE`), open where it changes a PropertyReference's part, so recorded quarters and years on Loans still entered as monthly show up at once. With open question 12's proposal, the payment proposal takes the interest and principal from the bank's purpose text where it states them (BBBank's form), and the schedule and the planned remaining debt are re-anchored on the actual remaining debt after the last booked payment, so a first payment with pro-rata interest (Teilzinsen) or a special repayment no longer leaves a lasting difference; the contract plan's figures stay visible as `plannedAsContracted`; a split that differs from the plan is flagged once, informative. No year is productively filed yet, so the deployment raises no change flag.*

### Open questions (decided)

**Decided by the owner on 2026-11-05 (chat), verbatim** (cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05“):

> - **1: wie vorgeschlagen** ({1, 3, 6, 12}).
> - **2: wie vorgeschlagen** (Anker `firstPaymentDate`).
> - **3: wie vorgeschlagen** (voller Intervall auf jedem Eintrag, auch dem ersten).
> - **4: wie vorgeschlagen** (Intervallwechsel in Folgeperiode erlaubt).
> - **5: wie vorgeschlagen** (Schließung unverändert; erfasster Zeitraum bis `closingDate` gilt als planpassend).
> - **6: wie vorgeschlagen** (`INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE`, offen bei abweichenden Anteilen, informativ bei gleichen, keine Quittierung).
> - **7: wie vorgeschlagen** (ab Deployment geflaggt).
> - **8: wie vorgeschlagen**, Ergänzung: die Beraterfrage zu „regelmäßig wiederkehrend“ bei Intervall über 1 jetzt in `beratungsfragen.md` §3 aufnehmen; bis zur Antwort gilt der Posten als unbestätigt.
> - **9: wie vorgeschlagen** (600 Monate).
> - **10: wie vorgeschlagen** (VC-X-53 allein, VC-X-54 danach).
> - **11: wie vorgeschlagen** (Plan primär, erfasster Zeitraum als Fallback, gewinnt bei Abweichung mit Flag).
> - **12: wie vorgeschlagen** (einfache Regel plus Abgleich mit echten Buchungen, kein Terms-Feld, keine Migration), mit zwei Bedingungen:
>   1. Der Verwendungszweck-Parser ist ein benanntes Bankformat wie die CSV-Presets, kein fest verdrahteter Regex; unbekanntes Format liefert still den Planvorschlag; die Herkunft (`PURPOSE_TEXT`, `SCHEDULE`) steht in der Antwort.
>   2. Die Umbasierung ändert die Bedeutung von `planned` zu „Prognose ab letzter Buchung“; das steht in einem Satz in §41.6 und in der Invariant-Suite, `plannedAsContracted` ist der alte Wert. Kein ADR nötig.
>
> Damit ist #121 beantwortet: Fall A ist durch die erste echte Lastschrift belegt, DE gleicht ab statt zu modellieren; die Zeile im Real-Data-Run wird mit Verweis auf §58O Frage 12 geschlossen.

So every question below is decided as its proposal states, with the two additions: (8) the Steuerberater question on „regelmäßig wiederkehrend“ for intervals above 1 is in `docs/germany/beratungsfragen.md` §3, and until it is answered that case counts as unconfirmed; (12) the purpose-text parser is a named bank format like the CSV import's presets (an unknown format silently gives the plan's split, the answer carries `source`), and the rebase changes the meaning of `planned` to the forecast from the last booked payment (one sentence in §41.6 and in the invariant suite; `plannedAsContracted` is the former value; no ADR). The questions as they were put:

1. **The allowed values.** **Proposal:** {1, 3, 6, 12}: the intervals German loan contracts use (monatlich, vierteljährlich, halbjährlich, jährlich), each dividing the year, so every plan repeats on the same calendar months. **Alternatives:** (a) every divisor of 12 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12), for the rare two- or four-monthly contract; (b) any integer 1–12, with plans that drift through the calendar months.
2. **The anchor.** **Proposal:** `firstPaymentDate`, each payment `k × n` months after it (as today's monthly rule; a calendar-quarter Loan is one whose `firstPaymentDate` is a quarter's end). **Alternative:** calendar-anchored intervals (quarters ending in March, June, September, December, whatever `firstPaymentDate`), which needs a rule for a `firstPaymentDate` off that grid.
3. **The first entry and stubs.** (The plan's rule; how real stubs are reconciled is open question 12.) **Proposal:** every entry charges its full interval (rule 4), the first one of a period too, as today's first monthly entry charges a full month; the first entry's interest period is its interval clipped at `debtFrom` (rule 8). A lender's stub interest then differs from the plan by the stub, as today by a part month (the ledger is the truth). **Alternatives:** (a) for intervals above 1, the first entry's interest pro rata by 30/360 days since `debtFrom` or the previous entry (a monthly plan unchanged, but two rules); (b) for every interval, which changes today's monthly figures (refused by "unchanged behaviour").
4. **A different interval in a follow-up period.** **Proposal:** allowed (an Anschlussfinanzierung may change the rhythm); each period follows its own interval from its own `firstPaymentDate`, and the first entry after the change charges its full interval while its §58L period runs from the day after the previous entry. **Alternatives:** (a) refused (`422 PAYMENT_INTERVAL_CHANGED`) until stubs are decided; (b) allowed only with `principalAtStart` (the follow-up contract restating the balance).
5. **A closing inside an interval.** **Proposal:** unchanged (§41.7: the entries after `closingDate` omitted, no stub entry; the final interest's schedule period is the nearest kept entry's, as today), and a recorded `interestPeriod` from the day after the last kept entry to `closingDate` counts as matching the plan for the flag (the closing's stub). **Alternative:** a closing stub in the derivation for every interval (the period of a split booked after the last kept entry runs to `closingDate`), which changes the final period of monthly Loans with a set change in their last month.
6. **The flag's name and level.** **Proposal:** `INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE`, an item flag, open when the recorded and the schedule's period give different parts, informative when the parts are equal; cleared by right terms or a superseding classification, no acknowledgement. **Alternatives:** (a) always open (every off-by-a-day statement blocks `final` until the classification is restated); (b) always informative (the decision's „geflaggt“ without effect on `final`); (c) open with an acknowledgement of §58E Part 2 (a new kind, migration of 0065's CHECKs).
7. **Existing recorded periods on Loans still at interval 1.** **Proposal:** flagged from the deployment on, like any other (that is the decision's purpose: it shows where the terms need the interval), with the release note. **Alternative:** compared only for classifications created after the deployment, or only for Loans whose terms state an interval other than 1 (fewer flags, but a monthly-entered annual Loan stays unnoticed).
8. **The 10-day rule with longer intervals.** **Proposal:** unchanged in form (`DE_CASH_TIMING@1`, its hash, §58F): the due date is the nearest entry of the interval's plan, which is now right where today's monthly plan invents due dates; the Steuerberater is asked before enablement whether quarterly, half-yearly and yearly interest count as „regelmäßig wiederkehrend“ (§ 11 EStG; not part of the tax review of 2026-11-01), and until the answer the item counts as unconfirmed for that case. **Alternatives:** (a) the 10-day rule only for interval 1, longer intervals by the booking date (a new rule version); (b) no question, treated as monthly.
9. **The 50-year cap.** **Proposal:** 600 months of intervals (rule 3), so the cap keeps meaning 50 years. **Alternative:** 600 payments for every interval (600 years for a yearly Loan; harmless with a `maturityDate`, but `INTEREST_ONLY` without one then plans six centuries).
10. **VC-X-54 and the order.** **Proposal:** VC-X-53 first, on its own (one migration); VC-X-54 after it, then also covering a part moved by an interval entered after the year's end (the pinning test extended until then). **Alternatives:** (a) both in one item and PR (terms records as part kinds with 0065 widened, one migration for both); (b) VC-X-54 first, so the first interval entered on an old Loan is already flagged as a part change.
11. **Keep the recorded `interestPeriod` as a fallback, or deprecate it.** **Proposal:** keep it as a secondary fallback (above, "Precedence"): the plan with its interval is the primary source; the recorded period is used only for a Loan without a schedule and, where it deviates from the plan, still for the allocation but always with `INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE`; equal to the plan it is redundant and the view reports `LOAN_SCHEDULE`; existing periods kept and flagged when they deviate; new ones still accepted; no migration. **Alternatives:** (a) **the plan wins** once the Loan has a schedule: a deviating recorded period is ignored for the allocation and only shown (the flag informative), the recorded period counting only for Loans without terms (amends L4's precedence; Loans still at interval 1 with a recorded quarter or year then fall back to the monthly period until their terms are corrected); (b) **deprecate:** as (a), and `POST /tax-classifications` refuses `interestPeriod` on a split whose Loan has a schedule (`422 INTEREST_PERIOD_FROM_SCHEDULE`), existing ones kept (0069 frozen) and read as in (a); (c) keep L4 unchanged (the recorded period always wins, the flag as above), which is the proposal without the reporting rule for case 3.
12. **Teilzinsen der ersten Rate (#121, Fall A).** (Its place as question 12: Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05. The owner's direction of 2026-11-05: „Warum machen wir es nicht so, dass die einfach Regel gilt und dann die Daten immer mit dem echten Upload abgeglichen und bei Abweichungen auf die Echtwelt Daten korrigiert werden“; the substance stays open.) The first real debit showed case A: interest for 36 days 30/360 from the payout, the annuity fixed, the principal share reduced. **Proposal:** the simple rule plus reconciliation with the real bookings (above, "The first payment"): (a) the proposal takes the split from the bank's purpose text (`RECHN.ZINS <interest> TILG./ENTG. <principal> TILGUNG PER <date>`) where it adds up to the debit, else the plan's split (fallback and counter-check); (b) the schedule and the planned remaining debt are rebased on the actual remaining debt after the last booked payment, the contract plan kept as `plannedAsContracted`/`differenceAsContracted`, Taxation reading the contract plan's dates; (c) `BOOKED_SPLIT_DIFFERS_FROM_PLAN` once on that payment, informative; §58L's stub period through the recorded `interestPeriod` where a set changes inside it; no migration. **Alternatives:** (a) `firstInterestFrom` on the first terms period, the first interest over rule 4's full interval plus the bond-basis `extraDays` before the period start in one rounding (equal to rule 4 by construction when it is the period start; 36 days in the real case; Loan F 360.00 / 240.00 / 119 760.00, the February variant 340.00, quarterly 970.00), in the same migration; (a′) the same field with the plain bond count from `firstInterestFrom` to the payment date (Loan F 36 days, the February variant 36 days and 360.00, quarterly 96 days and 960.00; no equality with rule 4 for due dates not on the 31st); a lender on 30E/360 would count differently in months of 31 days and February, which the real data cannot tell; (b) `firstInterestOverride`, the first interest as an amount from the lender's statement (no date for §58L's period); (c) a separate backlog row and migration after VC-X-53; (d) the reconciliation of the proposal without the rebase (the plan stays the contract's, `difference` cumulative as today); (e) case B as well (the stub as a separate debit), not seen in the real data.

### As implemented (VC-X-53)

Implemented as specified and decided (questions 1–12, Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05; above, "Open questions (decided)"), with **migration 0070** (the next free number; verified: 0069 was the last on main f574a96). Paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`.

**What was built:**

1. **The field** (`domains/financing/terms.ts`): `LoanTermsData.paymentIntervalMonths` (`PAYMENT_INTERVALS` 1, 3, 6, 12), in `SchedulePeriod`; `walkSchedule` takes the k-th date as `addMonths(firstPaymentDate, k × n)`, the interest `periodInterest(balance, rate, n)` (one rounding; `monthlyInterest` is `periodInterest` with 1), the cap as 600 months of intervals; check 7 over the interval; `termsFingerprint` gains the interval only when it is not 1.
2. **The API and the store:** the create body's `paymentIntervalMonths` (JSON integer; a string, a fraction, `null` or a boolean `400 INVALID_FORMAT`, another integer `400 OUT_OF_RANGE`; default 1), every terms response, the `CREATED` AuditRecord's metadata (always), `toTerms`; an idempotency snapshot stored before VC-X-53 replays as 1.
3. **The rebase** (`domains/financing/rebase.ts`, `reconciledPlan`): the counted splits of the Loan (§41.5, read in the schedule's snapshot, `scheduleInputs`, and in §41.6's `debtInputs`) grouped per Transaction; a regular debit (with a `LOAN_INTEREST` split) matched to its nearest entry of the contract plan, a principal-only payment to none; each re-anchors the plan (a `PlanRestart` in `walkSchedule`) with the entry after it, on the actual remaining debt after its booking date. `planOf`/`loanPlan` return the plan with `plannedBefore` (the planned balance, rebased from the last restart booked before the date). The schedule (`getLoanSchedule`) reads the rebased plan with `rebasedOn` and the entries' `flags`; `debtOn` gives `planned`/`difference` from it and `plannedAsContracted`/`differenceAsContracted` from the contract plan, `rebasedOn` of the day; `fixedRateEnd` from the rebased plan in both reads. `loanSchedule` stays the contract plan: Taxation (`tax-source-facts.ts`, `loan-interest-periods.ts`, `attribution-history.ts`) reads only it.
4. **The purpose text** (`domains/financing/purpose-formats.ts`): `LOAN_PURPOSE_FORMATS`, a registry by name as `GENERIC_CSV_PRESETS` (a format never changes under its name), today `BBBANK_LOAN_DEBIT`; `readPurpose` tries each, the first that recognises the text reads it. `proposePayment` proposes the text's split where it adds up to the amount (`source = PURPOSE_TEXT`, `purposeFormat`), else the plan's (`SCHEDULE`); `scheduleSplit` always; `PURPOSE_SPLIT_NOT_MATCHING` and `SPLIT_DIFFERS_FROM_SCHEDULE` informative.
5. **Taxation** (`domains/taxation/cash-timing.ts`, `loan-interest-periods.ts`, `tax-year-loan-interest.ts`, `tax-year-review.ts`): `interestTiming` takes the first entry's interval (`firstIntervalOf`), `LoanPeriodFacts` gains `firstIntervalMonths`, `entryTerms` and `closingDate`; `interestPeriodOf` returns the schedule's period (`LOAN_SCHEDULE`) for a recorded period equal to it (precedence case 3); `deviationOf` gives the deviation (either end; the closing stub of question 5 matches); the view's read carries it per split (`deviation`), `loanInterestOf` distributes the split once more by the schedule's period for `partsDiffer`, `deriveLoanItem` raises `INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE` with `details { loanId, recorded, schedule, termsId, paymentIntervalMonths, partsDiffer }`, `flagIsOpen` opens it where `partsDiffer`.
6. **Migration 0070** (`0070_loan_terms_payment_interval.ts`): `payment_interval_months smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`, CHECK `loan_terms_payment_interval` `IN (1, 3, 6, 12)`, no `UPDATE` (no version, no AuditRecord); `loan_terms_frozen` replaced with the column in its list, otherwise 0025's function word for word; `down` refuses (`23000`, naming the first such terms id) while a period is not 1, then restores 0025's function verbatim (compared with `pg_get_functiondef` before 0070) and drops the column.

**Deviations and interpretations:**

- (a) **The rebase is per booked payment, not only the last** (§58O (b) names the last booked payment): every booked payment re-anchors the plan in turn, each entry following the restart before it. With one booked payment this is §58O's text exactly (Loan F's and Loan M's figures); with several it is what example (c) requires (entry 2, booked as rebased, carries no flag) and keeps "no later entry repeats it". So the entries before the last restart are the plan as it stood before each booking, the contract's up to the first booking.
- (b) **The proposal reads the contract plan** (§58O "Unchanged guarantees": the proposal changes only where a purpose text states the split); `scheduleSplit` is the contract plan's entry. The schedule, `planned`, `difference` and `fixedRateEnd` read the rebased plan.
- (c) `rebasedOn` carries `transactionId` and `flags` (the `BOOKED_SPLIT_DIFFERS_FROM_PLAN` of the payment that re-anchored, as (c) wants it shown in the remaining-debt read's `rebasedOn`) besides `{ bookingDate, entryNumber, actualBalance }`; `entryNumber` is the number of the last entry before the rebased ones (a special repayment's: the last entry on or before its booking date; 0 before the first). In the remaining-debt read it is the last re-anchoring booked on or before `asOf`.
- (d) Edge rules of the rebase: a later booking with an entry at or before an earlier restart supersedes it; a restart whose entry the plan does not reach (the plan paid off earlier) applies where the plan ended; an actual debt below 0 re-anchors at 0; a follow-up period's `principalAtStart` still restarts the balance from its first entry when the rebase lies at or before it (the contract states it).
- (e) **The named format:** `LOAN_PURPOSE_FORMATS` lives in Financing (pure; the domain may not import the import adapters); every format is tried in order (a Transaction need not come from an import preset), the first that recognises the text reads it. The answer carries `purposeFormat` besides `source`. `PURPOSE_SPLIT_NOT_MATCHING` also covers a recognised pattern with an unreadable amount or date (`stated: null`). The pattern is case-sensitive, as the bank writes it.
- (f) `plannedAsContracted` and `differenceAsContracted` are Loan-level only (§58O names the read, not the per-property items; the items' `planned` and `difference` are the rebased ones, distributed as before).
- (g) The flag on a not attributed entry carries `notAttributed: true` in its `details`, so `flagIsOpen` keeps it informative there whatever `partsDiffer`.

Every other change in existing tests is the new DTO keys (`paymentIntervalMonths`, `plannedAsContracted`, `differenceAsContracted`, `rebasedOn`, `flags`, `source`, `purposeFormat`, `scheduleSplit`) and `paymentIntervalMonths: 1` in test literals.

The byte check of "omitted against explicit 1" is made in `loan-payment-interval.e2e.test.ts` on a monthly Loan with a 10-day-rule debit (its 2027 view at the property and an owner level, rendered before and after voiding the terms and entering them again with an explicit 1), not on ACC8's world, whose Loan has no attributed item.

**Release note (as implemented):**

*From VC-X-53 on, each Loan terms period states its payment interval (`paymentIntervalMonths`: 1, 3, 6 or 12; default 1). Every existing period is monthly, and every figure of a monthly Loan is unchanged. A Loan entered with another interval pays every 3, 6 or 12 months in its plan with that interval's interest, and the tax-year view distributes each interest debit over the whole quarter, half-year or year by the allocation sets of each day, without a recorded interest period. **There are now two plans.** Financing shows the plan **rebased** on the actual remaining debt after the last booked payment: the schedule, the remaining debt's `planned` (now the forecast from the last booking) and `difference`, and `fixedRateEnd`; the contract plan's figures stay visible beside it as `plannedAsContracted` and `differenceAsContracted`, and a booked split that differs from the plan is flagged once, informative (`BOOKED_SPLIT_DIFFERS_FROM_PLAN`). **Taxation reads the due dates (10-day rule) and the §58L interest periods from the contract plan**, never from the rebased one, so no tax figure depends on the rebase; the tax figures stay the booked splits. The payment proposal takes the interest and principal from the bank's purpose text where a named format states them (today BBBank's, `BBBANK_LOAN_DEBIT`) and they add up to the debit, and says so (`source`); otherwise it proposes the plan's split, as before. A recorded interest period that differs from the Loan's plan is flagged (`INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE`), open where it changes a PropertyReference's part, so recorded quarters and years on Loans still entered as monthly show up at once: void the last terms period and enter it again with the interval (a part that moves by it is flagged from VC-X-54 on, §58P). Whether quarterly, half-yearly and yearly interest counts as „regelmäßig wiederkehrend“ for the 10-day rule is open with the Steuerberater (`beratungsfragen.md` §3) and unconfirmed until answered. No year is productively filed yet, so the deployment raises no change flag; productive AfA recording stays disabled.*
