# 58P. Loan Terms Changes and Closings as Part Changes (VC-X-54, implemented: migration 0071)

**Status:** **implemented** (VC-X-54, migration 0071; below, "As implemented (VC-X-54)"); **open questions 1–11 decided by the owner on 2026-11-05, all as proposed** ("Open questions (decided)" at the end of this section; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05). Backlog VC-X-54, created by the owner's decision on §58L open question 10 (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04) and placed after VC-X-53 by the owner's decision on §58O open question 10 (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05). **Migration:** one, the next free number at implementation (**0071** at the time of writing: main 425de07 ends at 0070). Productive AfA recording stays disabled; nothing here touches it, and no unconfirmed tax assumption reads as released by it (the item adds a change flag; it changes no figure).

**What it amends:** §58G (the kinds of `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED`, its "Not a part change" list, "In the database"), §58L "Interaction with VC-X-28/48/49/50/51" (the bullet "Terms and a closing move the period, not only the year"), §58O "Interaction with VC-X-54 and the change flags" (the bullet "A part that moves … is not flagged until VC-X-54"), §58E Part 2's body `kind` (three more values), the invariant suite's "no silent move of a part"; migration 0065's (as widened by 0067) `tax_year_acknowledgement` CHECKs and its shape guard.

**Unchanged guarantees:** **every figure of the tax-year view is unchanged** (the parts are those of the terms, the closing and the sets as now recorded, §58D decision 1 as amended by §58L; the flag only says that they differ from what they were before a record made after the year's end). The tax year of every split (§58A, `DE_CASH_TIMING@1` and its pinned hash); `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`, its kinds `LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`/`_VOIDED`/`LOAN_CLOSED` and their year items (§58E Part 1, §58H Part 1); §58G's set kinds, §58H Part 2's deposit kinds, §58I Part 2's correction kinds and their rules; the part item's shape, the fingerprint, the levels, the routes, the order of checks and `CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` (§58G); §58L's rules 1–10, §58O's rules, its precedence of the plan and the recorded `interestPeriod` and its deviation flag; Financing (§41), its rebased plan (§58O question 12) and `paymentsInYear`; §59E and §60. The view writes nothing (P7-D8). No route changes.

**Why a section of its own, after §58O:** VC-X-54 is a backlog item of its own; §58L created it and left it out of VC-X-40, and §58O open question 10 (decided) orders it after VC-X-53. Its number is the next free letter (verified: §58O is the last §58 letter on main 425de07).

### The decided fact (verbatim)

Cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04“ (the owner's answer on §58L open questions 2, 3 and 5–12; recorded in full in §58L "Decided by the owner on 2026-11-04 (chat)"):

> - **L2, L3, L5 bis L12: wie vorgeschlagen.** Kein Deployment-Flag, ganzer Split nicht zugeordnet bei Lücken, Kalendertage, Eigentümer am Buchungstag, eine Verteilung je Split, `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` wie vorgeschlagen, §59E-Fall bleibt mit `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS` außerhalb der Basis, Konditionen und Schließungen als neue Zeile, eigener E2E-Test, Financing bleibt operativ.

§58L open question 10's proposal, which that answer took: „not in VC-X-40; a new backlog row (**VC-X-54**, created) for `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` kinds of `LoanTerms` and `Loan` `CLOSED` records (migration), as VC-X-49 left VC-X-50; until then a test pins that such a record after the year's end can move a part without a flag.“ And on the order, cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05“ (§58O "Open questions (decided)"):

> - **10: wie vorgeschlagen** (VC-X-53 allein, VC-X-54 danach).

§58O open question 10's proposal: „VC-X-54 after it, then also covering a part moved by an interval entered after the year's end (the pinning test extended until then).“

So three things are decided: **terms records and closings become kinds of `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED`** (not of a new code; §58G open question 1, decided 2026-11-03: „`PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` als ein Code für alles, was den Anteil statt des Jahres verschiebt; die Quelle steht im `kind`“), **with a migration**, and **an interval entered after a year's end is covered**. Everything else below (the kinds' names and granularity, the rule's edges, the items, the migration's form, the test that replaces the pin) is this section's proposal and open to the owner (open questions 1–11).

### As the code stands (main 425de07; paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`)

- **The part kinds:** `PART_CHANGE_KINDS` (`domains/taxation/attribution-parts.ts:27-34`) lists the set kinds (§58G), the deposit kinds (§58H Part 2) and the correction kinds (§58I Part 2); `PartChangeEntityType` (`:36`) is `LoanAllocationSet | RentPaymentReconciliation | Transaction`. The API's `kind` is `z.enum([...CHANGE_KINDS, ...PART_CHANGE_KINDS, OWNERSHIP_START_FLAG])` (`api/tax-statements.ts:43`), so a code may not stand in both lists.
- **Terms records and the closing are year kinds only:** `CHANGE_KINDS` (`domains/taxation/attribution-rule.ts:8-18`) holds `LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`, `LOAN_TERMS_VOIDED` and `LOAN_CLOSED`. `termsChanges` (`domains/taxation/attribution-history.ts:196-245`) replays each Loan's terms records, derives the payment dates per side (`datesOf`, `:253-256`) and flags only items whose **year** moves (`movedItems` with `attributeTaxYear`, `:226-230`); `closingChanges` (`:276-314`) does the same with the schedule without and with the closing (`:295-296`). Their candidates are the window splits of Loans a `VALID` set of which names P (`infrastructure/postgres/attribution-reads.ts:170-233`, the windows `:191`), filtered by `concerns` (`attribution-history.ts:211`).
- **The part changes read sets only:** for Loans, `partChanges` (`attribution-parts.ts:146-…`) walks only `LoanAllocationSet` records (`:162-168`) and computes P's part per side with `partOn` (`:172`; `domains/taxation/attribution-part-rule.ts:25-39`, the view's own `distributeOverPeriod`). Each candidate carries **one** interest period, computed **now** (`PartCandidate.period`, `attribution-parts.ts:56-63`; filled from the view's read in `infrastructure/postgres/part-reads.ts:47`), and `partChangeInputOf` reads the AuditRecords of `LoanAllocationSet` only (`part-reads.ts:33-39`). So a record that changes the period cannot be judged: there is no "before" period.
- **The period depends on the terms and the closing:** `interestPeriodOf` (`domains/taxation/loan-interest-periods.ts:51-61`) takes the recorded `interestPeriod` (VC-X-40) or the schedule's period of the nearest entry (`schedulePeriodOf`, `:64-71`, with the first entry's interval of VC-X-53), and the facts come from the **contract** plan of the `VALID` terms, cut at a closing (`infrastructure/postgres/loan-interest-periods.ts:21-39`; §58O question 12 (b): Taxation never reads the rebased plan). A terms record (a new `firstPaymentDate`, interval, rate that ends the plan earlier, a void) or a closing (entries after `closingDate` omitted) therefore changes a split's period, and with a set boundary inside the old or new period, P's part.
- **The pin:** `domains/taxation/tax-year-loan-periods.test.ts:428-451` ("pinned until VC-X-54 …"): new terms due on the 15th move P1's part 230.00 → 155.00, the quarterly interval 230.00 → 282.44, each without `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED`.
- **The database:** `tax_year_acknowledgement`'s `change_kind` CHECK (0065 `:21-24`, `:41`; widened by 0067 with `OWNERSHIP_START_BEFORE_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER`, `0067_acquisition_transfer_date_record.ts:30-32`, `:139-146`), `change_entity_type` (`LoanTerms` and `Loan` already listed), `tax_year_acknowledgement_kind_entity` (0065 `:28-33` plus 0067's `Acquisition` clause): it binds `Loan` to `LOAN_CLOSED` alone and has **no clause for `LoanTerms`**, which is bound by elimination only (every other entity type's clause refuses `LOAN_TERMS_*`, and every other kind has a clause naming its own entity). The shape guard `tax_year_acknowledgement_item_shape()` admits part items only under the set, deposit and correction kinds (0065 `:59`), with 0067's patch for its own kind (`0067_…:96-111`, by `pg_get_functiondef`).
- **Found while specifying (open question 10):** under §58O question 5, a recorded `interestPeriod` from the day after a `CLOSED` Loan's last kept entry to its `closingDate` "matches the plan" (`deviationOf`, `loan-interest-periods.ts:94`), and `interestPeriodOf` then returns **the schedule's** period (`:59`), not the recorded stub: the stub is not flagged, but it is not used either. Only `deviationOf` is tested for that case (`domains/taxation/loan-interest-interval.test.ts:184-189`). Example 2 below meets it.

### The rule

**A Loan's terms record or closing recorded after a year's end that moves P's part of an interest item of that year is a part change, by §58G's one rule, with the terms or the closing as the input.**

1. **The records:** each `LoanTerms` AuditRecord `CREATED` or `VOIDED` and each `Loan` AuditRecord `CLOSED` of a candidate Loan, each judged alone (§58E Part 1), with `occurred_at` **after 31 December of `year`** (Europe/Berlin, `recordedAfter`; open question 6).
2. **The candidates:** §58G's: the counting `LOAN_INTEREST` splits with a `loanId` of a Loan **any** of whose sets (`VALID` or `VOID`) names P, in the whole year (not only the windows: a period moves anywhere in the year).
3. **The two sides:**
   - for a **terms** record: the Loan's `VALID` terms just before and just after the record (§58E's replay of the terms records, as `termsChanges`), **the closing as now** (as `termsChanges`);
   - for the **closing**: the terms as now, the Loan without and with the closing (as `closingChanges`);
   - everything else as read now: the sets (§41.3, with `validUntil`), `debtFrom`, the split's current classification with its recorded `interestPeriod` and `taxYear` override.
4. **P's part per side:** the split's interest period by `interestPeriodOf` over **that side's contract plan** (§58L rule 1 with §58O's interval and precedence: the recorded period where it deviates from that side's plan, the plan's where it equals it, §58L rule 8 by the booking date where that side has no schedule), then `partOn` (§58G's table: `ATTRIBUTED` with the part, `NOT_ATTRIBUTED`, `NONE`).
5. **Only items whose tax year is `year` on both sides** (§58A per side, `attributeTaxYear` with that side's due date, as `termsChanges` derives it): an item whose year moves is the year kind's (`LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`/`_VOIDED`, `LOAN_CLOSED`), not a part item (§58G rule 1: "the same on both sides"; open question 4).
6. **Moved:** §58G's `partMoved` (decided 2026-11-03, open question 3): the states differ, not between `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` and `NONE`, or both `ATTRIBUTED` with other amounts (a one-cent move counts).
7. **The kind** (open question 1): `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED` (`LoanTerms` `CREATED`), `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED` (`LoanTerms` `VOIDED`, open question 2), `LOAN_CLOSED_PART` (`Loan` `CLOSED`). One change per record, PropertyReference and year, with every item it moved; `changeFingerprint` as §58G (the parts in it).
8. **A history that does not fit** (records not ending in the current status, a second `CLOSED`): `ATTRIBUTION_HISTORY_INCONSISTENT` with `LoanTerms` or `Loan`, the records unused and the status held, exactly as the year kinds report it (one entry per entity, not one per flag).

**What fires, in short:** a terms record or closing after the year's end that changes an interest split's period so that the split's weights change: a new or voided terms period with another `firstPaymentDate`, **another `paymentIntervalMonths`** (VC-X-53; §58O "Interaction with VC-X-54"), another rate or payment that ends the plan earlier or later, the first terms of a Loan without terms (rule 8 on the before side) or the void of its only terms (rule 8 on the after side), a closing that omits the entry nearest to a final debit; in each case only where a set boundary lies in the old or the new period, or a day of one of them has no set.

**What does not fire:**

- **A record that leaves every part equal:** a change of the period inside one set (§58L rule 7: the same `distribute` over the same set), a rate change that moves no payment date, the interval entered where every period lies in one set, a void and re-entry with identical dates.
- **A record on or before 31 December of the item's year** (the 31-December rule).
- **A split whose year moves:** the year kind flags it (rule 5).
- **A recorded `interestPeriod` that deviates on both sides:** it wins on both (§58O precedence case 2), so the parts are equal; `INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE` may appear or disappear with the record, which is no change kind (§58O "The deviation flag").
- **§58O's rebase and every booked split:** Taxation reads the contract plan only (§58O question 12 (b), decided), so a confirmed split that re-anchors Financing's plan moves no period; a ledger correction is §58I Part 2's. **A recorded `interestPeriod`** is a person's statement on the split (§58G "Not a part change").
- **A closing of a Loan without terms** (no schedule on either side, §58L rule 8 on both) and the Loan voided (§41.1: only without splits).
- **The deployment itself** (no AuditRecord; §58L open question 2's reasoning): existing records after a year's end are judged from the deployment on (open question 6), which is a release note, not a deployment flag.

### Items and details

- **The flag's entry** is §58G's, `kind` one of the three, `entityType` `LoanTerms` or `Loan`, and the kind's own keys: **`{ loanId, termsId, validFrom }`** for the terms kinds (as `LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`'s, `attribution-history.ts:239`), **`{ loanId, closingDate, closingReason }`** for `LOAN_CLOSED_PART` (as `LOAN_CLOSED`'s, `:309`).
- **`items`:** §58G's part shape, `sourceType` `TRANSACTION_SPLIT`, `{ sourceId, taxYear, stateBefore, partBefore, stateAfter, partAfter }`, sorted by `sourceType`, then `sourceId`. **No interest period in the items** (open question 8): the current period is on the item's `loanAllocation.interestPeriod` (§58L), and the stored part item, the fingerprint and the `ACKNOWLEDGED` AuditRecord keep §58G's shape.
- **The year flag and the item flag** `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` as §58G, the level by state (open while an entry has no acknowledgement).

### Acknowledgement (§58E Part 2, §58G, reused)

`POST …/tax-years/{year}/acknowledgements` with `kind` one of the three new values. No route, no step of the order of checks changes. **One record can now be a year change and a part change of the same year:** a terms record that moves a window split's year (§58O "Effects", the 10-day case) and another split's part, or a closing doing both, answers `409 CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` without `kind` (`details.kinds` e.g. `["LOAN_TERMS_ADDED", "LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED"]`); with `kind` each is acknowledged alone. This is the first case of `CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` for Loans (§58G "As implemented (VC-X-48)" 6). The command derives the new kinds in its own snapshot (`partChangeInputOf`, read with the terms and the closing). An acknowledgement clears only its own change (§58E, decided 2026-11-02).

### Migration (the next free number at implementation; 0071 at the time of writing)

`0071_tax_year_loan_schedule_part_kinds` (open question 9):

- **`tax_year_acknowledgement_change_kind_check`:** 0067's list plus `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`, `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED`, `LOAN_CLOSED_PART` (dropped and re-added under its name, as 0063–0067).
- **`tax_year_acknowledgement_change_entity_type_check`:** unchanged (`LoanTerms`, `Loan` are listed).
- **`tax_year_acknowledgement_kind_entity`:** 0067's text with the `Loan` clause widened to `(change_entity_type = 'Loan') = (change_kind IN ('LOAN_CLOSED', 'LOAN_CLOSED_PART'))`. **No `LoanTerms` clause** is added: the elimination already binds the terms kinds to `LoanTerms` and `LoanTerms` to the terms kinds, so an explicit clause would be redundant and no mutation of it could turn a test red; a schema test pins the elimination instead (below).
- **The shape guard** `tax_year_acknowledgement_item_shape()`: the part kinds' `IN` list of 0065 (`:59`) gains the three kinds, patched in the current definition by `pg_get_functiondef` as 0067 does (the passage must occur exactly once, else the migration fails); the `DEPOSIT_CLOSING` test then refuses a deposit item under them, and a year item under them is refused by the first test. `tax_year_acknowledgement_part_item` is unchanged (`source_type` `TRANSACTION_SPLIT`).
- **`down`:** refuses (`check_violation`, before changing anything) while an acknowledgement of a new kind exists (`ACTIVE` or `WITHDRAWN`: a person's statement is never dropped silently, as 0060–0067); otherwise reverses the patch and restores 0067's CHECKs verbatim. The down tests that run later `down`s first (0060, 0063, 0064, 0065, 0067 and `acquisition-transfer-date.test.ts`'s chain) run 0071's first.
- **No column** on `loan_terms`, `loan`, `loan_allocation_set` or any ledger or Taxation table. No backfill, no AuditRecord.

### Example (synthetic)

PropertyReferences P1 and P2 (`propertyReferenceId` P1 < P2); P1 owned by A and B `"1/2"` each (A < B), P2 by C `"1/1"`, all from 2026-01-01. Confirmed `OUTFLOW` debits with `LOAN_INTEREST` (and `LOAN_PRINCIPAL`) splits naming the Loan. Records with their `occurred_at` (UTC).

**1. The interval entered after the year's end (VC-X-53).** §58O's Loan Q: `principalOriginal` 120 000.00, `debtFrom` 2027-01-01, `ANNUITY` at `"3.000"`, `scheduledPayment` 1 800.00, `firstPaymentDate` 2027-03-31; sets `MANUAL` S1 from 2027-01-01 (P1 `"1/1"`), S2 from **2027-03-01** (P1 `"1/2"`, P2 `"1/2"`). The lender debits quarterly; the interest splits: d1 2027-03-31 **900.00**, d2 2027-06-30 **893.25**, d3 2027-09-30 **886.45**, d4 2027-12-31 **879.60** (sum 3 559.30). Records: r0 terms Tm **monthly** (interval 1) `CREATED` 2027-01-04; r1 Tm `VOIDED` **2028-02-10T09:00Z**; r2 terms Tq, the same with **interval 3**, `CREATED` **2028-02-10T09:05Z**.

| Record | d1 before → after (P1 / P2) | d2–d4 | Year of d1–d4 | Part change |
|---|---|---|---|---|

**2. A closing recorded after the year's end.** Loan C: `principalOriginal` 120 000.00, `debtFrom` 2027-01-01, one `INTEREST_ONLY` period from 2027-01-01 at `"3.000"`, `firstPaymentDate` 2027-01-31, monthly (interest 300.00 per entry). Interest splits: 2027-01-31, 02-28, 03-31, 04-30 each **300.00**; the final debit on **2027-05-20**: interest **190.00** (the lender's stub, synthetic) and principal 120 000.00. The Loan is closed with `closingDate` 2027-05-20, the `CLOSED` record r3 on **2028-01-20T08:00Z**.

Recording the stub on the classification (`interestPeriod` 2027-05-01 – 05-20, the closing stub of §58O question 5) is meant to fix it, but today `interestPeriodOf` replaces such a stub by the schedule's period (above, "Found while specifying"), so the stub would still go to P1 (open question 10). Under open question 10's proposal the stub is used: wholly T2, P2 190.00, and that classification is no part change (a recorded period, §58G).

**3. One record, two changes.** §58O's 10-day case (a quarterly Loan due on the 5th of February, May, August and November; a debit booked 2028-01-03, by the monthly plan due 2028-01-05 and in 2027) with a second, ordinary debit of the same Loan in 2027 whose period gains a set boundary under the quarterly plan: the interval entered by a terms record in 2028 is in P's 2027 view a year change `LOAN_TERMS_ADDED` (the January debit leaves 2027) **and** a part change `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED` (the other debit); acknowledging without `kind` answers `409 CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` with both kinds. The January debit is no part item (its year moves, rule 5).

### Interaction with the other flags

- **`ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`** (§58E, §58H Part 1): unchanged; it keeps judging the window candidates' years. A record can raise both flags (Example 3).
- **§58G's set kinds:** unchanged; they keep reading the terms and the closing as now (`partOn` with each candidate's current period). **§58H Part 2, §58I Part 2:** unchanged; a correction that changes an interest split's booking date keeps its own kind.
- **§58L/§58O item flags:** `INTEREST_PERIOD_UNKNOWN` (rule 8) and `INTEREST_PERIOD_DEVIATES_FROM_SCHEDULE` appear and disappear with such records; neither is a change kind, neither is acknowledged.
- **§59E and §60** (open question 7): a part change of an attributed `CAPITALIZED` interest item makes its component's basis differ from P's part (`LOAN_INTEREST_CAPITALIZED_NOT_IN_BASIS` with `BASIS_MISMATCH`, or `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS` where the new period spans two sets), as §58G "The effect on `final`" says for a set; a recorded schedule version compares its stored input fingerprint (§60, P's part in a Loan component), so it shows `DEPRECIATION_CHANGED_SINCE_RECORDED` independently. Acknowledging the part change clears neither. Recording stays disabled, so no productive version exists.

### The effect on `final`, ACC7 and ACC8

- **The rule for `final` stays §58C's.** A year with such a part change after its end is not final until each change is acknowledged; this can turn a `final: true` of today into `false` after the deployment, the intended correction (release note; no year is productively filed yet).
- **ACC7 and ACC8 expect no change** (open question 11): ACC7's Loans have no terms, so no terms record exists and no side has a schedule. ACC8's one interest split (booked 2026-09-20, the set from 2026-10-01) is not attributed on every side: its schedule period 2026-09-01 – 09-30 has no set, and without terms rule 8 finds none on the booking date, so whatever the order of its records, `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` is never a part change. A flag appearing there is a finding to report and explain, not to suppress.

### Release note (proposal; final text under "As implemented (VC-X-54)")

*From VC-X-54 on, a Loan's terms period added or voided, or the Loan's closing, recorded after a tax year's end, raises `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` (kinds `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`, `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED`, `LOAN_CLOSED_PART`) in the views of every PropertyReference whose part of that year's Loan interest it moved, as an allocation set already does. Such a record changes the plan's payment dates, so an interest split's period (§58L) and, where an allocation set changes inside it, the PropertyReferences' parts; entering the payment interval on an existing non-monthly Loan (VC-X-53) is the expected case. No figure changes: the parts are those of the terms and the closing as now recorded; the flag says that they differ from what they were. A year previously shown as `final` can be open again where such a record exists after its end; acknowledging each change in each view clears it. A record that moves a split's year keeps raising `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`; one that does both needs `kind` when acknowledged. No year is productively filed yet; productive AfA recording stays disabled.*

### As implemented (VC-X-54)

Implemented as specified and decided (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05, §58P Fragen 1–11, alle wie vorgeschlagen). Paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`.

- **The rule:** `domains/taxation/attribution-loan-schedule-parts.ts` (`scheduleSteps`, `planFactsOf`): each `LoanTerms` `CREATED`/`VOIDED` record (walked with `replay`/`walk` as `termsChanges`) and the Loan's one `CLOSED` record (replayed as `closingChanges`), judged alone, after 31 December of `year` in Europe/Berlin (`recordedAfter`, also for records made before the deployment, Frage 6). Per side the contract plan of that side's `VALID` terms (`planFactsOf`: `loanSchedule`, cut at a closing; the terms side with the closing as now, the closing side with the terms as now), the split's year per side (`attributeTaxYear` with that side's due date, the `taxYear` override as now; a split whose year differs from `year` on either side is no part item, Frage 4), its period per side (`interestPeriodOf` with the recorded `interestPeriod` as stored), P's part per side (`partOn` over the sets as now), `partMoved`. Kinds by action (Frage 1, 2): `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`, `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED` on `LoanTerms` with `{ loanId, termsId, validFrom }`, `LOAN_CLOSED_PART` on `Loan` with `{ loanId, closingDate, closingReason }`; items in §58G's part shape, no period in them, §58G's fingerprint (Frage 8). An inconsistent terms or closing history is `ATTRIBUTION_HISTORY_INCONSISTENT` with `LoanTerms`/`Loan`, named once beside the year kinds' entry.
- **`attribution-parts.ts`:** `PART_CHANGE_KINDS` gains the three kinds, `PartChangeEntityType` `LoanTerms` and `Loan`; `PartCandidate` gains `recordedPeriod`, `financialCategoryCode`, `taxYearOverride` (optional), `LoanSetsHistory` an optional `schedule` (`LoanScheduleHistory`: the Loan, `debtFrom`, its terms with records, its `CLOSED` records); `partChanges` takes the rule registry in its context (the view and the command pass theirs; with schedule histories and no registry it throws rather than guess).
- **Reads:** `infrastructure/postgres/part-reads.ts` (`loanScheduleOf`): for each Loan of §58G's wide read, the Loan read in the Realm, its terms (`VALID` and `VOID`) in the Realm, their `CREATED`/`VOIDED` and the Loan's `CLOSED` AuditRecords by `audit_record_entity_idx`, in the view's and the command's snapshots. `tax-year-reads.ts` hands each split's recorded `interestPeriod` through (`LoanInterestSplit.recordedPeriod`, reads only). `loan-interest-periods.ts` (`loanPeriodFactsOf`) builds its facts with the same `planFactsOf`, so the view's period and both sides cannot drift.
- **Question 10:** `interestPeriodOf` returns the plan's period only for a recorded period **equal** to it; every other recorded period is used (`source` `CLASSIFICATION`), so a recorded closing stub, which `deviationOf` still counts as matching (not flagged), now goes to the stub's sets (Example 2: P2 190.00). No productive data holds such a stub.
- **Migration 0071** (`0071_tax_year_loan_schedule_part_kinds`, the next free number, verified: main d6f0095 ended at 0070): as "Migration" above; the shape guard patched by `pg_get_functiondef` (the passage found exactly once, else the migration fails), no `LoanTerms` clause (Frage 9). The hand-run `down` chains of 0060, 0063, 0064, 0065, 0067 and 0070's tests run 0071's `down` first (under `withMigrationLock`).
- **API:** no route change (the enum spreads `PART_CHANGE_KINDS`); `docs/development/api-inventory.md` unchanged.
- **The pin replaced** (Frage 5): `tax-year-loan-periods.test.ts` "VC-X-54 (§58P Frage 5, the former pin inverted) …" plus the counter-check (the same records made before the year's end: same figures, no record after the year's end, no flag).
- **ACC7, ACC8:** unchanged and green; no flag appeared.

**Deviations and interpretations:**

1. **The inverted pin's two cases** (the spec said "each … flagged with `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`, P1 230.00 → 155.00 and 230.00 → 282.44"): due on the 15th is entered as a follow-up terms period from 2027-03-01 (one `CREATED` record: `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED` 230.00 → 155.00). The quarterly interval can only be entered by a void and a re-entry (P3-D2), and each record is judged alone (Frage 2): the void is `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED` 230.00 → 155.00 (rule 8 after), the re-entry `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED` 155.00 → 282.44. 230.00 → 282.44 in one record is not possible.
2. **Example 3 made concrete** (the spec gives no figures): Loan monthly `INTEREST_ONLY` due on the 5th from 2027-02-05; a follow-up period quarterly from 2027-12-01 (first payment 2028-02-05) recorded 2028-02-10; sets P1 from 2027-01-01, P1/P2 half each from 2027-11-01; the January debit 2028-01-03 (300.00) moves 2027 → 2028 (`LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`), the ordinary debit 2027-12-20 (310.00) moves P1 155.00 → 285.00 (`LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`, its period 2027-11-06 – 12-05 before, 2027-10-06 – 11-05 after); without `kind` `409 CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` with both kinds, from real data too.
3. **Two mutations of the spec's table are equivalent here** (reported, not hidden): "the candidates restricted to Loans with a `VALID` set naming P" (the sets are read as now, so a P named by no `VALID` set has `NONE` on both sides of a terms record or closing: no item either way); "the period per side from the rebased plan" (every booked interest debit re-anchors Financing's plan at its matched contract entry, so around a booked split the rebased dates are the contract's; the rebase test pins exactly that, and Taxation reads the contract plan).
4. **`partChanges` takes the registry** in its context (optional in the type; required, with an error otherwise, once schedule histories are given) instead of reading it from the input.

| `partMoved` replaced by a comparison of the periods | inside one set, S2 from April (11) |
| `NOT_ATTRIBUTED` ↔ `NONE` flagged | the uncovered-day test (1) |
| `VOIDED` judged as `CREATED` | the void tests (8) |
| the new kinds coded as the year kinds | Example 1, the repository's order of checks (13) |
| the kind CHECK without `LOAN_CLOSED_PART` | the schema tests (3) |
| the `Loan` clause without `LOAN_CLOSED_PART` | the schema tests (4) |
| the shape guard's list without the terms kinds | the shape guard, `up`/`down` (2) |
| `down` without its refusal | the `down` test (1) |
| the Realm filter dropped from the terms read in `part-reads.ts` | Realm isolation (1) |
| question 10 reverted | Example 2's stub in the domain, the view and the repository (3) |
| the schedule histories not read | repository and e2e (8) |

**Release note:** *From VC-X-54 on, a Loan's terms period added or voided, or the Loan's closing, recorded after a tax year's end (also before this release), raises `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED` (kinds `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`, `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED`, `LOAN_CLOSED_PART`) in the views of every PropertyReference whose part of that year's Loan interest it moved, as an allocation set already does; entering the payment interval on an existing non-monthly Loan is the expected case. No figure changes by the flag: the parts are those of the terms and the closing as now recorded. A year shown as `final` can be open again; acknowledging each change in each view clears it. A record that moves a split's year keeps raising `ATTRIBUTION_INPUT_CHANGED`; one that does both needs `kind`. A closing stub recorded on a classification (`interestPeriod` from the day after the last kept entry to the closing date) is now used for the allocation, unflagged (no productive data holds one). No year is productively filed yet; productive AfA recording stays disabled.*

### Open questions (decided)

**Decided by the owner on 2026-11-05 (chat), verbatim** (the §58P part of the answer; cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05“):

> Beide Listen beantwortet. §58P durchgehend wie vorgeschlagen.
>
> **§58P, VC-X-54: alle elf wie vorgeschlagen.**
>
> - **1** drei Kinds je Datensatzaktion. **2** auch Voids zählen, jeder Datensatz für sich. **3** Jahres-Kinds bleiben neben den Anteils-Kinds, getrennt quittiert. **4** ein Posten, dessen Jahr wandert, ist kein Anteils-Posten. **5** Pin-Test durch sein Gegenteil plus Gegenprobe ersetzen. **6** 31.-Dezember-Regel, auch für Datensätze vor dem Deployment. **7** §59E und §60 unverändert. **8** keine Zeiträume im Posten, Fingerprint bleibt. **9** eine Migration ohne redundante `LoanTerms`-Klausel. **10** der Abschluss-Stub wird in VC-X-54 repariert, Beispiel 2 hängt daran, nichts Produktives ändert sich. **11** eigener PR nach VC-X-53, ACC7 und ACC8 unverändert.

So every proposal below is the decision and every alternative is not taken.

1. **The kinds' names and granularity.** **Decided (as proposed):** three kinds, by record: `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED` and `LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED` on `LoanTerms`, `LOAN_CLOSED_PART` on `Loan` (the names §58L open question 10's alternative used; one kind per record action, as the set kinds). **Alternatives (not taken):** (a) one `LOAN_TERMS_PART_CHANGED` for both terms actions (two kinds in all; the action only in the AuditRecord); (b) one `LOAN_SCHEDULE_PART_CHANGED` for terms and closing (one kind on two entity types; `kind_entity` then needs an `OR` per entity); (c) the year kinds' codes (`LOAN_TERMS_ADDED`, `LOAN_CLOSED`) reused under `PROPERTY_PART_CHANGED`: not possible without a second discriminator, since `kind` must name one change (§58G open question 4) and the API's enum holds both flags' kinds.
2. **Do voided terms count?** **Decided (as proposed):** yes (`LOAN_TERMS_PART_VOIDED`), as the year kinds and the set kinds count a void: a void without re-entry moves parts as much as an addition (rule 8 on the after side), and each record is judged alone (Example 1: the void r1 moved nothing, the re-entry r2 did). **Alternatives (not taken):** (a) only additions, a void never a part change (less noise for the void-and-re-enter correction, P3-D2's only way to fix a period; a void left alone then moves parts silently); (b) a void and the re-entry by the same person within one day judged as one change (a new pairing rule against §58E's "each change judged alone").
3. **The year kinds stay beside the part kinds.** **Decided (as proposed):** yes, unchanged: a terms record or closing can be a year change (window splits whose year moves) and a part change (other splits) of the same year, two entries of two flags, acknowledged separately with `kind` (`409 CHANGE_AMBIGUOUS` without it; Example 3). **Alternatives (not taken):** (a) a record that is a year change in P's year raises only the year flag there (part items suppressed): fewer entries, but a part moved by the same record goes silent; (b) one entry with both item shapes (refused by the owner's decision on §58E open question 4 and §58G open question 1: „brächten eine zweite Form in den Flag-Eintrag“).
4. **An item whose year moves.** **Decided (as proposed):** not a part item (rule 5): it is the year kind's in both years, and §58G's part item names one `taxYear` for both sides. **Alternative (not taken):** a part item as well, in the year it is in now, with `stateBefore` `NONE` (it was not in that year's view before): a second flag on the same move.
5. **The pin test (§58O open question 10).** **Decided (as proposed):** the implementation PR of VC-X-54 removes the test "pinned until VC-X-54 …" (`tax-year-loan-periods.test.ts:428-451`) and puts its inverse on the same fixtures (due on the 15th and quarterly, each recorded after the year's end, now flagged with `LOAN_TERMS_PART_ADDED`), keeping a counter-check that without any record after the year's end nothing is flagged; this is a test change, not a pinned rule (`frozen-rules.test.ts` and the stage-rules hash test are untouched). **Alternative (not taken):** keep the old test renamed as the counter-check only and add the positive cases elsewhere.
6. **The cut-off.** **Decided (as proposed):** §58E's 31-December rule (`occurred_at` after 31 December of the item's year, Europe/Berlin), for every record, also those made before the deployment (as VC-X-28 and VC-X-48 did; the release note says years can reopen; none is productively filed). **Alternatives (not taken):** (a) only records made after the deployment (no reopened year, but a past interval entered after a year's end stays silent); (b) a later cut-off such as the year's statutory filing date (DE does not know whether or when a return was filed; §58E open question 5's reasoning).
7. **§59E and recorded schedule versions (§60).** **Decided (as proposed):** no change: a part change of a `CAPITALIZED` interest item shows in §59E's flag (`BASIS_MISMATCH`, `SEVERAL_ALLOCATION_SETS`) and in a recorded version's comparison (`DEPRECIATION_CHANGED_SINCE_RECORDED`) as for a set; acknowledging it clears neither; recording stays disabled. **Alternatives (not taken):** (a) an acknowledged part change also marks the recorded version's comparison as seen (a statement clearing a flag of another kind, against §58E's "a statement clears exactly its own flag"); (b) a part change of a capitalised item refused as acknowledgeable until §59E's flag is resolved.
8. **The periods in the items.** **Decided (as proposed):** none: §58G's part item unchanged (stored table, fingerprint, `ACKNOWLEDGED` record), the current period shown on the item's `loanAllocation.interestPeriod`. **Alternatives (not taken):** (a) additive `interestPeriodBefore`/`interestPeriodAfter` per item in the DTO only, outside the fingerprint and not stored (the reader sees why the part moved; an acknowledgement's record lacks it); (b) the same stored and fingerprinted (two `daterange` columns on `tax_year_acknowledgement_part_item`, a larger migration).
9. **The migration's form.** **Decided (as proposed):** one migration (the next free number, 0071 at the time of writing): the kind CHECK widened, the `Loan` clause of `kind_entity` widened, **no** explicit `LoanTerms` clause (the binding by elimination is pinned by a schema test; an explicit clause would be redundant and no mutation of it could turn a test red), the shape guard patched by `pg_get_functiondef` as 0067, `down` refusing while an acknowledgement of a new kind exists. **Alternatives (not taken):** (a) an explicit `LoanTerms` clause for readability (documented as redundant, without its own mutation); (b) the shape guard replaced as a whole by `CREATE OR REPLACE` (0065's text plus 0067's patch written out; one more place to keep in step).
10. **The recorded closing stub (found while specifying).** `interestPeriodOf` returns the schedule's period for a recorded period that §58O question 5 counts as matching the plan (`loan-interest-periods.ts:59`, `:94`), so a recorded stub from the day after the last kept entry to `closingDate` is not flagged but also not used (Example 2: the May stub stays in April's set). **Decided (as proposed):** fix it in VC-X-54's implementation, since Example 2's remedy depends on it: such a stub is used for the allocation with `source` `CLASSIFICATION` and no flag (§58O question 5's intent; precedence case 3 covers only a period **equal** to the plan); it can change figures only for recorded closing stubs (none productive). **Alternatives (not taken):** (a) a separate bug-fix PR before VC-X-54 (its own release note); (b) keep the code (the stub then has no effect, and the documentation of §58O question 5 is narrowed to "not flagged").
11. **Order, tests, ACC7 and ACC8.** **Decided (as proposed):** a PR of its own after VC-X-53 (decided order), one migration, its own e2e test `tax-year-loan-schedule-parts.e2e.test.ts`, ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged. **Alternative (not taken):** a step in ACC8 entering an interval after the year's end (ACC8's figures and its `review` change).

**Still open (owner):** none of questions 1–11 (decided 2026-11-05, above). The questions the implementation raises are under "As implemented (VC-X-54)".

# 58Q. Extending a Seller's Ownership up to the Economic Transfer (VC-X-55, implemented: migration 0072)

**Status:** **implemented** (VC-X-55, migration 0072; below, "As implemented (VC-X-55)"). Open questions 1–11 decided by the owner on 2026-11-05 (below, "Open questions (decided)"; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05): 1, 2, 4–8, 10 and 11 as proposed (1: option (A)), **3 and 9 differing** (the route at the Acquisition, `If-Match` on its version); the rule text below follows the decisions. Follow-up row **VC-X-57** (the buyers' Ownerships from `economicTransferDate` on `confirm`, so the case stops arising; specified in §58R and implemented with migration 0073; changes P2-D6 by ADR-044, accepted 2026-11-06). Since VC-X-57 this act covers legacy data and old drafts only, and an Acquisition confirmed from the transfer answers `OWNERSHIP_EXTENSION_NOT_APPLICABLE` `CONFIRMED_FROM_TRANSFER` (§58R rule 8). Backlog VC-X-55, created by the owner's decision on §58N open question 5 (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04). **Migration:** **0072** (`0072_ownership_extend_to_economic_transfer`; verified free at implementation: main d881d92 ends at 0071, VC-X-54's). Productive AfA recording stays disabled; nothing here touches it, and no unconfirmed tax assumption reads as released by it.

**What it amends:** §26.1 (its text names this command as the only path that ever extends a `validUntil` or moves a `validFrom`, decided question 3; "In the database (VC-2-03)": `ownership_frozen` admits exactly this change), §27.1 (`transferDate` = `ownershipStart` for an Acquisition whose Ownerships were aligned; the response gains `ownershipAlignedAt`, additive), §28.1A "The seller side" (the seller's row can reach the transfer), §58N "The rule for the Ownerships" (option (b) stays for every Acquisition not aligned by this command; for an aligned one the gap is closed and the flag no longer arises), §58E Part 2 (a new acknowledgement kind, open question 7), the invariant suite's ownership rows; migrations 0019/0020's `ownership_frozen`, 0050's `acquisition_confirmation_violation`/`acquisition_increase_violation` (the `d :=` lines as patched by 0067), 0067's `acquisition_frozen` and 0065's (as widened by 0067 and, if merged first, 0071) `tax_year_acknowledgement` CHECKs.

**Unchanged guarantees:** an Ownership's `share`, owner, PropertyReference and `acquisitionId` never change; `VOID` stays final; `close` never extends a period (`ALREADY_ENDED`, §26.1) and §26.2 never moves history; Σ ≤ 1 and no overlap per owner hold on every day, through the repository and past it (0019/0020's `ownership_invariants`). An Acquisition's data, statuses and `economicTransferDate` stay as §27.1 and §58N fix them. §58N's option (b) stays the rule for every Acquisition this command has not aligned. The anschaffungsnahe check (§58K, `DE_ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE@1`), the AfA rules and their pinned hashes, the buyers' AfA figures, §27.4's weights and parts, every property-level figure of the tax-year view, Realm isolation and §30.1's answers are unchanged. DE still writes no cash, no split and no classification.

**Why a section of its own, after §58P:** VC-X-55 is a backlog item of its own, created by §58N question 5; its number is the next free letter (verified: §58P is the last §58 letter on main d6f0095).

### The decided fact (verbatim)

Cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-04“ (the owner's answer on §58N open question 5, recorded in full in §58N "Open questions (decided)"):

> - **5: nicht nur informativ.** `OWNERSHIP_START_BEFORE_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` ist `OPEN`, sobald ein Verkäufer derselben Anschaffung im selben Realm eine AfA-Komponente hat, sonst `INFORMATIVE`. Das Review hat recht: zwischen Vertrag und Übergang bekäme sonst niemand AfA, und das ist eine falsche Zahl in DE, kein bloßer Hinweis. Bei einem externen Verkäufer rechnet DE nichts Falsches, also informativ. Das `OPEN` wird durch eine Quittierung über §58E Teil 2 geschlossen, neuer Kind `OWNERSHIP_START_BEFORE_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER`; damit bleibt Altbestand reparierbar. Dazu eine neue Backlog-Zeile für die eigentliche Korrektur: das Verlängern einer am `contractDate − 1` geschlossenen Verkäufer-Ownership bis zum Übergang mit Beleg, als Änderung von §26.1, denn heute kann das niemand.

And on §58N question 1 (the same answer): „**1: (b), wie vorgeschlagen.** Die Ownerships bleiben, das erfasste Datum startet nur Fenster und AfA, `ownershipStart` bleibt für alle heutigen Leser gleich, die Meldung nennt die Abweichung. (a) würde `ownership_frozen` zum ersten Mal lockern und Altbestand mit späteren Fakten unreparierbar lassen. P2-D6 (Beginn am Vertragsdatum) ist eine Modellentscheidung, die nicht nebenbei in VC-X-52 kippt.“

So four things are decided: **a correction exists** (not only the acknowledgement); **it extends a seller's Ownership closed on `contractDate − 1` up to the transfer**; **with evidence** („mit Beleg“); **as an amendment of §26.1**. The tax rule behind it is §59A's decided disposal year: the seller's AfA runs „up to the **transfer of economic ownership** (Nutzen und Lasten, Gefahr; R 7.4 Abs. 8 EStR), never the notarial date“ (§59A, decided 2026-10-31; the month counting for the seller confirmed by the tax review, §59A "Resolved by the tax review (2026-11-01)", Frage 4; mündlich bestätigt durch den Steuerberater, laut Projektinhaber am 2026-11-01). Everything else below (what happens to the buyers' rows, which rows the act covers, the route, the guards, the flags) was this section's proposal and is **decided by the owner on 2026-11-05** ("Open questions (decided)"; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05). The main point, question 1: extending the seller's row while the buyers' rows keep starting on the contract date is refused by Σ ≤ 1 on every day of the gap (below, "Why the seller's row cannot simply be extended"); decided: option (A), „Wirtschaftlicher Eigentümer bis `t` ist der Verkäufer, mit Miete und AfA.“

### As the code stands (main d6f0095; paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`)

- **No route extends a period.** `api/ownerships.ts` has create, read, `close`, `void`, the ownership change and the list (`:143`, `:172`, `:181`, `:202`, `:223`, `:257`). `planClose` (`domains/ownership/ownership.ts:128-134`) refuses a later day as `ALREADY_ENDED` (`:132`; "a close never extends a period"), and so does §26.2's plan (`domains/ownership/change.ts:77`).
- **The database refuses it.** `ownership_frozen` (0019 `:57-77`, replaced by 0020 `:24-45` with `acquisition_id`) keeps `valid_from` fixed (`:31-38`) and raises "validUntil is only set or moved earlier, never extended" (0020 `:39-41`) for every later or cleared `valid_until`, past the repository as through it. No marker, role or setting admits an exception.
- **Σ ≤ 1 and no overlap** (`ownership_invariants`, an `AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE` row trigger, 0019 `:80-133`, replaced by 0020 `:47-…`): on every written row it checks the per-owner overlap and the sum of shares on the row's `validFrom` and on every `validFrom` of another `VALID` row inside the row's period (a sum only rises where a period starts).
- **0050's predecessor guard** (`ownership_predecessor_of_confirmed`, 0050 `:171-209`) fires on an insert with an end, a void and **any moved end, an extension included**, and refuses it when a `VALID` row of the same owner starting on the old end + 1 carries a `CONFIRMED` Acquisition. That is a **buyer's** predecessor (§28.1A). A plain seller has no such successor row, so the guard does not freeze a seller's row; the backlog row's "0050's `ownership_predecessor_of_confirmed` freezes the seller's predecessor row once the purchase is confirmed" does not hold for a seller (corrected here and in the row). It does fire for a buyer's predecessor ending on `contractDate − 1` (question 2).
- **`ownershipStart`** (`domains/acquisition/acquisition.ts:78-81`): the contract date once `economicTransferRecordedAt` is set (VC-X-52), else `economicTransferDate ?? contractDate`. In the database the same `CASE` in 0050's two functions (0067 `:94`, `D_TO`) and in the allocation's default `effectiveDate` (`infrastructure/postgres/land-building-allocation-repository.ts:58`).
- **The seller's AfA ends on the row's end.** §59A's tenure is `continuousOwners` over the Party's rows (`domains/depreciation/purchase-tenure.ts:42-47`); the cut-off looks for a `CONFIRMED` Acquisition naming the Party as a seller whose `ownershipStart` is the day after the tenure's end (`buyerOn`, `:31-33`; `item-part.ts:159-161`), and `lastDay` is the tenure's end with `lastDaySource` `BUYER_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER_DATE` when that buyer has `economicTransferDate` (`:99-111`). For legacy data dated by §58N the tenure ends on `contractDate − 1`, the buyer is found by `ownershipStart` = `contractDate`, and the seller's last AfA month is the month of `contractDate − 1`. `recording-stage.ts:148` reads the sellers' `ownershipStart` the same way.
- **The buyers' AfA starts at the transfer** (`domains/depreciation/purchase-work.ts:144`, `start = a.economicTransferDate`), their `ownedFrom` is `ownershipStart` (`schedule.ts:118`). Between the two nobody gets AfA: the flag `OWNERSHIP_START_BEFORE_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` (`purchase-work.ts:294-301`; the level by `sellersWithAfaComponent`, `infrastructure/postgres/ownership-start-reads.ts:14-35`; the year flag over `[ownershipStart, economicTransferDate − 1]`, `domains/taxation/ownership-start-changes.ts:46-53`, facts from `ownershipStartFactsOf`, `ownership-start-reads.ts:41-55`).
- **The tax-year view's owners** take each item's participants on its share date (§58C; `participantsOn`, `domains/taxation/tax-year-shares.ts:51-…`). In the gap the buyers are the owners of every rent, expense and interest item, not the seller.
- **Ownership records are no change kind.** `CHANGE_KINDS` (`domains/taxation/attribution-rule.ts:8-18`) and `PART_CHANGE_KINDS` (`attribution-parts.ts:27-34`) name no Ownership record: an Ownership write after a year's end that moves the owners' parts of that year raises no flag today.

### Why the seller's row cannot simply be extended

The legacy state after §58N, for an Acquisition X with contract date `c`, recorded transfer `t > c`, seller S and buyer A: S's row ends on `c − 1`, A's row carrying X starts on `c`. Extending S's row to `t − 1` and leaving A's start on `c` (the outline's "the buyer's Ownership start unchanged", §58N's option (b)) puts S's sold share **and** A's bought share on every day of `[c, t − 1]`. On such a day the sum is (the other owners) + S's old share + A's new share = the sum on `c − 1` + `acquiredShare`. For a PropertyReference that was `COMPLETE` on `c − 1` that is `1 + acquiredShare > 1`: `ownership_invariants` refuses the update at A's `validFrom` `c` (`OWNERSHIP_TOTAL_EXCEEDS_ONE`, `details.date` = `c`). A seller who keeps a part (§28.1A: S `3/4` → S `1/4` from `c`) is refused earlier, as `OVERLAPPING_OWNERSHIP` with S's own remainder row. It is consistent only when the PropertyReference lacked at least `acquiredShare` on `c − 1`, which no real purchase recorded by WF-002 produces.

So **under option (b) the decided correction is impossible**, whatever guard is relaxed, unless Σ ≤ 1 itself is given up for the gap. This section therefore moves the buyers' start to the transfer **in the same act** (question 1, decided: (A)); option (b) of §58N stays for every Acquisition the act is not applied to. The alternatives not taken are listed with question 1.

### The rule (decided: option (A), question 1)

**A command on an Acquisition whose `economicTransferDate` was recorded later (§58N) extends every seller Ownership that ended on `contractDate − 1` to `economicTransferDate − 1`, with evidence; in the same act the buyers' Ownerships carrying the Acquisition start on `economicTransferDate`, so the shares sum to the same value on every day as before the purchase until the transfer, and `ownershipStart` becomes the transfer.**

1. **Only that exact case.** For the Acquisition X in the path (decided question 3: the route at the Acquisition, since the act moves several rows of X at once and `validUntil` follows from X):
   - X is of the caller's Realm, not `CANCELLED` (`DRAFT` or `CONFIRMED`, question 4);
   - X's `economicTransferDate` `t` was **recorded later** (`economicTransferRecordedAt` set, §58N) and `t > contractDate` `c` (with `t = c` there is no gap);
   - X is **not yet aligned** (`ownershipAlignedAt` `null`);
   - at least one `VALID` row of X's PropertyReference held by a **seller** of X ends on `c − 1` (otherwise moving the buyers' start alone would open a gap with nobody on it);
   - the new end of every extended row is `t − 1`, derived from X; the client sends no date.
2. **The act** (one transaction, all or nothing), its rows fixed from the state under the locks:
   - **(i) every seller row of X**: each `VALID` row of the PropertyReference whose owner is a seller of X and whose `validUntil` is `c − 1`: `validUntil` → `t − 1`, all at once, since extending one seller alone leaves the other's share missing on `[c, t − 1]` (question 2). A seller of X without such a row (an owner DE never recorded) has nothing to extend.
   - **(ii) every buyer row of X**: each `VALID` row carrying X (by §28.1 requirement 2 they all start on `c`): `validFrom` → `t`.
   - **(iii) every buyer predecessor**: each `VALID` row of a buyer of X ending on `c − 1` (§28.1A: A held `1/2` before buying `1/2`): `validUntil` → `t − 1`, so the buyer's held share on `t − 1` and with it `acquired_P` (§28.1A), §27.4's weights and §59A's share bought stay what they were (question 2).
   - **(iv) the Acquisition**: `ownershipAlignedAt` set (the act's time), the evidence stored (question 5), `version` + 1. From then on **`ownershipStart(X)` = `t`** (below).
3. **The write order** (as §26.2's, review on #44, so every intermediate state satisfies the invariants): (iv) first, then (ii) the buyers' starts moved later (sums on `[c, t − 1]` only fall), then (i) and (iii) the ends moved later (sums on `[c, t − 1]` rise back to the value of `c − 1`, which was ≤ 1), each group in `id` order. Under this order 0050's predecessor guard does not fire for (iii): it looks for a successor starting on the **old** end + 1, `c`, and the buyer's row already starts on `t`; for every later write the guard protects the new predecessor (end `t − 1`, successor from `t`), as §28.1A intends.
4. **Refused while a later fact rests on the old dates** (`422 OWNERSHIP_EXTENSION_BLOCKED`, `details.blockedBy`, every blocker listed, by code then id):
   - `SELLER_KEEPS_PART` (`ownershipId`): a seller of X holds a `VALID` row starting on `c` (§28.1A's "a seller who keeps a part"; question 2);
   - `SELLER_ROW_IN_GAP` (`ownershipId`, `validFrom`): a seller of X holds a `VALID` row starting in `[c + 1, t − 1]` (bought back before the transfer): the extension would overlap it;
   - `BUYER_ROW_ENDS_BEFORE_TRANSFER` (`ownershipId`, `validUntil`): a buyer's row carrying X ends before `t` (resold inside the gap); its start cannot move past its end. A buyer's row ending on or after `t` is moved; its successors are untouched;
   - `BUYER_PREDECESSOR_NOT_ADJACENT` (`partyId`): a buyer of X held a share on `c − 1` by a row not ending on `c − 1` (a broken state that §28.1A's 5a/5b would already report);
   - **after the plan, the invariants over the state after the act** (§26.1: `OVERLAPPING_OWNERSHIP`, `OWNERSHIP_TOTAL_EXCEEDS_ONE`, with their details; a change of another owner inside the gap that the act would contradict is caught here), and, for a `CONFIRMED` X, **requirements 2–6 of §28.1 re-checked on `t`** (with §28.1A's 5a/5b): `blockedBy` `[{ code: "CONFIRMATION_REQUIREMENTS", violations }]` in `CONFIRMATION_BLOCKED`'s format. Requirement 1 (buyers active) is not re-checked: a buyer inactive since stays a buyer (P2-D1). The completeness on `t − 1` and on `t` equals the state before (a check, not a new rule: a refusal here is a bug).
   - **Not a blocker:** a land/building allocation of X whose `effectiveDate` is `c` (no AfA or check reads it: `domains/depreciation` and `tax-year-depreciation.ts` never read `effective_date`; it stays as recorded); an `ACTIVE` acknowledgement of `OWNERSHIP_START_BEFORE_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` (question 8); a recorded schedule version (§60; question 6); a change of another owner inside the gap that the invariants accept.
5. **`ownershipStart`, amended:** `economicTransferDate` once `ownershipAlignedAt` is set; else the contract date once `economicTransferRecordedAt` is set (§58N); else `economicTransferDate ?? contractDate` (P2-D6). Every reader of §58N's list reads it unchanged (confirm, 0050's functions, §27.4, §59A's `ownedFrom` and the seller's cut-off, `recording-stage.ts`, the listing of a purchase, the allocation's default `effectiveDate`, §27.1's `transferDate`). For an aligned X `ownershipStart = economicTransferDate`, so `OWNERSHIP_START_BEFORE_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` no longer arises (below).
6. **History:** nothing is voided or recreated; the rows keep their ids, shares and `acquisitionId`. Each moved row has an AuditRecord with its old and new date, so `GET …/ownerships` (the full history) shows the corrected periods and the AuditRecords show what they were.

### The command

```text
POST /api/v1/acquisitions/{acquisitionId}/align-ownerships-to-transfer
```

(Decided question 3, differing from the proposal: the route at the Acquisition. „Der Akt bewegt mehrere Zeilen von X auf einmal; eine Route an einer einzelnen Ownership-Zeile täuscht eine Einzelkorrektur vor und braucht `validUntil`, das sich aus X ergibt.“ Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05.)

- **Domain owner:** Acquisition (the act and its `ownershipAlignedAt`), writing X's Ownerships in the same transaction (as §26.2 writes Ownerships for an Acquisition); §26.1's text names this command as the only path that extends a `validUntil`. **Authorization:** as §27.1; X and every row the act touches belong to the caller's Realm.
- **Body** (strict; unknown keys `400`; no date: every new date follows from X):
  - `sourceReferences` (1–10 strings of 1–500, trimmed as §26.1, **at least one**, `400 REQUIRED` for an empty or missing list): the evidence that the seller held Nutzen und Lasten until the transfer (e.g. „Übergabeprotokoll, Abschnitt 2 (synthetisch)“); new, not the date's evidence reused (question 5);
  - `notes` (≤ 2000, optional), recorded in the AuditRecords only.
- **Order of checks** (the first refusal answers; nothing is written):
  1. `400` (body, id);
  2. X unknown or foreign → `404` (`details.acquisitionId`);
  3. X `CANCELLED` → `409 CONFLICT` with `reason = "ACQUISITION_CANCELLED"` (also with a stale `If-Match`, a final status answers before the version, as §28.1 and §58N);
  4. X already aligned → `409 CONFLICT` with `reason = "OWNERSHIPS_ALREADY_ALIGNED"` and `details: { acquisitionId, ownershipAlignedAt, ownershipStart }` (also for a retry with the same body: the act is never applied twice);
  5. `If-Match` (§16.1, optional) on **X's** version → `412` (decided question 9);
  6. `422 OWNERSHIP_EXTENSION_NOT_APPLICABLE` with `details.reason`, the first of: `TRANSFER_DATE_NOT_RECORDED` (X's date was set on create or is missing: its rows already start on the transfer, or there is no transfer to extend to), `TRANSFER_ON_CONTRACT_DATE` (`t = c`), `NO_SELLER_ROW` (no `VALID` row of a seller of X ends on `c − 1`);
  7. `422 OWNERSHIP_EXTENSION_BLOCKED` with `details.blockedBy` (rule 4).
- **Success:** `200` with `{ acquisition, extended: [Ownership…], moved: [Ownership…], completeness, shareSum }` (`acquisition` as §27.1 with `ownershipStart` = `t`, `ownershipAlignedAt` and `version` + 1, `ETag: "<version>"` of X; the Ownerships as §26.1, each with `version` + 1, in `id` order; `completeness` and `shareSum` for `t − 1`, equal to those of `c − 1` before).
- **AuditRecords** (each with `acquisitionId`, `sourceReferences`, `notes`): `EXTENDED_TO_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` on each extended row (old and new `validUntil`), `START_MOVED_TO_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` on each moved buyer row (old and new `validFrom`), and one `OWNERSHIPS_ALIGNED_TO_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` on the Acquisition with `contractDate`, `economicTransferDate`, the old and new `ownershipStart`, the status and the ids of every row, so the act reads as one (as §26.2's `OWNERSHIP_CHANGED`). None on a refusal, none on a read.
- **Idempotency (§15):** `Idempotency-Key` with scope `acquisition.align-ownerships-to-transfer`, fingerprint of the Acquisition id and the normalized body (texts trimmed, `sourceReferences` as given). Replay `200` with the recorded body and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; another payload with the same key `409`. Without a key a retry answers step 4's `409`.
- **Concurrency and locks** (one READ COMMITTED transaction, the order of every Ownership writer, §26.1/§27.1): claim the key → the PropertyReference's no-op write → the buyers and sellers of X `FOR SHARE` in id order (nothing is checked on them; the order only) → X `FOR UPDATE` → every Ownership of the PropertyReference held by a buyer or seller of X `FOR UPDATE` in id order → re-read → plan → write (rule 3) → AuditRecords → record the key. So it serialises with `confirm`, `cancel` and §58N's command (same Acquisition lock), with cost, payment and allocation writes (they write X's row) and with every Ownership write of the PropertyReference (they take it first). A `confirm` of a `DRAFT` X that comes first is seen (the act then re-checks requirements 2–6 on `t`); one that waits confirms on `ownershipStart` = `t`.

### Effects

- **`OWNERSHIP_START_BEFORE_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` closes by itself.** `ownershipStart(X) = economicTransferDate`, so `ownershipStartFlag` raises nothing on X's read and on §59A's component, and `ownershipStartFactsOf` reads no aligned Acquisition (its filter gains `ownership_aligned_at IS NULL`): the year flag disappears from every year of the former gap, `OPEN` or `INFORMATIVE`. No acknowledgement is needed; one given before stays stored and counts nowhere (question 8).
- **The seller's AfA in the gap** (§59A, rules unchanged): S's tenure ends on `t − 1`; the cut-off finds X by `ownershipStart` = `t`, which has `economicTransferDate`, so `lastDay` = `t − 1`, `lastDaySource` `BUYER_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER_DATE`, the disposal year that of `t − 1` with its months by `endMonthCounts` (the month of `t − 1` in full). The months between the contract and the transfer, which nobody had, are S's. A **gap across a year end** moves S's disposal year (contract 2024-12-01, transfer 2025-02-01: before, 2024 the disposal year with 11 months; after, 2024 in full and 2025 with 1 month). The buyers' AfA is unchanged in every figure: their start was `t` already, and `ownedFrom` moving from `c` to `t` adds no month (none before the start counted).
- **§27.4, §28.1A, §59A's shares:** every share, `acquired_P`, weight and part unchanged (rule 2 (iii) keeps the buyers' day-before shares). `OWNER_WITHOUT_ACQUISITION` cannot arise from the act (the buyers hold nothing they did not buy, from `t` on).
- **The tax-year view** (§58C), in each year touching `[c, t − 1]`:
  - **the owners' parts move:** every item whose share date lies in the gap now belongs to the seller (and the buyers' predecessor shares), not to the buyers; the property's figures, `NOT_OWNED` and the sum over the owners are unchanged to the cent (rent, expenses, interest, WEG; only who holds them);
  - **the seller's AfA** gains the gap's months (above); the AfA section of the property changes by exactly that, the buyers' by nothing;
  - **the purchase's listing year** (`tax-year-depreciation.ts:248-258`, by `ownershipStart`) moves to `t`'s year where `c` and `t` are in different years; X has no AfA before `t`, so no figure moves by it;
  - **"an owner in the year"** (§58C, `NOT_AN_OWNER_IN_YEAR`): the seller becomes one in `t − 1`'s year; a buyer whose only days of a year were in the gap no longer is (contract in December, transfer in January).
  - These are figures of past years moved by a record after their end, and no change kind covers Ownership records: **question 7** (decided: a year flag of its own, open where the year had ended before the act).
- **The change flags of §58E, §58G–§58J and §58P:** not raised by the act itself (no item's year moves; no property part moves); their kinds are unchanged. VC-X-54's kinds (0071) and this section's (question 7) widen the same CHECK; the later migration carries both lists.
- **The anschaffungsnahe check** (§58K): unchanged; its window starts on `economicTransferDate`, which the act does not touch.
- **Recorded schedule versions** (§60): the act changes owner parts of the seller's component (`lastDay`, the fractions of the gap's months) and the buyers' `tenure_from` (`c` → `t`), so `inputFingerprint` of every year from `c`'s year changes and a version recorded before shows `DEPRECIATION_CHANGED_SINCE_RECORDED` (open) until a new one supersedes it (§60, "an Ownership change that changes an owner part"). Not refused (question 6, decided). Productively no version exists (recording disabled).

### Example (synthetic)

PropertyReference P, building completed 1990 (2 % by `DE_AFA_BUILDING_LINEAR`, §59A). **Acquisition W:** seller none, buyer S, `contractDate` 2015-06-01, `economicTransferDate` 2015-07-01 (entered on create), confirmed; S's row O_S `"1/1"` from 2015-07-01 carrying W; building part 120,000.00, so S's AfA 2,400.00 a year (200.00 a month). **Acquisition L** (§58N's example): buyer A, seller S, `acquiredShare` `"1/1"`, `contractDate` **2025-03-01**, confirmed before VC-X-34 without the date, building part 160,000.00 (3,200.00 a year). O_S closed on **2025-02-28**, A's O_A `"1/1"` from 2025-03-01 carrying L. Rent 1,000.00 a month, each paid on the 3rd (share date, §58C). On **2026-01-15** §58N's command recorded `economicTransferDate` **2025-05-01** with „Übergabeprotokoll 2025-05-01 (synthetisch)“.

- **Before VC-X-55, year 2025:** S's AfA (W) 2 months = **400.00** (`lastDay` 2025-02-28); A's AfA (L) May–December 8/12 = **2,133.33**; nobody in March and April (10 months of 12 depreciated). Rent: S 2,000.00 (January, February), A 10,000.00, P 12,000.00. `OWNERSHIP_START_BEFORE_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` `OPEN` in 2025 (S holds O_S carrying W), not final until acknowledged.
- **The command** on **2026-02-10**: `POST /acquisitions/L/align-ownerships-to-transfer` with `{ "sourceReferences": ["Übergabeprotokoll 2025-05-01, Abschnitt 2 (synthetisch)"] }` → `200`: O_S `validUntil` 2025-02-28 → **2025-04-30** (`EXTENDED_TO_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER`), O_A `validFrom` 2025-03-01 → **2025-05-01** (`START_MOVED_TO_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER`), L `ownershipAlignedAt` set, `ownershipStart` and `transferDate` **2025-05-01** (`OWNERSHIPS_ALIGNED_TO_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER`); `completeness` `COMPLETE`, `shareSum` `"1/1"` on 2025-04-30 as on 2025-02-28 before.
- **After, year 2025:** S's AfA 4 months = **800.00** (`lastDay` 2025-04-30, `BUYER_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER_DATE`); A's **2,133.33** unchanged; 12 months of 12. Rent: S **4,000.00**, A **8,000.00**, P **12,000.00** unchanged. `OWNERSHIP_START_BEFORE_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` gone; by question 7 (decided) `OWNERSHIP_EXTENDED_TO_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER` open in 2025 (the act lies after 2025-12-31) until acknowledged. §27.4 for L: `CONFIRMED`, A weight `1/1`, every part unchanged.
- **Unchanged:** 2024 in every figure (S 2,400.00 AfA, 12,000.00 rent); 2026 in every figure (A 3,200.00, S none); the check of L (window 2025-05-01 – 2028-05-01); P's property-level figures of 2025 except the AfA section (+400.00, S's part).
- **An existing owner buying (§28.1A):** A `1/2` (W1) and S `1/2` (W2) until 2025-02-28, A `1/1` (X) from 2025-03-01, X's transfer recorded as 2025-05-01. The act extends S's row **and** A's `1/2` predecessor to 2025-04-30 and moves A's `1/1` to 2025-05-01; `acquired_A` = `1/1 − 1/2` = `1/2` before and after; A's tenure stays continuous (no disposal for A).
- **Counter-examples:** a second call → `409 OWNERSHIPS_ALREADY_ALIGNED`; `If-Match: "1"` on L at version 2 → `412`; an L whose seller has no recorded row (S's row voided as a recording error before) → `422 NO_SELLER_ROW`; an Acquisition created with `economicTransferDate` 2025-05-01 → `422 TRANSFER_DATE_NOT_RECORDED`; a seller keeping `1/4` from 2025-03-01 → `422 OWNERSHIP_EXTENSION_BLOCKED` `SELLER_KEEPS_PART`; A resold to C on 2025-04-01 → `BUYER_ROW_ENDS_BEFORE_TRANSFER` (O_A ends 2025-03-31); a cancelled L → `409 ACQUISITION_CANCELLED`; Realm B → `404`.

### Migration (the next free number at implementation; 0072 at the time of writing)

`0072_ownership_extend_to_economic_transfer` (question 10, decided as proposed):

- **`acquisition`:** `ownership_aligned_at` (`timestamptz`, `NULL`) and the evidence column of question 5 (`ownership_alignment_source_references` `text[]`); CHECK `acquisition_ownership_alignment`: the two set together, only with `economic_transfer_recorded_at IS NOT NULL` and `economic_transfer_date > contract_date`; the evidence 1–10 entries, none `NULL` or empty (as 0067's). No backfill: every existing row stays `NULL`.
- **`acquisition_frozen`** (0067's text, patched by `pg_get_functiondef` as 0067 does, the passage checked to occur once): admits exactly one more change, the two columns from `NULL` to set on a `DRAFT` or `CONFIRMED` row with a recorded date after the contract date, no status step, `version` + 1, nothing else; refuses any other change of them (also back to `NULL`).
- **`ownership_frozen`** (0020's function, replaced): `valid_from` may move from `c` to `t`, and `valid_until` may move from `c − 1` to `t − 1`, **only** where an Acquisition X of the row's Realm and PropertyReference with `ownership_aligned_at IS NOT NULL`, `contract_date = c` and `economic_transfer_date = t` exists and the row is X's (for `valid_from`: `acquisition_id = X`; for `valid_until`: the owner is a seller of X, or a buyer of X and the row is not X's). The state is read, not a session setting: past the repository the change is the act itself (X aligned first, rule 3), and it is one-shot by construction (afterwards no row ends on `c − 1` or starts on `c` by X). Every other rule of 0020's function, `VOID` final, the fixed fields and "never extended" for every other row, is unchanged.
- **The act's consistency at commit:** a deferred constraint trigger `ownership_alignment_complete` on `acquisition` (when `ownership_aligned_at` is set) and on `ownership` (when a date of a row of an aligned X moves) checks at commit, for every aligned X written in the transaction: no `VALID` row carries X with `valid_from ≠ economic_transfer_date`; no `VALID` row of a seller of X ends on `c − 1`; for a `CONFIRMED` X `acquisition_increase_violation(X) IS NULL` (§28.1A's 5a/5b on `t`). So neither half of the act commits alone, past the repository either. `ownership_invariants` stays the guarantee of Σ ≤ 1 and no overlap on every row.
- **`ownershipStart` in the database:** 0050's two functions' `d :=` line (0067's `D_TO`) and the allocation's default read gain the aligned case first (`CASE WHEN a.ownership_aligned_at IS NOT NULL THEN a.economic_transfer_date WHEN a.economic_transfer_recorded_at IS NOT NULL THEN a.contract_date ELSE coalesce(…) END`), patched as 0067 patched them.
- **`tax_year_acknowledgement`** (question 7): the kind CHECK gains `OWNERSHIP_EXTENDED_TO_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER`, `kind_entity`'s `Acquisition` clause widened to both Acquisition kinds, the shape guard refuses any item of it (0067's pattern). The list is the one on main at implementation (0071's kinds included if VC-X-54 is merged first).
- **No index:** the guard's lookups use `acquisition`'s primary key and `acquisition_party`'s key; a repository test reads the plan.
- **`down`:** refuses (`23514`, before changing anything) while a row has `ownership_aligned_at` or an acknowledgement of the new kind exists (the moved dates cannot be restored without their marker, and 0020's guard could no longer tell them from an extension); otherwise restores 0020's `ownership_frozen`, 0067's `acquisition_frozen`, 0050's functions as 0067 left them and the CHECKs verbatim, drops the trigger and the columns. The down chains of the later tests (0067's `acquisition-transfer-date.test.ts`, 0071's) run 0072's first.

### Interaction with the other sections

- **§58N:** option (b) stays the default for every Acquisition; the act is an explicit, evidenced correction per Acquisition. An aligned Acquisition reads as one created with its date (`ownershipStart = economicTransferDate`), except that its history shows the moved rows.
- **§28.1A's guard:** after the act it protects the buyers' new predecessors (end `t − 1`); the act itself passes it by its write order (rule 3), which a test pins.
- **§26.2:** unchanged; a later sale ends the moved rows as any other. A §26.2 change dated inside `[c, t − 1]` written before the act is caught by the invariants or by `BUYER_ROW_ENDS_BEFORE_TRANSFER`.
- **VC-X-54 (§58P):** independent; both widen the acknowledgement kind CHECK, the later migration carries both lists.

### Tests the implementation needs

- **Domain (pure):** the plan: each condition of rule 1 alone and the first of two in the order of checks (`409` before `412` for a cancelled X, `412` on a stale X version and none without `If-Match`); a seller row ending one day before or after `c − 1` not extended (`NO_SELLER_ROW` when it is the only one), the new end exactly `t − 1`; `t = c + 1` (a one-day gap); a gap across a year end (2024-12-01 → 2025-02-01) and a transfer on 1 March of a leap year (`t − 1` = 29 February); two sellers (both extended); an external seller without a row beside one with a row; the buyer predecessor (§28.1A) extended; each blocker of rule 4 alone, and all at once listed in order; `ownershipStart` for undated, created-with-date, recorded and aligned Acquisitions; the flag gone once aligned.
- **§59A (pure):** the example: S 400.00 → 800.00, `lastDaySource` `BUYER_ECONOMIC_TRANSFER_DATE` before and after, A 2,133.33 unchanged in every year; the year-end gap (S's disposal year moves from 2024 to 2025, A's figures equal); the §28.1A case (A's W1 component without a disposal, X computed in full); **unchanged money sums:** a seeded property test over purchases, gaps and shares: the buyers' figures byte-identical before and after, the seller's figures equal outside the gap's months, every component's parts summing as before.
- **Tax-year view (pure and PostgreSQL):** the example's 2025 owners (S 4,000.00 / A 8,000.00 rent), P's property figures byte-identical except the AfA section, 2024 and 2026 byte-identical in every figure, `owners` plus `NOT_OWNED` summing to the property's to the cent; `NOT_AN_OWNER_IN_YEAR` for a buyer with only gap days in a year; the flag of question 7 (open after the year's end, informative before, closed by its acknowledgement, opened again by a withdrawal).
- **Repository (PostgreSQL):** the example end to end through the repository (versions + 1 on each row and on L, the three AuditRecords with old and new dates and the evidence, none on a refusal or a read); every refusal writing nothing; idempotent replay and a key with another payload; **Realm isolation:** L of Realm B `404`, Realm B's identical legacy data unchanged and still flagged; **history:** the full history read shows the moved periods, the AuditRecords the old ones; concurrency (RC): the act against `confirm` of a `DRAFT` (both orders), against a `close` and a §26.2 change of the PropertyReference, against §58N's command on a second Acquisition, two acts at once (the second `409 OWNERSHIPS_ALREADY_ALIGNED`).
- **Past the repository (0072), each with a counter-check (the guard neutralised, the test red) and a mutation:** a raw extension of a seller's row without an aligned X (refused "never extended"; counter-check: with X aligned in the same transaction it passes); a raw extension to a day other than `t − 1`; a raw extension of a row ending on another day than `c − 1`; a raw `valid_from` move of a row not carrying X, or to a day other than `t`; a raw alignment without moving the rows (refused at commit by `ownership_alignment_complete`; counter-check: with the rows moved it commits); the rows moved in the wrong order (the seller first: `OWNERSHIP_TOTAL_EXCEEDS_ONE`, the reason for rule 3); `ownership_aligned_at` set on a `CANCELLED` row, on one without a recorded date, with `t = c`, back to `NULL`, with a status step, without `version` + 1, without evidence; 0050's guard still refusing a void of a buyer's new predecessor after the act; the acknowledgement kind with another entity and with an item refused; `down` refused with an aligned row or an acknowledgement, otherwise restoring every function and CHECK verbatim (`pg_get_functiondef` / `pg_get_constraintdef` against a schema migrated to 0071), then `up` again; an existing legacy row untouched by `up` and `down`.
- **API:** the route's body (strict, `REQUIRED` evidence, a `validUntil` key `400` as unknown), the order of checks, the response shape with X's `ETag`, `412` on a stale X version, `409` before `412` for a cancelled X.
- **End to end:** a new `acquisition-align-ownerships.e2e.test.ts` (synthetic values, a settable clock): the example over HTTP (W, legacy L inserted by `insertConfirmedAsBeforeVcX34`, §58N's command, the views 2024–2026 before and after at both levels, the act, the flags, the acknowledgement of question 7), the §28.1A case, Realm B `404`, no cash mutated. ACC7 and ACC8 unchanged (every Acquisition of both is dated on create).
