# 58S. Data Export: the Kassenbuch as CSV and a Property as JSON (VC-X-04, implemented)

**Status:** **implemented** (VC-X-04, no migration, PR #290, not merged; below, "As implemented (VC-X-04)"); specified and decided 2026-11-06. **Open questions 1–13 decided by the owner on 2026-11-06** (chat; "Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (chat)" under "Open questions (decided)" at the end of this section): 1 and 4–13 as proposed; 2 and 3, which belong together, differing: the default CSV stays RFC 4180 with `,`, decimal point and no BOM and is written character for character, **without** a formula guard; a second dialect `dialect=excel-de` (`;`, decimal comma, BOM, the same columns) carries the formula guard ("`dialect`" below). The body below is amended accordingly. Implementation after VC-X-12, without a migration (the owner's order: „VC-X-57 zu Ende, VC-X-12 mit 0074, dann VC-X-04 ohne Migration.“). Backlog VC-X-04 (constitution Art. I "Data must always remain exportable"; ADR-030 "Open Data Formats and Exportability"; `technology.md` §35 "Exportability": JSON for structured complete exports, CSV for tabular financial data, stable identifiers kept). Go-live checklist issue #281, item 2. **Migration:** none. **Routes:** two new `GET` routes, nothing else changes. Productive AfA recording stays disabled; nothing here touches it, and no unconfirmed tax assumption reads as released by it (no tax figure is exported).

**What it adds:** `GET /api/v1/exports/transactions.csv` (the Realm's Kassenbuch, §30.1's filters) and `GET /api/v1/property-references/{propertyReferenceId}/export.json` (one PropertyReference with its Ownerships, Acquisitions, Loans, WEG memberships and deposits). The UI guide (`docs/development/ui-guide.md` §3.1 and §6.1) lists both as a P1 function (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-06).

**Unchanged guarantees:** every existing route, response, filter and error code is unchanged; §30.1's list, its order, its paging and its query plan (VC-X-19) are unchanged. Both exports only read: no write, no AuditRecord, no MRE call, no `Idempotency-Key`. Money is never a float (§86, §31.2; in `dialect=excel-de` the decimal point becomes a comma as a string operation, the digits unchanged), shares stay exact fractions (§87), dates stay `YYYY-MM-DD` and timestamps RFC 3339 (§88), in both CSV dialects. Realm isolation is that of the reads (§9, §30.1, §23.3). No figure, sum or rule is computed anew: every value comes from an existing DTO or from a column the DTO already shows.

**Why a section of its own, after §58R:** VC-X-04 is a cross-cutting backlog item of its own; §58S is the next free letter (verified on main ddeb373 and on every remote branch: §58R is the last §58 letter, no branch adds §58S; §58R itself stays untouched).

### The decided facts (verbatim)

Issue #281, item 2: „`GET /api/v1/exports/transactions.csv` (Kassenbuch, Realm, Filter wie §30.1) und `GET /api/v1/property-references/{id}/export.json` (Objekt mit Ownerships, Anschaffung, Darlehen, Mitgliedschaften, Kaution); Spec-PR, dann Implementierung.“

Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-06: „**P1-Ergänzung im UI-Leitfaden: freigegeben.** In §3.1 eine Zeile „Export | CSV des Kassenbuchs, JSON je Objekt | P1“ und in §6.1 die Zeile „Export | Direkt, sobald VC-X-04 umgesetzt ist | Routen aus der Spec“. Das kann mit dem Spec-PR zum Export gehen.“ … „**Reihenfolge wie von dir genannt:** VC-X-57 zu Ende, parallel der Spec-PR zum Export, danach Backup und Proxy.“

### As the code stands (main ddeb373; paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`)

- **The list:** `api/transactions.ts:40` (`GET /transactions`) parses `listQuery` (`api/transaction-dto.ts`, `listFields` and `listFilter`) and calls `PostgresTransactionQueryRepository.list` (`infrastructure/postgres/transaction-query-repository.ts:66`), which builds the filter in `filtered`, counts and pages in one `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` snapshot, newest booking first. A foreign `financialAccountId` / `propertyReferenceId` filter is an empty page there (the Realm condition in `filtered`). A malformed one never reaches it: `listFields` refuses it first with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`RESOURCE_ID`, `api/validation.ts:7`); the repository's own UUID checks (`:69–70`) only guard other callers.
- **The DTOs:** `toDto` and `toSplitDto` (`api/transaction-dto.ts`) carry every Transaction and split field below; `counterpartyNameRaw` and `counterpartyIbanRaw` are in the DTO (§30.1's "no counterparty fields yet" refers to a filter only). Money is `Money.amount`, a fixed-scale string (`shared/money.ts:160`, `"1250.00"`), at most 18 integer digits (`MAX_INTEGER_DIGITS`).
- **The property reads:** §23.3 (`api/property-references.ts:143`), §26.1 without `asOf` (the full history, `VOID` included), §27.1/§27.2/§27.3, §41.1–§41.3 and §41.6 (`GET /property-references/{id}/loans` leaves `VOID` Loans out), §49.1/§49.2 (`GET /property-references/{id}/weg-memberships`), §47.1/§47.3 (the single read with `cash`), §19.1 (Parties). A deposit has no PropertyReference of its own; §58A's rule derives it ("The deposit's PropertyReference", `infrastructure/postgres/mover-reads.ts:32`).
- **Nothing exports yet:** no route answers anything but JSON; no route streams.

### The rule (decided 2026-11-06)

**Both exports are reads of the caller's Realm in one `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` snapshot, built from the existing DTOs and filters, never from new figures. The CSV is by default RFC 4180 in UTF-8, written character for character; on request (`dialect=excel-de`) it is the same columns for a German spreadsheet, with `;`, decimal comma, BOM and the formula guard. The JSON is one document with a format name and version. Neither includes AuditRecords; both include every status, `VOID`, `CANCELLED`, `CORRECTED`, `IGNORED` and reversals marked as such, unless a filter says otherwise.**

### Access, Realm and the 404 rule (both routes)

- **Auth:** behind `requireDeAccess` like every business route (`Authorization: Bearer <MRE token>`, `organizationid: <mreRealmId>`; `mre-integration.md` §47.2). Its answers (`401`, `403`, `503 AUTH_UNAVAILABLE`) are unchanged and JSON (§12). Every role with DE access may export: the exports show nothing the reads do not already show to it (open question 12 for the contact data).
- **Realm:** every row is selected by `mre_realm_id` first; a child row is only reached through a parent of the Realm (composite foreign keys). Another Realm's rows are never read, also not to count them.
- **404 rule:** a **path** id that is unknown or foreign is `404 NOT_FOUND` with `details.propertyReferenceId` (the JSON route; existence is never revealed, §23.3). A **filter** id that is unknown or foreign matches nothing, as in §30.1: the CSV is the header line only, not a `404`. A malformed id is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` in both places.
- **No MRE call:** both answer from DE's rows (`displayName` and `cachedAddress` are the cached, non-authoritative values of §23.3). A test asserts the fake MRE's call count is unchanged.
- **Headers on success:** `Cache-Control: no-store` (personal data: counterparty names, IBANs, contact data); `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="…"` (below); `X-Export-Generated-At` (RFC 3339, UTC, milliseconds: the snapshot's start as the server clock reads it); `X-Export-Format` (below). No `ETag`.

### `GET /api/v1/exports/transactions.csv`

- **Query:** exactly §30.1's filters, parsed by the same schema (`listFields` without `page` and `pageSize`): `financialAccountId`, `status`, `provenance`, `reviewable`, `current`, `propertyReferenceId`, `financialCategoryCode`, `bookingDateFrom`, `bookingDateTo`, with §30.1's meanings, combinations and refusals (`400 INVALID_RANGE` when inverted, `400` for an unknown value). Two parameters of its own: `rows` = `transactions` (default) or `splits` (open question 1, decided as proposed); `dialect` = `rfc4180` (default) or `excel-de` (open questions 2 and 3, decided; "`dialect`" below). `page` and `pageSize` are unknown parameters here (`400`): the export is the whole filtered set. The filter is built by the **same function** as §30.1's list (`filtered`, moved to a module both read), so the two never diverge.
- **What history:** without `status` or `current`, every Transaction of the filter, as §30.1's raw list: `CORRECTED` originals, reversals, replacements and `IGNORED` ones included, each with its `status` and `correctionRole` (open question 5). `current=true` gives the current Transactions of §35.3; summing their `signedAmount` gives the net effect per account and period. Transactions are never deleted, so nothing "voided" is missing. **No AuditRecords** (open question 8): the amendments of an unconfirmed Transaction are not in the file, only its current values; a confirmed one is never changed, only corrected, and the correction chain is in the rows. `include` is an unknown parameter in version 1 (`400`); `?include=audit` is later work ("Later work" below).
- **Rows:** `rows=transactions`: one row per Transaction. `rows=splits`: one row per split, the Transaction's columns repeated on each; a Transaction without splits is one row with empty split columns. Split rows of one Transaction are consecutive, in `position` order.
- **Columns, in this order** (the header names are the DTO's field names, open question 6):

  | # | Column | Value |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | `transactionId` | UUID, lower case |
  | 2 | `bookingDate` | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
  | 3 | `valueDate` | `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty |
  | 4 | `financialAccountId` | UUID |
  | 5 | `direction` | `INFLOW` / `OUTFLOW` |
  | 6 | `amount` | the non-negative amount, e.g. `1250.00` |
  | 7 | `signedAmount` | `amount`, with `-` for `OUTFLOW` (`-312.40`); `0.00` never signed |
  | 8 | `currency` | `EUR` |
  | 9 | `status` | as the DTO |
  | 10 | `provenance` | as the DTO |
  | 11 | `description` | text or empty |
  | 12 | `counterpartyNameRaw` | text or empty |
  | 13 | `counterpartyIbanRaw` | text or empty |
  | 14 | `propertyReferenceId` | the Transaction's own, or empty |
  | 15 | `splitCount` | integer ≥ 0 |
  | 16 | `correctionOfTransactionId` | UUID or empty |
  | 17 | `correctionRole` | `REVERSAL` / `REPLACEMENT` or empty |
  | 18 | `reversalTransactionId` | UUID or empty |
  | 19 | `replacementTransactionId` | UUID or empty |
  | 20 | `confirmedAt` | RFC 3339 or empty |
  | 21 | `confirmedBy` | as the DTO (the confirming MRE user's email, §34.2), or empty |
  | 22 | `createdAt` | RFC 3339 |
  | 23 | `version` | integer |

  With `rows=splits` ten more follow: 24 `splitPosition`, 25 `splitAmount`, 26 `signedSplitAmount` (signed by the Transaction's `direction`), 27 `financialCategoryCode`, 28 `splitPropertyReferenceId`, 29 `loanId`, 30 `securityDepositId`, 31 `wegAnnualStatementId`, 32 `wegSpecialAssessmentId`, 33 `splitDescription`; all empty on the row of an unsplit Transaction. `mreRealmId` is not a column (one Realm per file; it is in `X-Export-Realm`). Columns are only ever **added at the end** in a later format version; none is renamed or reordered.
- **Values** (the default dialect `rfc4180`; `excel-de` changes only what "`dialect`" below lists):
  - **Money:** the exact decimal string of `Money.amount`: decimal point, exactly two decimals for EUR, no thousands separator, no currency sign, never rounded, never through a float; up to 18 integer digits as stored. `signedAmount` is a string operation (a `-` prefix), not arithmetic.
  - **Dates and timestamps:** as the DTO (§88): `YYYY-MM-DD`; RFC 3339 in UTC with milliseconds (`2026-10-02T08:15:00.000Z`), never a locale format.
  - **`null`:** an empty field. DE stores no empty strings in these columns (trimmed, empty = `null`, §31.2), so empty is unambiguous.
- **Encoding and escaping, default `dialect=rfc4180` (open questions 2 and 3, decided):**
  - UTF-8, **no BOM**; the first byte is the `t` of `transactionId`.
  - RFC 4180: delimiter `,`, record separator CRLF (also after the last record), a header line always (also for an empty result).
  - A field is enclosed in double quotes exactly when it contains `,`, `"`, CR or LF; a `"` inside is doubled. Other fields are written bare. Line breaks inside a description are kept, inside the quotes.
  - **No formula guard, no other change of any value:** the file is the exact portability file, for machines and for moving the data („Die RFC-Datei bleibt zeichengenau, denn sie ist für Maschinen und für den Umzug der Daten.“; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-06). Parsed back with an RFC 4180 parser, every field equals its DTO value character for character, also a description starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR. The spreadsheet risk of such a value (CWE-1236; bank texts and counterparty names come from third parties, `technology.md`: no trust in CSV content) is covered where it arises, in `dialect=excel-de`.
- **`dialect=excel-de`** (open questions 2 (b) and 3 (b), decided): the same file for a person opening it by double-click in a German Excel („Der eine echte Nutzer öffnet die Datei per Doppelklick in einem deutschen Excel“). Everything not listed here is as in the default: the same columns in the same order and with the same header names, the same rows, order, filters, `rows`, streaming, counts, limits and errors.
  - **Encoding:** UTF-8 **with BOM**: the first three bytes are `EF BB BF` (U+FEFF), then the `t` of `transactionId`. The BOM is sent once, before the header line, also for an empty result.
  - **Delimiter `;`**; record separator **CRLF** (also after the last record); a header line always.
  - **Quoting:** a field is enclosed in double quotes exactly when it contains `;`, `"`, CR or LF; a `"` inside is doubled. A `,` alone does not quote a field here (it is no delimiter); other fields are written bare.
  - **Money** (`amount`, `signedAmount`, `splitAmount`, `signedSplitAmount`): the default's exact string with its one `.` replaced by `,` (`1250,00`, `312,40`): exactly two decimals for EUR, **no thousands separator**, no currency sign, never rounded, never through a float or a locale formatter; up to 18 integer digits as stored. A string operation on `Money.amount`, like the sign.
  - **Negative amounts keep the `-`** (`signedAmount` `-312,40`, `signedSplitAmount` likewise), `0,00` never signed: German Excel reads `-312,40` as a negative number, and the sign is the same string prefix as in the default. No parentheses, no trailing minus.
  - **Dates and timestamps stay ISO**, exactly as in the default: `YYYY-MM-DD` (`2026-10-01`) and RFC 3339 in UTC with milliseconds (`2026-10-02T08:15:00.000Z`), never `01.10.2026`. Reason: they stay exact and sortable as text and identical to the JSON and the API; a German Excel recognises `YYYY-MM-DD` as a date on opening; a local `TT.MM.JJJJ` would add a second date format and, for the timestamps, a time zone conversion (Europe/Berlin) that would change the values. The timestamps open as text.
  - **Integers** (`splitCount`, `version`, `splitPosition`) and ids, codes and enum values unchanged.
  - **Formula guard** (CWE-1236, OWASP's CSV injection advice), **only in this dialect** and **only in the four free-text columns** `description`, `counterpartyNameRaw`, `counterpartyIbanRaw` and `splitDescription`: a value whose first character is `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR gets a leading `'`, then the quoting rule above applies to the guarded value. Ids, codes, dates, amounts and integers are never guarded (a negative `signedAmount` stays `-312,40`). A value already starting with `'` is not changed; the guarded `=x` and a stored `'=x` therefore look the same in this dialect, which is why it is not the portability file (the release note says so).
  - **Headers:** `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8; header=present` (as the default; the BOM does not change it); `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="kassenbuch-<YYYY-MM-DD>-excel-de.csv"` (so both files can lie side by side); `X-Export-Format: vermieter-cockpit.transactions-csv; version=1; rows=transactions; dialect=excel-de` (or `rows=splits`). The default's `X-Export-Format` names `dialect=rfc4180`.
  - **An invalid value** (`dialect=excel`, `dialect=EXCEL-DE`, `dialect=` empty, `dialect` given twice) is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with `details.fields: [{ "field": "dialect", "code": "INVALID_FORMAT" }]`, as every other enum filter of `listFields` (`z.enum`, `fieldErrors` in `api/validation.ts`), before the count and before the first byte. The values are case-sensitive, as `rows` and §30.1's enums.
- **Order (open question 4):** oldest booking first: `bookingDate` ascending, then `createdAt`, then `transactionId`, then split `position`, i.e. §30.1's order reversed, read backwards from the same index `(mre_realm_id, booking_date DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC)`.
- **Streaming and size (open question 11):**
  - The response is **streamed** (`Transfer-Encoding: chunked`), read in keyset batches of 500 Transactions (with their splits, one query each) inside the one snapshot, so memory stays bounded and the file is consistent.
  - **Before the first byte**, the filtered Transactions are counted in the snapshot. Above **100,000**: `409 CONFLICT` with `reason = "EXPORT_TOO_LARGE"`, `details.total` and `details.limit`, as JSON; narrow the filter (e.g. by year). The count goes out as `X-Export-Transaction-Count` (and, with `rows=splits`, `X-Export-Row-Count`), so a client can check it has every row.
  - An error **after** the first byte cannot change the status any more: the server destroys the connection without the closing chunk, so the client sees a broken transfer, never a complete-looking file. Logged; without a request id until VC-X-10 brings one with structured logging (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-06).
  - A client that disconnects ends the read and the snapshot.
- **Headers:** `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8; header=present`; `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="kassenbuch-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv"` (the UTC date of `X-Export-Generated-At`); `X-Export-Format: vermieter-cockpit.transactions-csv; version=1; rows=transactions; dialect=rfc4180` (or `rows=splits`); `X-Export-Realm: <mreRealmId>`. For `dialect=excel-de` the filename and `X-Export-Format` as "`dialect`" above.

### `GET /api/v1/property-references/{propertyReferenceId}/export.json`

- **Query:** none; any parameter is `400`. Path id as above (`400` malformed, `404` unknown or foreign).
- **Response `200`**, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="objekt-<propertyReferenceId>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.json"`, `X-Export-Format: vermieter-cockpit.property-export; version=1`. Not streamed: a property's records are few, the document is built in the snapshot and sent whole.
- **Schema (format version 1).** Every element is the **existing single-read DTO** named, field for field, so the export never has a second shape of an entity; `ETag`s are not part of it:

  | Key | Content | Which, and in what order |
  |---|---|---|
  | `exportFormat` | `"vermieter-cockpit.property-export"` | |
  | `exportFormatVersion` | `1` (a JSON integer; it is not an amount) | |
  | `generatedAt` | RFC 3339, as `X-Export-Generated-At` | |
  | `mreRealmId` | the caller's Realm | |
  | `propertyReference` | §23.3's single read | |
  | `ownerships` | §26.1's DTO | every Ownership of P, `VOID` included (as §26.1's history read): `validFrom`, `createdAt`, `ownershipId` |
  | `acquisitions` | §27.1's DTO, plus `costs` (§27.2, `VOID` included), `payments` (§27.2's links, unlinked ones included) and `landBuildingAllocations` (§27.3's history) | every Acquisition of P, `DRAFT`, `CONFIRMED` and `CANCELLED`: `contractDate`, `createdAt`, `acquisitionId` (ascending; §27.1's list is newest first) |
  | `loans` | `{ loan, terms, allocationSets, balanceStatements }`: §41.1's DTO; §41.2's terms history, `VOID` included; §41.3's sets of the Loan, `VOID` included, each with all its entries (other PropertyReferences of the Realm included, since the set is the Loan's fact); §41.6's lender statements, `VOID` included | every Loan any of whose sets, in any status, names P, the Loan in any status (unlike §41.3's per-property list, which leaves `VOID` Loans out): `loanId` |
  | `wegMemberships` | `{ membership, weg }`: §49.2's DTO and §49.1's DTO of its WEG | every membership of P, `VOID` included: `validFrom`, `createdAt`, `membershipId` |
  | `securityDeposits` | §47.1/§47.3's single read with `cash` | every deposit, in any status, whose PropertyReference by §58A's rule is P: `securityDepositId` |
  | `securityDepositsNotAttributed` | `{ securityDepositId, reason, candidates }` | every deposit whose §58A PropertyReference is `null` with `SEVERAL_PROPERTY_REFERENCES` and P among `candidates`; it is listed, not exported, in every candidate's file (open question 9, decided as proposed). A deposit whose §58A PropertyReference is `null` with `NO_RECONCILED_RENT` is in **no** property's file, neither here nor in `securityDeposits`: it appears **only** in the Realm-wide export of VC-X-04 Part 2 (open question 10) |
  | `parties` | §19.1's DTO, current values | every Party named by a `…PartyId` / `…PartyIds` field above (owners, buyers, sellers, lenders), `INACTIVE` included: `partyId` (open question 12) |

- **Values:** Money as §31 (`{ "amount": "1250.00", "currency": "EUR" }`, a string, never a number); Ownership shares and `acquiredShare` as reduced fractions `"n/d"`; the MEA as printed (§49.2); `cachedSurface` a decimal string (§23.3); dates and timestamps as §88; `null` as `null`. Arrays are always present (empty `[]`). Keys in the order of the table and of each DTO.
- **What history:** every status, as the table says. Derived values only where the named DTO already carries them (§47.3's deposit figures, §27.1's `transferDate`); no other derived read (no schedule, remaining debt, owner allocation, tax-year view, AfA; open question 13). **No AuditRecords** (open question 8; `?include=audit` is later work, below). **Not in format version 1** (open question 10): the Transactions (they are the CSV, `?propertyReferenceId=P`), WEG plans, statements and assessments, RentalContractReferences, rent reconciliations, tax classifications, depreciation assets, Party external references, deposits with `NO_RECONCILED_RENT`; the Realm-wide complete export of VC-X-04 Part 2 carries them.
- **Size:** the records over all collections are counted in the snapshot; above **10,000**: `409 CONFLICT` with `reason = "EXPORT_TOO_LARGE"`, `details.total`, `details.limit`. Far above a private landlord's property.

### Error codes and the api inventory

| Status | Code / reason | When |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `VALIDATION_ERROR` (`details.fields[]`: `INVALID_FORMAT`, `INVALID_RANGE`, unknown parameter) | as §30.1; `page`, `pageSize` on the CSV; any parameter on the JSON; a bad `rows` or `dialect` value (`INVALID_FORMAT` on `rows` / `dialect`); `include` on either route; a malformed path id |
| `401` / `403` / `503` | as `requireDeAccess` | unchanged |
| `404` | `NOT_FOUND`, `details.propertyReferenceId` | JSON route only: unknown or foreign PropertyReference |
| `409` | `CONFLICT`, `reason = "EXPORT_TOO_LARGE"`, `details.total`, `details.limit` | above 100,000 Transactions (CSV) or 10,000 records (JSON); before the first byte |

Every error is JSON (§12), also on the CSV route. **api-inventory** (`docs/development/api-inventory.md`, regenerated by `yarn api:inventory` in the implementation PR, not in this docs-only PR): two lines, `GET /api/v1/exports/transactions.csv` (a new module `exports`) and `GET /api/v1/property-references/:propertyReferenceId/export.json` (module `property-references`); "Routes: 172" becomes 174. Express 4 matches the `.` in both paths literally. The route list of §30 and §22 get a pointer to §58S at implementation. `dialect` adds no route and no inventory line (a query parameter).

### Later work (not version 1)

- **`?include=audit` only with VC-X-24** (open question 8, decided as proposed: „Keine AuditRecords in Version 1; `?include=audit` erst mit VC-X-24.“; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-06). Until VC-X-24's retention and pseudonymisation are implemented, `include` is an unknown parameter on both routes (`400`). Its shape (e.g. the pseudonymised history as an `auditRecords` array per entity in the JSON) is specified together with VC-X-24, not here.
- **VC-X-04 Part 2: the Realm-wide complete export** (open question 10, decided as proposed; its own backlog row): every entity of the Realm, including what format version 1 leaves out ("What history" of the JSON route) and the deposits with `NO_RECONCILED_RENT`, which no property's file carries (open question 9). Not specified here.

### Example (synthetic)

Realm `6a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5`; account A `0b1c2d3e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`; PropertyReference P `7e000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000aa`. Three Transactions, all booked on A:

- **T1** `5d2c0f1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000101`: 2026-10-01, `INFLOW` 1250.00, `BANK_CSV`, `CONFIRMED`, description `Miete Oktober, Whg. 3 "EG links"`, counterparty `Erika Mustermann` / `DE02120300000000202051`; splits 1 `RENT_BASE` 1000.00 on P, 2 `RENT_OPERATING_COST_ADVANCE` 250.00 on P.
- **T2** `…0102`: 2026-10-05, `OUTFLOW` 312.40, `MANUAL`, `CONFIRMED`, description `Hausgeld 10/2026`; split 1 `WEG_NON_RECOVERABLE` 312.40 on P (Hausgeld; P is a unit of WEG W `0e000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` with membership `0e000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011` since 2026-01-01, which a `WEG_*` split needs; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-06).
- **T3** `…0103`: 2026-10-07, `INFLOW` 50.00, `BANK_CSV`, `UNREVIEWED`, description `=HYPERLINK("http://x.example")`, counterparty `+Test` / `DE89370400440532013000`; no splits.

`GET /api/v1/exports/transactions.csv?financialAccountId=0b1c2d3e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001&bookingDateFrom=2026-10-01&bookingDateTo=2026-10-31` (default `dialect=rfc4180`) answers `200` with `X-Export-Transaction-Count: 3` and (CRLF line ends, no BOM, 1,098 bytes; T3's texts unchanged, no formula guard):

```text
transactionId,bookingDate,valueDate,financialAccountId,direction,amount,signedAmount,currency,status,provenance,description,counterpartyNameRaw,counterpartyIbanRaw,propertyReferenceId,splitCount,correctionOfTransactionId,correctionRole,reversalTransactionId,replacementTransactionId,confirmedAt,confirmedBy,createdAt,version
5d2c0f1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000101,2026-10-01,2026-10-01,0b1c2d3e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001,INFLOW,1250.00,1250.00,EUR,CONFIRMED,BANK_CSV,"Miete Oktober, Whg. 3 ""EG links""",Erika Mustermann,DE02120300000000202051,,2,,,,,2026-10-03T09:00:00.000Z,vermieter@example.org,2026-10-02T08:15:00.000Z,2
5d2c0f1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000102,2026-10-05,,0b1c2d3e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001,OUTFLOW,312.40,-312.40,EUR,CONFIRMED,MANUAL,Hausgeld 10/2026,,,,1,,,,,2026-10-05T10:00:00.000Z,vermieter@example.org,2026-10-05T09:58:00.000Z,2
5d2c0f1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000103,2026-10-07,2026-10-07,0b1c2d3e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001,INFLOW,50.00,50.00,EUR,UNREVIEWED,BANK_CSV,"=HYPERLINK(""http://x.example"")",+Test,DE89370400440532013000,,0,,,,,,,2026-10-08T07:30:00.000Z,1
```

- Σ `signedAmount` = 1250.00 − 312.40 + 50.00 = **987.60**; with `&current=true` T3 drops out (`UNREVIEWED`): **937.60**.
- With `&rows=splits`: `X-Export-Row-Count: 4` (T1 two rows, T2 one, T3 one with empty split columns); T1's rows end `…,1,1000.00,1000.00,RENT_BASE,7e000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000aa,,,,,` and `…,2,250.00,250.00,RENT_OPERATING_COST_ADVANCE,7e000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000aa,,,,,`, T2's `…,1,312.40,-312.40,WEG_NON_RECOVERABLE,7e000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000aa,,,,,`. Σ `signedSplitAmount` = **937.60**, equal to the confirmed Transactions' sum (a confirmed Transaction's splits sum exactly to its amount, §34.2).
- With `&page=2`: `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, `details.fields: [{ "field": "page", … }]`. With another Realm's account as `financialAccountId`: `200`, the header line only, `X-Export-Transaction-Count: 0`.

The same request with `&dialect=excel-de` answers `200` with the same counts, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="kassenbuch-2026-11-06-excel-de.csv"` (for `X-Export-Generated-At` on 2026-11-06), `X-Export-Format: vermieter-cockpit.transactions-csv; version=1; rows=transactions; dialect=excel-de` and these bytes (1,103: the BOM's 3 more and T3's two `'`). The BOM is not printable; it is written here as the escape `\xEF\xBB\xBF`, standing for the three bytes `EF BB BF` (the file begins `EF BB BF 74 72 61`, i.e. BOM, `tra`). Everything else is literal; every line ends with CRLF, also the last; no backslash occurs in the file:

### Tests the implementation needs

- **Route tests** (`api/exports.test.ts`): every §30.1 filter on the CSV, alone and combined (the same cases as §30.1's list tests, one table), `rows=splits`, `page`/`pageSize`/an unknown parameter/`rows=all` → `400`, `INVALID_RANGE`, the headers (`Content-Type`, `Content-Disposition`, `Cache-Control`, `X-Export-*`), an empty result (header line, CRLF, count 0); the JSON route's `400`/`404`; `EXPORT_TOO_LARGE` with the limits injected small.
- **The CSV's bytes, default `rfc4180`** (a golden file of the example above, compared byte for byte, 1,098 bytes): no BOM; CRLF after every record; quoting of `,`, `"`, CR, LF; **no formula guard**: T3's `=HYPERLINK(…)` and `+Test` written unchanged, and a value starting with each of `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB, CR in each of the four text columns parsed back unchanged; umlauts as UTF-8; `0.00` unsigned; the largest amount §31.2 accepts (18 integer digits) exact; a parse back with an RFC 4180 parser gives every DTO value character for character.
- **The CSV's bytes, `dialect=excel-de`** (a second golden file, the excel-de example above, 1,103 bytes): the first three bytes `EF BB BF`, then `transactionId`, the BOM exactly once (also on an empty result: BOM, header, CRLF); `;` between fields and `,` nowhere as a delimiter; CRLF after every record; quoting on `;`, `"`, CR, LF, and **not** on a lone `,`; decimal comma in all four money columns, no `.` in any of them, no thousands separator (`1250,00`, the 18-digit amount exact with its `,`); `-312,40` with its `-`, `0,00` unsigned; the same column count, header names and order as the default (header split on `;` equals the default's split on `,`); dates and timestamps byte-equal to the default's; the formula guard on each of `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB, CR in each of the four text columns, on none of the other columns (a negative `signedAmount`, an id, a code untouched), and not on a value starting with `'`; a guarded value containing `;` or `"` quoted after guarding (`"'=A;B"`); a parse back with `;` as delimiter, the guard `'` stripped and the `,` read as the decimal point gives every DTO value. `dialect=rfc4180` given explicitly equals the default byte for byte.
- **`dialect` refused:** `excel`, `EXCEL-DE`, empty, twice → `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with `field: "dialect"`, `code: "INVALID_FORMAT"`, as JSON without BOM, before any count; `include=audit` → `400` on both routes.
- **Headers per dialect:** `Content-Disposition` `kassenbuch-<date>.csv` / `kassenbuch-<date>-excel-de.csv`; `X-Export-Format` with `dialect=rfc4180` / `dialect=excel-de`; `Content-Type` the same.
- **History and sums:** a corrected Transaction (original `CORRECTED`, reversal, replacement) and an `IGNORED` one are rows of the raw export and not of `current=true`; Σ `signedAmount` of `current=true` equals §35.3's net effect from the list API for the same filter; Σ `signedSplitAmount` per `financialCategoryCode` equals the splits' sums read through `GET /transactions/{id}`; the money sums of the Realm are unchanged by the export (it writes nothing: row counts and `version`s of every table before and after).
- **Order and streaming:** more than one batch (e.g. 1,201 Transactions with batch size 500): the order is complete and stable across batch edges with equal `bookingDate` and `createdAt`; a write committed during the stream is not in the file (snapshot); `X-Export-Transaction-Count` equals the rows; a failure injected after the first batch ends the response without the closing chunk. The same batch test with `dialect=excel-de`: the BOM exactly once, at the start, no `;`/`,` mix at a batch edge.
- **JSON:** the example above as a golden document; each collection with a `VOID` / `CANCELLED` member; a Loan whose only set naming P is `VOID`, and a `VOID` Loan; a set with P and another PropertyReference; an Acquisition with a voided cost and an unlinked payment; a membership and its WEG; a deposit attributed to P (with `cash`), one with `SEVERAL_PROPERTY_REFERENCES` (in both candidates' files), one with `NO_RECONCILED_RENT` (in no property's file, neither in `securityDeposits` nor in `securityDepositsNotAttributed`; it is Part 2's); `parties` once each, `INACTIVE` included; every element deep-equal to the single-read route's body.
- **Realm isolation** (both routes): Realm B's Transactions, Ownerships, Acquisitions, Loans, memberships, deposits and Parties never appear in A's files; B's PropertyReference id → `404`; B's account as filter → header only; a Realm-A Loan set cannot name a Realm-B property (existing foreign keys) — asserted via the export, not assumed.
- **No MRE call** for either route (fake MRE call count unchanged). **No AuditRecord** written (count before and after).
- **Inventory:** `route-inventory.test.ts` with the two lines; `yarn api:inventory:check`.

### Release note

*New: two exports in open formats (constitution Art. I, ADR-030). `GET /api/v1/exports/transactions.csv` returns the Kassenbuch of the Realm as CSV (RFC 4180, UTF-8 without BOM, comma, decimal point, `YYYY-MM-DD`), with the filters of `GET /transactions` and one row per Transaction or, with `rows=splits`, per split; corrected, reversed and ignored Transactions are included unless `current=true` is given. By default every value is written exactly as stored, character for character, so the file can be read back without loss; it is meant for programs and for moving the data. For opening by double-click in a German Excel, `dialect=excel-de` gives the same columns with semicolons, decimal comma (`1250,00`, no thousands separator), a UTF-8 BOM and ISO dates; there, text in the four free-text columns starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a line break is prefixed with `'` so that a spreadsheet does not run it as a formula (such a value then reads the same as one stored with a leading `'`). `GET /api/v1/property-references/{id}/export.json` returns one property with its Ownerships, Acquisitions, Loans, WEG memberships, deposits and the Parties they name, voided records included and marked. Neither contains the change history (AuditRecords). Exports above 100,000 Transactions or 10,000 records answer `409 EXPORT_TOO_LARGE`; narrow the filter. An export broken off after its first byte is logged without a request ID until structured logging (VC-X-10) adds one.*

### Open questions (decided)

1. **One row per Transaction or per split.** **Proposal:** `rows=transactions` by default (Σ `signedAmount` is the cash, no double counting), `rows=splits` on request (Σ `signedSplitAmount` per category and property; the Transaction columns repeated). **Alternatives:** (a) only per split (one format, but summing `signedAmount` counts a split Transaction several times); (b) only per Transaction with the categories joined in one column (`RENT_BASE:1000.00;…`), not summable in a spreadsheet; (c) two files in a ZIP (not an open plain format any more). **Decided (as proposed; Frage 1):** `rows=transactions` by default, `rows=splits` on request.
2. **Delimiter, decimal mark, BOM.** **Proposal:** RFC 4180 with `,` and decimal point, UTF-8 **without** BOM: exact, machine-readable, the same digits as the API; German Excel opens it through "Daten → Aus Text/CSV" (LibreOffice asks anyway). **Alternatives:** (a) the same with a BOM (Excel recognises UTF-8 on double-click, but still splits on `;` in a German locale, and some tools read the BOM as part of the first header); (b) a second dialect `dialect=excel-de`: `;`, decimal comma (`1250,00`, still exact, no thousands separator), BOM, same columns; (c) `;` and decimal comma as the only format (convenient in German Excel, not RFC 4180). **Decided, the proposal plus alternative (b) (Frage 2):** the default stays RFC 4180 with `,`, decimal point and no BOM, as the exact portability file; in addition `dialect=excel-de` with `;`, decimal comma without thousands separator, BOM and the same columns ("`dialect`" in the CSV route above). Alternatives (a) and (c) not taken.
3. **The formula guard.** **Proposal:** a leading `'` in the four free-text columns when the value starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR (OWASP's CSV injection advice; counterparty names are chosen by whoever sends money). Documented, so a re-import strips it; the value `'=x` and the guarded `=x` then look the same, which the release note says. **Alternatives:** (a) no change of any value (exact round trip, the risk left to the spreadsheet's warnings); (b) the guard only in `dialect=excel-de` (question 2 (b)). **Decided, alternative (b) (Frage 3):** the formula guard only in `dialect=excel-de`; the default (`rfc4180`) changes no value (alternative (a)'s exact round trip for the default). The proposal, a guard in every file, is not taken.
4. **Order.** **Proposal:** oldest first (a Kassenbuch reads forward; a running balance can be added in the spreadsheet). **Alternative:** §30.1's newest first (one order everywhere). **Decided (as proposed; Frage 4):** oldest first.
5. **Default scope of the CSV.** **Proposal:** the raw set, as §30.1 without filters (nothing is dropped from an export by default; `status` and `correctionRole` say what each row is); `current=true` for the net Kassenbuch. **Alternative:** `current=true` by default and `current=false` for the raw set (the file sums to the cash, but deviates from §30.1's meaning of an absent filter). **Decided (as proposed; Frage 5):** the raw set as §30.1 without filters; `current=true` for the net Kassenbuch.
6. **Column names.** **Proposal:** the DTO's English field names (stable, the same as the API and the JSON). **Alternatives:** German headers (`Buchungsdatum`, `Betrag`, …) for the reader in a spreadsheet; or English names with readable extra columns (`financialAccountName`, `financialCategoryName`, property `displayName`), which are values of other records, cached or translated, and change over time. **Decided (as proposed; Frage 6):** the DTO's English field names; no resolved names.
7. **Voided and cancelled records in the JSON.** **Proposal:** included, marked by `status` (a recording error and its correction are part of the record, as §26.1's history read shows them). **Alternative:** only the records that count (`VALID`/`ACTIVE`/not `CANCELLED`), smaller but not complete. **Decided (as proposed; Frage 7):** voided and cancelled records included, marked by `status`.
8. **AuditRecords.** **Proposal:** in neither export in version 1: their retention and pseudonymisation (VC-X-24, decided 2026-11-06, not implemented) must hold in an export too, and no audit read exists yet (ui-guide §6.1, decision of 30.10.2026). **Alternatives:** (a) `?include=audit` once VC-X-24 is implemented, the pseudonymised history in an `auditRecords` array per entity; (b) a Realm-wide audit export of its own (`GET /exports/audit-records.jsonl`) with VC-X-24. **Decided (as proposed; Frage 8):** no AuditRecords in version 1; `?include=audit` only with VC-X-24 ("Later work" above).
9. **Deposits of the property.** **Proposal:** §58A's rule (the one PropertyReference on which the Tenant's confirmed rent is booked); a deposit with several candidates is listed by id in `securityDepositsNotAttributed` of each candidate; one without reconciled rent is in no property's file and comes with the Realm-wide export (question 10). **Alternatives:** (a) the deposit exported in full in every candidate's file (duplicated, reads as attributed); (b) a `propertyReferenceId` on the deposit (a migration and a decision of its own; §58A names it as a later option); (c) asking MRE for the Tenant's property (an MRE call, not reproducible from DE's data). **Decided (as proposed; Frage 9):** §58A's rule; several candidates as an id list; a deposit without reconciled rent only in the Realm-wide export of question 10 (VC-X-04 Part 2).
10. **Scope of version 1.** **Proposal:** what issue #281 names, nothing more; a Realm-wide complete export (all entities as JSON Lines, Transactions as this CSV) as **VC-X-04 Part 2**, a backlog line of its own, to meet Art. I's "migrate away" in full. **Alternatives:** (a) the property file grows now (WEG plans, statements and assessments of each membership; RentalContractReferences and reconciliations of the Tenants; tax classifications and depreciation assets of P); (b) no Part 2 until a migration target exists. **Decided (as proposed; Frage 10):** the scope of issue #281; the Realm-wide complete export as VC-X-04 Part 2, its own backlog row created now.
11. **Limits and streaming.** **Proposal:** CSV streamed in one snapshot with a cap of 100,000 Transactions (a private landlord books a few thousand a year), JSON whole with a cap of 10,000 records, both `409 EXPORT_TOO_LARGE` before the first byte. **Alternatives:** (a) no cap (an export of everything may hold a snapshot for long); (b) an asynchronous export job with a download link (API-OPEN-005, more machinery than needed now); (c) the CSV built in memory with `Content-Length` (simpler, but memory grows with the file). **Decided (as proposed; Frage 11):** CSV streamed in one snapshot up to 100,000 Transactions, JSON up to 10,000 records, `409 EXPORT_TOO_LARGE` before the first byte.
12. **Parties and contact data in the JSON.** **Proposal:** the Parties named by the exported records, with §19.1's fields (names, `email`, `phone`): the file is then readable without the API, and it is the caller's own Realm data, shown by `GET /parties/{id}` to the same roles. **Alternatives:** (a) ids only (smaller, no contact data in a file that may be passed on); (b) names only, without `email` and `phone`. **Decided (as proposed; Frage 12):** the Parties with §19.1's fields.
13. **Derived values.** **Proposal:** only those the single-read DTOs already carry (deposit figures and state, `transferDate`), so every element equals its single read; no schedule, remaining debt, owner allocation, tax or AfA figure. **Alternatives:** (a) stored facts only, the deposit's derived figures removed (the element then differs from its read); (b) the derived reads added (`schedule`, `remainingDebt`), which are computed by rules and versions that would have to be named in the file (`docs/product/reports.md` §3). **Decided (as proposed; Frage 13):** only the derived values the single reads already carry; no schedule, remaining debt, tax or AfA figure.

**Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (chat)** (verbatim, without the owner's first line about where the questions came from; cited as „Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-06“; the bullets 1–13 answer open questions 1–13 above):

„Alle 13 beantwortet. Abweichungen bei 2 und 3, die zusammengehören.

- **1: wie vorgeschlagen.** `rows=transactions` als Standard, `rows=splits` auf Anfrage.
- **2: wie vorgeschlagen, plus Alternative (b).** Standard RFC 4180 mit `,`, Dezimalpunkt, ohne BOM, als exakte Portabilitätsdatei. Zusätzlich `dialect=excel-de` mit `;`, Dezimalkomma ohne Tausendertrenner, BOM, gleiche Spalten. Grund: Der eine echte Nutzer öffnet die Datei per Doppelklick in einem deutschen Excel; das sind wenige Zeilen Code, und die exakte Datei bleibt der Standard.
- **3: Alternative (b), Formel-Schutz nur in `dialect=excel-de`.** Die RFC-Datei bleibt zeichengenau, denn sie ist für Maschinen und für den Umzug der Daten. Der Excel-Dialekt ist für Menschen am Tabellenprogramm, dort gehört der Schutz hin. So bleibt der Round-Trip exakt, und das Risiko ist da abgedeckt, wo es entsteht.
- **4: wie vorgeschlagen.** Älteste zuerst.
- **5: wie vorgeschlagen.** Rohmenge wie §30.1 ohne Filter, `current=true` für das Netto-Kassenbuch.
- **6: wie vorgeschlagen.** Englische DTO-Feldnamen, stabil wie API und JSON. Keine aufgelösten Namen, die sich ändern.
- **7: wie vorgeschlagen.** Voided und Cancelled enthalten, über `status` erkennbar.
- **8: wie vorgeschlagen.** Keine AuditRecords in Version 1; `?include=audit` erst mit VC-X-24.
- **9: wie vorgeschlagen.** Kautionen nach §58A; mehrere Kandidaten als ID-Liste, ohne abgeglichene Miete nur im Realm-Export aus Frage 10.
- **10: wie vorgeschlagen.** Umfang wie #281; Realm-weiter Vollexport als VC-X-04 Teil 2, eigene Backlog-Zeile jetzt anlegen.
- **11: wie vorgeschlagen.** CSV gestreamt in einem Snapshot bis 100.000 Transaktionen, JSON bis 10.000 Datensätze, `409 EXPORT_TOO_LARGE` vor dem ersten Byte.
- **12: wie vorgeschlagen.** Parteien mit §19.1-Feldern; es sind die eigenen Realm-Daten, die dieselben Rollen auch einzeln lesen.
- **13: wie vorgeschlagen.** Nur die abgeleiteten Werte, die die Einzel-Reads schon tragen; kein Plan, keine Restschuld, keine Steuer- oder AfA-Zahl.

Reihenfolge bleibt: VC-X-57 zu Ende, VC-X-12 mit 0074, dann VC-X-04 ohne Migration.“

**Still open (owner):** none. Questions 1–13 are decided (2026-11-06, above): 1 and 4–13 as proposed; 2 the proposal plus alternative (b) (`dialect=excel-de`), 3 alternative (b) (the formula guard only in `dialect=excel-de`), amended in the body above. The details of `dialect=excel-de` the decision does not name (ISO dates and timestamps, the `-` of negative amounts, CRLF, the quoting set, `INVALID_FORMAT` for a bad value, the filename) are this section's reading, stated in "`dialect`" above. **Follow-up backlog row the decisions create:** **VC-X-04 Part 2** (the Realm-wide complete export, including the deposits without reconciled rent). Implemented after VC-X-12, without a migration ("As implemented (VC-X-04)" below).

### As implemented (VC-X-04)

Implemented as specified and decided (open questions 1–13, Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-06), **without a migration** (main c8ddbe0, after VC-X-12's 0074). Paths relative to `services/de-backend/src/`.

**What was built:**

1. **One filter for list and export** (`infrastructure/postgres/transaction-reads.ts`): `filtered` (moved out of `transaction-query-repository.ts`, unchanged; the Realm condition first), `matchesNothing` (no status left, a malformed id filter) and `splitsOf` (the splits of many Transactions in `position` order, also used by `GET /transactions/{id}`). §30.1's list, order, paging and query plan are unchanged (`transaction-query-plan.test.ts` green).
2. **The Kassenbuch read** (`infrastructure/postgres/transaction-export-repository.ts`, `PostgresTransactionExport`, port `TransactionExportQueries` in `domains/ledger/transaction-query.ts`): one `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` transaction; the clock read right after its first statement (`X-Export-Generated-At`); the count (and with `rows=splits` the row count, one per split or one for an unsplit Transaction) first; then keyset batches of 500 ids, oldest first (`booking_date`, `created_at`, `id` ascending; the cursor is the row comparison against the last id's own key, read back in SQL, so it is exact to the microsecond), each batch's DTO rows and splits by one query each. A throw of the sink ends the read and rolls the snapshot back.
3. **The use cases** (`application/exports.ts`): `exportTransactions` (the limit 100,000 checked on the head, before the sink's head: `ExportTooLargeError`), `exportProperty` (below); `PROPERTY_EXPORT_LIMIT`, `TRANSACTION_EXPORT_LIMIT` and the batch size injectable for tests.
4. **The CSV** (`api/transaction-csv.ts`): the 23 (+ 10) columns of the table above, every value from `toDto` / `toSplitDto`; `signedAmount` / `signedSplitAmount` a `-` prefix (zero never signed); the two dialects as decided: `rfc4180` (`,`, no BOM, quoted exactly on `,` `"` CR LF, no guard) and `excel-de` (BOM once, `;`, quoted exactly on `;` `"` CR LF, `.` → `,` in the four money columns as a string operation, the formula guard `'` before `=` `+` `-` `@` TAB CR in `description`, `counterpartyNameRaw`, `counterpartyIbanRaw` and `splitDescription` only, then quoting; a value already starting with `'` unchanged; dates, timestamps, ids, codes and integers as the default). CRLF after every record.
5. **The routes** (`api/exports.ts`, module `exports`, mounted after the other routers; `ExportCommands` in `AppCommands`): `GET /api/v1/exports/transactions.csv` parses §30.1's `listFields` without `page`/`pageSize` (exported as `filterFields`, with the same date-range check) plus `rows` and `dialect` (`z.enum`, case-sensitive), strict; the filter through `listFilter`, as the list. The sink sets the headers and writes the header line on the head, each batch as one chunk, waiting for `drain`; a client that disconnects rejects the next write (`ClientGoneError`), which ends the read. `GET /api/v1/property-references/{propertyReferenceId}/export.json` takes no parameter and answers with `res.end` (no `ETag`; Express's `send` would add one). Headers as specified. `ExportTooLargeError` is in the central error table (`api/error-answers/exports.ts`): `409 CONFLICT`, `details: { reason: "EXPORT_TOO_LARGE", total, limit }`.
6. **The property read** (`infrastructure/postgres/property-export-snapshot.ts`): `PostgresPropertyExportSnapshots` opens one `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` transaction and builds the single reads' own repositories on it (`joiningSnapshot`: a `Kysely` whose `transaction()` joins the open one, so a repository read that opens its own snapshot runs in this one; read only, a write fails in PostgreSQL). `PropertyExportScope` gives P's id lists in the export's order and in the Realm: Acquisitions (contract date, creation, id), Loans with a set naming P in any status (by id), memberships (valid from, creation, id), and the deposits by §58A (`depositFactsOf`: attributed to P; `SEVERAL_PROPERTY_REFERENCES` with P among the candidates). `exportProperty` reads each element through the single read's repository method (`findById`, §26.1's `history`, `listCosts` and `listPayments` without filter, §27.3's `list`, §41.2's terms, §41.3's sets, §41.6's statements via `debtInputs` and `statementViews`, also for a `VOID` Loan), then the Parties named by `ownerPartyId`, `buyerPartyIds`, `sellerPartyIds`, `counterpartyPartyId`, the classification's and the land/building allocation's `advisorPartyId`, `lenderPartyId`, `borrowerPartyIds` and `administratorPartyId`, once each by id. The API maps each with the single read's DTO function (now exported from its route file).
7. **Wiring:** `main.ts` and the three acceptance harnesses that build the whole app (`phase-2-acceptance.test-support.ts`, `phase-3-acceptance.e2e.test.ts`, `slice-1-acceptance.e2e.test.ts`) get `exports`. api-inventory regenerated: 172 → 174 routes, the new module `exports` (the JSON route is listed under `property-references`, by its path, as `route-inventory.ts` groups).

The JSON golden test compares the spec's document without any replacement.

Decided on #290: export only for now, the other routes with backlog VC-X-61 („Vorerst nur beim Export, mit Backlog-Zeile für alle Routen.“; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-06).
- (e) **No request id exists in DE:** an error after the first byte is logged as `export aborted after the first byte: GET /api/v1/exports/transactions.csv (<error name>)`, without data; the connection is destroyed without the closing chunk. A client that went away is not logged. The Ownership history is read with one page past the limit and refused on its total before anything else.
- (g) **`X-Export-Row-Count`** is sent only with `rows=splits` (as specified); `X-Export-Transaction-Count` always.
