### The switch `DEPRECIATION_RECORDING_STAGE`

- **Values:** exactly `1`, `2` or `3`. **Unset means `1`.** Any other value (`""`, `0`, `4`, `01`, ` 2`, `two`) fails the start with `Invalid configuration: DEPRECIATION_RECORDING_STAGE`, without echoing the value: `z.enum(['1', '2', '3']).default('1')`, transformed to a number, in `configSchema` (as §60's switch).
- **Read once at startup** by `loadConfig`. `main.ts` hands it to the record use case and to the schedule read as a plain dependency (`releasedStage: 1 | 2 | 3`) with **no default**: whoever builds them states the value. Not settable through the API, not stored, not per Realm. The startup log line of §60 names it: `depreciation schedule recording: disabled, released stage 1` (proposal).
- **Independent of `DEPRECIATION_RECORDING_ENABLED`** (A6): set while recording is off it is accepted, does nothing, and the schedule read shows it. Setting it releases nothing by itself. It says up to which stage the command may record once recording is on.
- **Stage 1 only, in this assignment** (decided 2026-11-02). VC-X-45 prepares the gate and its tests with stage 1 as the shipped default. No stage is released productively, and `docker-compose.yml` and the `Dockerfile` set neither switch. The values `2` and `3` are exercised in tests only, through test-only construction (as §60's switch). A productive setting above `1` needs, in this order: recording enabled by §60 "Turning it on"; a documented owner decision releasing that stage, in `docs/development/phase-8-plan.md` and in this section, with the note of A5 where the owner names an advisor's confirmation; then the operator's setting and a restart. **Decided 2026-11-02 (second round, 236-5):** that decision is one entry per stage in the release protocol `docs/development/freigabe-afa-erfassung.md`, taken only when the stage's criteria there are met, never by a calendar date ("Releasing stage 2 or 3" below).

### The stage of a component and of a year (`DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1`)

**The registry entry** (A3): `{ code: "DE_RECORDING_STAGES", version: 1, title, effectiveFrom, source: "Prüfbericht 2026-11-01, F (mündlich bestätigt durch den Steuerberater, laut Projektinhaber am 2026-11-01); owner decisions 2026-11-01 (design, A1, A3, A6) and 2026-11-02; api-design §60A", criteria: [{ code, stage }] }`.
- It is registered beside the calculation rules, not among them: it is not pinned in `frozen-rules.test.ts`, not named in a recorded version's rule versions, not covered by `inputFingerprint` and not read by the start check. It moves no figure.
- A change of the mapping is a new version (`@2`), never an edit in place. A registry test asserts that every criterion is listed once with a stage of 1, 2 or 3.

| Criterion | Stage | What raises it | The years it applies to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PURCHASE` | 1 | a purchase component (§59A) without any criterion below | the component's active years |
| `CAPITALIZED_ITEM` | 2 | a building's later Herstellungskosten item (§59B; „nachträgliche HK“) | the item's active years |
| `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CAPITALIZATION` | 2 | an item capitalised on the anschaffungsnahe check (`anschaffungsnaheAcquisitionId`, §58B) | the item's active years |
| `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN` | 2 | the purchase's check `NOT_COMPUTABLE`, or an open `WEG_HAUSGELD_MAINTENANCE_NOT_COUNTED` (A1; a running window alone does not); **and** (decided 2026-11-02, second round, 236-4) the check `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` while a summed source is still `DEDUCTIBLE` (its suggestion `CAPITALIZED` not yet followed); **and** (decided 2026-11-05, §58M; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05) the check not final for `WEG_STATEMENT_MISSING` | the purchase's active years; for the `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` fact, the purchase's active years from the year of the first summed source on (the earliest of the check's `affectedYears`, §58B); for the `WEG_STATEMENT_MISSING` fact, the purchase's active years from the first year of the check's window on |
| `LOAN_INTEREST_COMPONENT` | 2 | a component whose source is Loan interest (§59E) | each year it is active in |
| `MOVABLE_ASSET` | 2 | a separate asset's component (`DE_AFA_MOVABLE_LINEAR`, §59B; „bewegliche WG“) | its active years |
| `SHORTER_USEFUL_LIFE_ENTRY` | 3 | a purchase with a shorter-life entry, in any review state (`UNREVIEWED` and `NEEDS_REVIEW` included, `FROM_START` included, §59G) | the purchase's active years |
| `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE` | 3 | an owner with more than one purchase component of the building and a share reduction (§59A, `PRO_RATA_ALL_COMPONENTS`) | the active years of that owner's purchase components **from the year of the owner's first share reduction on** (decided 2026-11-02, second round, 236-2; before it each purchase is judged on its own, and several purchases without a reduction stay stage 1, 236-3), **counting only a reduction at which more than one purchase of that owner is active** (decided 2026-11-02, third round, decision 3: a reduction before the second purchase does not start it; implemented by #246, VC-X-45 follow-up 2, "As implemented" 10) |
| `MOVABLE_ASSET_LATER_ADDITION` | 3 | a later item added to a separate asset (§59B, `LATER_ITEM_TO_VERIFY`; „spätere Ergänzungen beweglicher WG“) | the separate asset's active years |

- **The highest applicable stage wins** (decided 2026-11-02): a component's stage is the highest of its criteria, and a year's stage is the highest of every component active in it. A year with a Loan interest component is at least stage 2, and stage 3 when it also has a stage-3 component.
- **Every requested year and every component is checked** (decided 2026-11-02): every year of the run (`fromYear` … `throughYear`, §60) and every component of the asset are judged, computable or not. Nothing is left out because it has no figure, carries a reason, or is excluded from a sum: a not-computable component or part, an item without a usable start, a component whose start is unknown (`TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING`: it counts in every year of the run, as in §60 step 4's top-level `components`), and an entry not yet confirmed all raise the stage as their facts say.
- **A building's items held by a separate asset** (decided 2026-11-02, second round, 236-1): an item the building excludes because an `ACTIVE` separate asset holds it (§59B, `excludedItems`) does **not** raise the building's stage. It is judged as a component of the separate asset, whose own stage (`MOVABLE_ASSET`, and `MOVABLE_ASSET_LATER_ADDITION` where it applies) governs that asset's record: the stage belongs to the asset whose version is recorded. "Every requested year and every component is checked" (above) is about the asset being recorded and is unchanged.
- **A check above 15 % with a suggestion not yet followed** (decided 2026-11-02, second round, 236-4): `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` while a summed source still has `treatment` `DEDUCTIBLE` is a known incomplete state, like A1's Hausgeld flag. It raises the purchase to stage 2 (`ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN`) from the year of the first summed source on. Once every summed source is classified `CAPITALIZED` on the check (§58B "the user follows the suggestion"), the fact ends, and the items carry their stage themselves (`ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CAPITALIZATION`, `CAPITALIZED_ITEM`). The mapping's criteria and stages are unchanged, so `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1` stays `@1` and its pinned hash stays as it is (the fact is one more way to meet an existing criterion; the years are derived in code, as for every criterion).
- **VC-X-27 (maintenance paid from the Hausgeld) is covered by A1:** until VC-X-27 is implemented, a purchase whose check carries an open `WEG_HAUSGELD_MAINTENANCE_NOT_COUNTED` meets `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN` and is at least stage 2. After VC-X-27 (§58M) the flag names only unjudged lines; a cost line summed above 15 % keeps the purchase at stage 2 through 236-4 (the stage reads the flag and the summed sources unchanged). **A check not final for `WEG_STATEMENT_MISSING`** (decided 2026-11-05, question 2 of #269; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-05; verbatim in §58M "As implemented (VC-X-27)", "Open questions of #269 (decided)"): „`WEG_STATEMENT_MISSING` erfüllt das bestehende Kriterium `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN`, also Stufe 2, ab dem ersten Jahr des Fensters, solange die Prüfung aus diesem Grund nicht final ist. Das ist dieselbe Logik wie in A1 für den Hausgeld-Hinweis: Die Summe ist bekannt unvollständig.“ So the check's `NOT_FINAL` reason `WEG_STATEMENT_MISSING` is a further way to meet `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN` (like 236-4): the purchase's active years from the first year of the check's window (the year of `economicTransferDate`) on, while the reason holds; once every statement of the read range is confirmed (the last year ended) the fact ends, and the purchase is stage 1 again if nothing else holds it. `PurchaseCheckFacts` gains `wegStatementMissingFrom` (that year, else `null`), read in the same snapshot (`depreciation-purchase-checks.ts`). **The mapping is unchanged:** `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1`, its criteria and its pinned hash stay as they are (one more fact meeting an existing criterion, as 236-4).
- **Facts, never review states, decide:** an unconfirmed shorter-life entry is stage 3 („auch unbestätigt“). A `VOID` asset, entry or record raises nothing: it is not part of the schedule.

### What blocks at every stage (decided 2026-11-02)

- **Missing facts and unsupported methods stay blocking**, whatever stage is released. §60 step 4 is unchanged: every not-computable year refuses the record (`SCHEDULE_NOT_COMPLETE`). Releasing a stage never makes a component computable and never turns an unsupported method into a supported one: §59C's method reasons, `HISTORICAL_RULE_NOT_SUPPORTED` (§59A), §59D's `ACQUISITION_COST_UNCLASSIFIED`, §59F's `PERFORMANCE_DATE_MISSING` and `PERFORMANCE_SPANS_YEAR_END`, and §59G's reasons (Part 1's included) refuse at stage 3 as at stage 1.
- **§58E's statements replace neither evidence nor computation:** an acknowledgement or a confirmation clears exactly its own flag in the tax-year view (§58E). It never lowers a stage, never makes a component computable, never supplies a missing fact, and never stands in for a VERIFY point.
- **Open VERIFY flags** do not block a record by themselves (§60 open question 1, unchanged), and a released stage does not resolve them: a recorded version stores the flags that stood, and the year stays not final while they are open. An unconfirmed assumption never reads as released.

### `POST …/schedule-versions`: the stage check (§60, amended)

The order of checks of §60, with one step added:
1. `400`, all field errors at once; then, while recording is off, `409 RECORDING_NOT_ENABLED` before any data access (§60, unchanged: the stage is never derived while off);
2. the asset unknown or of another Realm → `404`;
3. `VOID` → `409 ASSET_NOT_ACTIVE`;
4. the schedule of the run, derived in the command's own snapshot: `409 SCHEDULE_NOT_COMPLETE` (unchanged);
5. **new: the stage**, in the same snapshot. Any year of the run whose stage is above `releasedStage` → **`409 CONFLICT`** with `reason = "STAGE_NOT_RELEASED"` and `details: { assetId, releasedStage, years: [{ year, stage, components: [{ componentId, kind, stage, criteria }] }] }`, listing every year above the released stage in ascending order, components by `componentId`;
6. §60's steps 5–9, unchanged.

- **The whole run is refused:** no version is recorded for the years of the run that would be at or below the released stage. An earlier `throughYear` whose years are all within the released stage can be recorded, as for step 4.
- **Why after step 4:** missing facts block at every stage (decided), so the person learns first what to supply, then what the installation has not released. Both are refusals, and neither writes anything.
- **Nothing written, idempotency:** as §60's refusals: no row, no AuditRecord, no `Idempotency-Key` stored, so the same key can be used again after a release.
- **Error:** `StageNotReleasedError` (`application/errors.ts`), mapped in `api/error-answers.ts`: `409 CONFLICT`, "The schedule contains years of a release stage that is not released in this installation.", `details` as above.

### The schedule read (§59A, §60, additively)

- **`recordingStage`:** `{ released: 1 | 2 | 3, rules: "DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1" }` beside `recordingEnabled`, shown whatever `recordingEnabled` says (A6). It describes the installation's setting only and confirms nothing about the figures.
- **`years[].stage`:** `{ stage, components: [{ componentId, stage, criteria }] }` for a year with a component, `null` otherwise.
- **`DEPRECIATION_STAGE_NOT_RELEASED`** (open year flag) on each year whose stage is above the released stage, `details: { stage, releasedStage, components: [{ componentId, kind, stage, criteria }] }`. It is raised beside the year's reasons and flags and replaces none of them, and it is shown while recording is off too. It adds no new state to `final`: the year cannot be recorded, so `DEPRECIATION_SCHEDULE_NOT_RECORDED` keeps it open anyway.
- **The tax-year view (§58C)** does not read the stage. Its `final` stays false for every year with AfA while nothing is recorded (§60).

### Recorded versions

- The `RECORDED` AuditRecord's metadata (§60) gains `{ releasedStage, stageRules: "DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1", years: [{ year, stage }] }`. No column, no migration, no part of `inputFingerprint` or of the reproduction (A3).
- A later lower setting, or a new version of the mapping, changes, flags or refuses no stored version.

### Tests the implementation must have (to be written with VC-X-45)

- **Config** (`config.test.ts`): unset → `1`; `1`, `2`, `3`; `""`, `0`, `4`, `01`, ` 1`, `two` → the start fails naming `DEPRECIATION_RECORDING_STAGE` without the value. Independent of the other switch: stage `3` with recording off starts, the read shows it, and `POST` answers `409 RECORDING_NOT_ENABLED`.
- **Registry:** `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1`'s criteria and stages; not in `frozen-rules.test.ts`, not in a recorded version's rule versions; a test registry with another mapping changes no `inputFingerprint` and no figure.
- **The stage (pure):**
  - each criterion alone gives its stage;
  - combinations give the highest;
  - a purchase with an `UNREVIEWED`, a `NEEDS_REVIEW` or a `FROM_START` shorter-life entry is 3;
  - a year with a Loan interest component is 2, and 3 with a shorter-life entry as well;
  - A1: a running window alone gives 1, a `NOT_COMPUTABLE` check or an open `WEG_HAUSGELD_MAINTENANCE_NOT_COUNTED` gives 2;
  - a not-computable item still raises its years;
  - a component without a start raises every year of the run;
  - a `VOID` entry raises nothing.
- **The command** (PostgreSQL, the switch on in test-only construction):
  - released 1 and a run whose last year has an item → `409 STAGE_NOT_RELEASED` for the whole run, the item named; an earlier `throughYear` without it → `201`;
  - released 2 → `201`; released 2 with a shorter-life purchase → `409`;
  - a year both not computable and above the stage → `SCHEDULE_NOT_COMPLETE` first; with the fact supplied → `STAGE_NOT_RELEASED`;
  - nothing written on a refusal (the row counts of 0052's tables, `audit_record`, `idempotency_key`); the key reusable after the stage is raised;
  - an acknowledgement or a confirmation of §58E present changes no stage and no answer.
- **The read:** `recordingStage` with recording off and on; the flag on exactly the years above the released stage, none at released 3; `years[].stage`.
- **Compose smoke** (proposal): against the default `docker-compose.yml`, the read shows `released: 1`, and `POST` answers `409 RECORDING_NOT_ENABLED`.
- **Mutations** that must turn the tests red, each alone: the highest stage replaced by the first or the lowest; an unconfirmed entry skipped; years or components without a figure skipped; a refusal per year instead of for the whole run; the stage check before the recording switch (data read while off); the default changed from `1`; the stage put into `inputFingerprint`; `STAGE_NOT_RELEASED` raised before `SCHEDULE_NOT_COMPLETE`.

### As implemented (VC-X-45, stage 1)

The release stages above (VC-X-45), stage 1 prepared, with the owner's decisions 236-1, 236-2 and 236-4 of 2026-11-02 (second round; Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-02) applied in items 3, 4 and 9; **no productive enablement**: `DEPRECIATION_RECORDING_ENABLED` stays `false` by default and nothing here turns it on. No migration.

1. **The switch.** `DEPRECIATION_RECORDING_STAGE` (`config.ts`): exactly `1`, `2` or `3`, unset `1`, anything else fails the start naming the variable without its value. `main.ts` hands it to the record use case and the schedule read as `releasedStage` (no default); the start log reads `depreciation schedule recording: disabled, released stage 1`. Set while recording is off it is accepted and only shown (A6). Tests state both switches through `depreciationCommands(…, { recordingEnabled, releasedStage })` (stage `1` unless stated).
2. **The mapping.** `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1` (`domains/depreciation/rules/de-recording-stages.ts`), §60A's nine criteria with their stages, in a registry of its own (`RECORDING_STAGE_RULES`), not in `TAX_RULES`: not frozen (`frozen-rules.test.ts` unchanged), never in a version's rule versions or an `inputFingerprint`. Its hash is pinned in `infrastructure/hashing/recording-stages.test.ts` so that a change is `@2`. A criterion missing from a version, or no version on the day, counts as stage 3.
3. **The stage** (`recording-stage.ts`, pure): from the property-level schedule and its snapshot, over every component of every requested year, computable or not; a component without a start counts in every year of the run. A1's facts come from Taxation's check in the same snapshot (`infrastructure/postgres/depreciation-purchase-checks.ts`, `effectsOf`; `ScheduleRead.purchaseChecks`, read by the schedule source and the record command only, not by the tax-year view). A purchase whose check the snapshot does not give counts as `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN` (only a test read lacks it). A share reduction is a sale by the owner (`sellerPartyIds`) or a day on which the owner holds less than the day before; a row change keeping or raising the share is none. A component's criteria are judged per year: `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE` and the `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` fact of `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN` apply from a first year on (item 9), every other criterion in each year the component counts in. `MOVABLE_ASSET_LATER_ADDITION` is set on every component of the separate asset, so it covers the asset's active years.
4. **Excluded items (236-1).** An item the building excludes because an `ACTIVE` separate asset holds it (`excludedItems`) raises nothing on the building: no component of the building's years, no `kind: "EXCLUDED_ITEM"` (the kind is gone; components are `ACQUISITION` or `CAPITALIZED_ITEM`). It is judged on the separate asset, whose own components keep `MOVABLE_ASSET` (and `MOVABLE_ASSET_LATER_ADDITION`). Without an `ACTIVE` link the item is the building's again (`CAPITALIZED_ITEM`). The earlier cautious reading (the item counted in the building's years as `EXCLUDED_ITEM`) is withdrawn.
5. **The command.** Step 5 of §60A, after `SCHEDULE_NOT_COMPLETE` and before §60's steps 5–9 (so also before `412` and the no-op): `StageNotReleasedError` → `409 CONFLICT`, `reason: "STAGE_NOT_RELEASED"`, `details: { assetId, releasedStage, years: [{ year, stage, components: [{ componentId, kind, stage, criteria }] }] }` with every component of each year above the stage. The refusal rolls the record's transaction back: no row, no AuditRecord, no `Idempotency-Key`. The `RECORDED` AuditRecord's metadata gains `releasedStage`, `stageRules` and `stageYears: [{ year, stage }]` (named `stageYears`, since `years` already holds the amounts).
6. **The read.** `recordingStage: { released, rules: "DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1" }`; `years[].stage`: `{ stage, components: [{ componentId, stage, criteria }] }` or `null`; the open flag `DEPRECIATION_STAGE_NOT_RELEASED` with `details: { stage, releasedStage, components }` on each year above the released stage, counted in `review.open`, whether recording is on or off. At the owner level the stage is the asset's (from the property level). No figure, reason, status or other flag changes.
7. **ACC8.** The Einbauküche no longer raises ACC8's building (236-1; asserted in `phase-8-acceptance.e2e.test.ts`: no kitchen component in the building's 2027 stage, the kitchen's own read `MOVABLE_ASSET`, stage 2). Its acceptance test (`phase-8-acceptance.test-support.ts`) and `tax-year-afa.e2e.test.ts` still state `releasedStage: 2` (test-only), because stage 1 does not suffice for what they record: the building's own capitalised items (`CAPITALIZED_ITEM` from 2026 or 2027, Loan interest in `loan-interest-capitalized.e2e.test.ts`), the separate asset itself (`MOVABLE_ASSET`), and in `tax-year-afa.e2e.test.ts` the repair's check above 15 % before its suggestion is followed (236-4). Every figure is unchanged. The reproduction support (`depreciation-reproduction.test-support.ts`) and the record-path tests that are not about stages state `3`.
8. **Not done here:** the compose smoke (a proposal in the tests above) is not added; `docker-compose.yml` and the `Dockerfile` set neither switch, so the defaults apply (recording off, stage 1).
9. **The decisions 236-2 and 236-4** (`recording-stage.ts`; tests in `recording-stage-decisions.test.ts` and `infrastructure/postgres/depreciation-recording-stage-decisions.test.ts`). **236-2:** `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE` applies to the owner's purchase components only from the year of the owner's first share reduction on: a sale by the owner counts in the year of its `economicTransferDate`, else of its `contractDate` (no transfer precedes the contract); a reduced row counts in the year of the day after its `validUntil`. Before it the purchases are judged each for itself (236-3: several purchases without a reduction stay stage 1, unchanged). **236-4:** a purchase whose check is `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` while one of its summed sources (the check's `sources`, the lower bound's list of §59F, as VC-X-38 left `effectsOf`) is not yet `CAPITALIZED` meets `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN` from the earliest `taxYear` of the summed sources on (the earliest of `affectedYears`, or earlier where a straddling source, never suggested as a whole, comes first). `PurchaseCheckFacts` gains `summedSources: [{ taxYear, treatment }]`, read in the same snapshot. Once every summed source is `CAPITALIZED` the fact ends and the items carry their own stage (`CAPITALIZED_ITEM`, `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CAPITALIZATION`). **The mapping is unchanged:** `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1`, its nine criteria and its pinned hash stay as they are (the fact meets an existing criterion; the years are derived in code). **Reading (cautious, confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-02, third round, decision 2:** „`DISTRIBUTED_82B` zählt bei 236-4 wie `DEDUCTIBLE`. … So wie umgesetzt.“**):** a summed source classified `DISTRIBUTED_82B` (also counted by the check, §58B) counts as not followed like `DEDUCTIBLE`; distributed maintenance is still not capitalised, and a suggestion not followed stays not followed however many years the deduction runs. **The year of the first reduction** (236-2 as implemented here) is narrowed by the owner's decision 3 of the third round: only a reduction at which more than one purchase of the owner is active starts the criterion (implemented by #246, VC-X-45 follow-up 2: item 10).
10. **The decisions of the third round** (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-02; VC-X-45 follow-up 2; `recording-stage.ts`; tests in `recording-stage-decisions.test.ts` and `infrastructure/postgres/depreciation-recording-stage-layers.test.ts`). **Decision 3:** `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE` applies to the owner's purchase components from the year of the owner's first share reduction (as in 9: a sale by the owner, or the day after a reduced row) **at which more than one purchase of that owner is active**; a reduction while one purchase is active starts nothing, and a later purchase does not reach back to it. **"Active" as read here** (the reading of "VC-X-45 follow-up 2"), from the facts the derived schedule already gives per owner part of a purchase component (no new fact, no change to the schedule): an owner part of the Party with `acquiredShare` above 0 (it bought a share, §28.1A; a part whose share did not increase is no layer) whose `tenure.from` (the economic transfer) is on or before the reduction day and whose `tenure.lastDay`, if any, is not before the day before it (not wholly sold before the reduction; a part this very reduction ends still counts). The tenure is the schedule's (§28.1A, `PRO_RATA_ALL_COMPONENTS`): on the row model the database enforces (one row per owner and day) a purchase stays active while the owner's holding continues from its transfer, and ends only when the owner holds nothing. A reduction on the day of the second purchase's transfer counts it as active. A part whose start or last day the schedule does not know (`TRANSFER_DATE_MISSING`; a not-computable component has no `lastDay`) counts as active (the cautious reading). **Decision 2:** `DISTRIBUTED_82B` counts like `DEDUCTIBLE` (the reading of 9, confirmed; no change, pinned by a test). `openProposalFrom` returns `null` explicitly for a check `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` without a summed source (before, `every` on the empty list already gave `null`; the guard makes it explicit). **The mapping is unchanged:** `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1`, its criteria and its pinned hash stay as they are; no migration, no route, no figure changes.

### Superseded by the decisions of 2026-11-02, second round (to implement: VC-X-45 follow-up)

Stage 1 as implemented above stays in force until the follow-up lands; nothing here changes code. Each point names what it replaces:
1. **236-1, excluded items** (replaces "As implemented" 4): the building no longer counts an item a separate asset holds (no `kind: "EXCLUDED_ITEM"` component in the building's years, no `MOVABLE_ASSET` from it); the separate asset's own components keep their criteria. ACC8's building is then judged on its own components only: the owner's decision expects stage 1 from 2027 („ACC8 bleibt damit ab 2027 auf Stufe 1“). The follow-up states ACC8's stage per year and asset from its facts, and names any year that another criterion of the building (a capitalised item, `CAPITALIZED_ITEM`) still raises, rather than forcing a stage.
2. **236-2, the years of `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE`** (replaces this spec's reading of every active year, which "As implemented" 3 follows): only the active years from the year of the owner's first share reduction (a sale by the owner or a day on which the owner holds less than the day before, as "As implemented" 3 defines it) on. The years before are judged per purchase (stage 1 unless another criterion applies).
3. **236-3, confirmed:** several purchases of one owner without a share reduction stay stage 1 (already so; the follow-up keeps its test).
4. **236-4, `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` with a suggestion not yet followed** (new; A1 as implemented does not raise it): `ANSCHAFFUNGSNAHE_CHECK_OPEN` on the purchase from the year of the first summed source on while a summed source is still `DEDUCTIBLE`, read from Taxation's check in the same snapshot (`depreciation-purchase-checks.ts`, `effectsOf`), as A1's facts are.
5. **236-5, the release criteria:** docs only (`freigabe-afa-erfassung.md`); no code.

**Tests the follow-up must have:** an excluded item leaves the building's stage as without it, and the separate asset's own read and record still carry `MOVABLE_ASSET`; ACC8's stages per year and asset (the e2e and the acceptance test state the released stage they need, with the reason in a comment); `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE` absent before the year of the first reduction and present from it, for a sale and for a reduced row; several purchases without a reduction stage 1; `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` with one summed source still `DEDUCTIBLE` → stage 2 from the year of the first summed source and not before; all followed → the purchase no longer raised by the fact, the items stage 2 by their own criteria; `NOT_ABOVE_THRESHOLD` and a running window alone → stage 1 (A1 unchanged); `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1`'s pinned hash unchanged. **Mutations** (each alone): an excluded item counted again; `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE` in every active year; the `ABOVE_THRESHOLD` fact ignored, or applied to every active year of the purchase, or kept after every source is followed.

### Decided on 2026-11-02, third round: what follows (VC-X-45 follow-up 2)

**Implemented by #246** (VC-X-45 follow-up 2; "As implemented" 10); the decisions below are unchanged. Productive recording stays disabled, only stage 1 shipped. Decisions (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-02):
1. **Decision 1, ACC8 from 2027: confirmed, no change.** „ACC8 bleibt ab 2027 auf Stufe 1“ (236-1) meant the effect of the excluded item only. ACC8's building carries its own capitalised items from 2027 (`CAPITALIZED_ITEM`, stage 2), so its 2027 stays stage 2, as "As implemented" 7 states and the acceptance tests assert (`releasedStage: 2`, test-only). `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1` and its mapping stay unchanged.
2. **Decision 2, `DISTRIBUTED_82B` like `DEDUCTIBLE` under 236-4: confirmed, no change** ("As implemented" 9, the cautious reading, is the decision). Its existing test stands.
3. **Decision 3, the start of `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE`** (narrows 236-2 as implemented in "As implemented" 3 and 9): the criterion applies to the owner's purchase components from the year of the owner's **first share reduction at which more than one purchase of that owner is active**. A reduction while only one purchase of the owner is active does not start it (with one purchase there is nothing to split pro rata), nor does a later purchase reach back to it (a later purchase is a new layer). The reduction is defined as in "As implemented" 3 and 9 (a sale by the owner, in the year of its `economicTransferDate`, else its `contractDate`; a reduced row, in the year of the day after its `validUntil`). **The reading taken here** of "active": a purchase component of the owner that has begun on the day of the reduction (its economic transfer on or before that day) and has not ended (not wholly sold before it); the follow-up names it in the code and asks the owner where a case falls between. Several purchases without such a reduction stay stage 1 (236-3, unchanged). The mapping's criteria and stages are unchanged: `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1` stays `@1`, its pinned hash too (the years are derived in code).

**Tests the follow-up must have** (in `recording-stage-decisions.test.ts` and its repository test): an owner with one purchase who sells a part in 2026 and buys a second share in 2027, with no later reduction → `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE` in no year (both purchases stage 1 unless another criterion applies); the same owner reducing again in 2028 → the criterion from 2028 on and not in 2026 or 2027; two purchases active at a reduction in 2027 → from 2027 on (236-2 unchanged); each for a sale and for a reduced row; a reduction on the day of the second purchase's transfer, by the reading above; several purchases without a reduction → stage 1 (236-3); `DE_RECORDING_STAGES@1`'s pinned hash unchanged; the record command's `409 STAGE_NOT_RELEASED` `details` naming the criterion only in its years; unchanged money sums of the schedule; no AuditRecord from a read; Realm isolation. **Mutations** (each alone): the first reduction counted whatever the number of active purchases (236-2 as implemented now); a later purchase reaching back to an earlier reduction; the criterion in every active year.

### Not in VC-X-45 (pointers)

- Releasing stage 2 or 3: each needs its own documented owner decision (above), one entry per stage in `docs/development/freigabe-afa-erfassung.md` once that stage's criteria are met (decided 2026-11-02, second round, 236-5; "Releasing stage 2 or 3" below). Enabling recording: §60 "Turning it on".
- A stage per Realm, a stage in the tax-year view, re-versioning recorded versions: not proposed.

### Releasing stage 2 or 3 (decided 2026-11-02, second round, 236-5)

- **One owner decision per stage, in the release protocol** `docs/development/freigabe-afa-erfassung.md`, **never a calendar date.** Each stage has its checklist there; the decision is taken only when every point of it is met, with the evidence of each point named, and the note of A5 for every written confirmation. Releasing stage 2 does not release stage 3.
- **Stage 1** is released by the first enablement of recording (§60 "Turning it on"). **VC-X-41 Part 2 lands before it** (Entscheidung des Projektinhabers, 2026-11-02, §59G "Decided on 2026-11-02 (chat): what follows for Part 2"): not for its cases, which stay stage 3, but because it changes `shorterUsefulLife.fromEvidenceYear` and `subsequentCostRate.shorterLife`, which freeze at that enablement.
- **Stage 2** needs: VC-X-27, VC-X-36 and VC-X-38 implemented; a stage-1 year recorded productively; the owner's real annual statement (Jahresabrechnung) run through phases 6 to 8; the written confirmation of questions 14 to 17 and 23 of the tax review.
- **Stage 3** needs: VC-X-41 implemented in both parts; questions 8, 9, 11 and 12 answered in writing; the advisor's written confirmation of §59G's open questions 2 (the switch from January) and 11 (the residual value when the declared AfA differs), decided by the owner on 2026-11-02;
 a sample case (Musterfall) with its expected result green, as the report recommends under G. **It presupposes stage 2's criteria** (decided by the owner on 2026-11-02, third round: „Stufe 3 setzt die Kriterien von Stufe 2 voraus, ja.“): a released stage 3 also records every stage-2 year, so stage 2's checklist is met first.
- Then, as above: the operator's setting of `DEPRECIATION_RECORDING_STAGE` and a restart. A stage released is recorded in this section and in `docs/development/phase-8-plan.md` too.

2. ~~The years `SEVERAL_PURCHASES_PARTIAL_SALE` applies to~~ **decided 2026-11-02, second round (236-2):** from the year of the first share reduction on (to implement: VC-X-45 follow-up).
3. ~~**ACC8 from 2027**~~ **decided 2026-11-02, third round (decision 1): the reading taken here is confirmed**; 2027 stays stage 2 and the mapping is unchanged („Mein Satz meinte nur die Wirkung des ausgeschlossenen Items.“). The question was (raised by recording 236-1): the decision expects ACC8 to stay at stage 1 from 2027; ACC8's building also holds capitalised items (`CAPITALIZED_ITEM`, stage 2) from 2027. Does „ACC8 bleibt ab 2027 auf Stufe 1“ refer to the excluded item's effect only (the reading taken here), or should the building's 2027 be stage 1 as a whole?

# 61. Market Valuation API

### Queries

```text
GET /api/v1/property-references/{propertyReferenceId}/market-valuations
GET /api/v1/market-valuations/{id}
```

### Commands

```text
POST /api/v1/market-valuations
POST /api/v1/market-valuations/{id}/confirm
```

Never expose:

```text
PATCH Property.currentMarketValue
```

# 62. Investment Metric API

### Queries

```text
GET /api/v1/property-references/{propertyReferenceId}/metrics
GET /api/v1/property-references/{propertyReferenceId}/metrics/{metricCode}
GET /api/v1/portfolios/{id}/metrics
```

Metrics are read-only derived outputs.

---

# 63. Metric Calculation

```text
POST /api/v1/investment/calculations
```

Request:

```json
{
  "scopeType": "PROPERTY",
  "propertyReferenceId": "...",
  "asOfDate": "2028-12-31",
  "metricCodes": ["NOI", "LTV", "CCR"]
}
```

Response should include:

- value
- formula version
- important input references
- warnings
- calculation timestamp

# 64. Investment Metric Snapshot API

### Queries

```text
GET /api/v1/investment-metric-snapshots
GET /api/v1/investment-metric-snapshots/{id}
```

### Commands

```text
POST /api/v1/investment-metric-snapshots
POST /api/v1/property-references/{propertyReferenceId}/snapshot-metrics
```

Snapshot generation is explicit.

Trigger policy may evolve later.

# 65. Investment Scenario API

Post-MVP or later MVP phase.

### Queries

```text
GET /api/v1/investment-scenarios
GET /api/v1/investment-scenarios/{id}
```

### Commands

```text
POST /api/v1/investment-scenarios
PUT  /api/v1/investment-scenarios/{id}/assumptions
POST /api/v1/investment-scenarios/{id}/calculate
```

# 66. Scenario Isolation

Scenario calculation endpoints must never update:

- actual rent
- actual Transactions
- actual Loan terms
- current Market Valuation

# 67. Reporting API

### Queries / Generation

```text
POST /api/v1/reports/property-summary
POST /api/v1/reports/tax-package
POST /api/v1/reports/annual-summary
POST /api/v1/reports/portfolio-summary
```

Report creation must call domain calculations.

It must not implement hidden formulas.

---

# 68. Tax Package

Example:

```text
POST /api/v1/reports/tax-package
```

Request:

```json
{
  "propertyReferenceId": "...",
  "taxYear": 2027,
  "ownerPartyIds": ["..."]
}
```

Output may provide:

- downloadable archive
- report manifest
- missing-review warnings

---

# 69. Dashboard Query API

Dashboards should use dedicated read models where performance requires.

Example:

```text
GET /api/v1/dashboard/properties/{id}
```

Response may aggregate:

- rent status from MRE
- cashflow from Ledger
- remaining debt from Financing
- tax status
- current valuation
- metrics

This is a read model only.

---

# 70. Composite Read Models

Composite API responses are allowed for UI efficiency.

They must not become canonical owners of data.

Example:

```text
PropertyDashboardView
```

may include copies of:

- Property name
- rent due
- cashflow
- debt
- valuation

but these fields remain derived/read-only.

---

# 71. Search API

A future cross-domain search may exist:

```text
GET /api/v1/search?q=...
```

Search results should return references, not independent domain state.

---

# 72. Automation API

### Queries

```text
GET /api/v1/automation-rules
```

### Commands

```text
POST /api/v1/automation-rules
POST /api/v1/automation-rules/{id}/enable
POST /api/v1/automation-rules/{id}/disable
POST /api/v1/automation-rules/{id}/test
```

### Queries

```text
GET /api/v1/ai-suggestions
GET /api/v1/ai-suggestions/{id}
```

### Commands

```text
POST /api/v1/ai-suggestions/{id}/reject
```

# 74. AI Transaction Classification Flow

```text
Transaction
    ↓
POST /ai/classification-suggestions
    ↓
AISuggestion
    ↓
User accepts
    ↓
PUT /transactions/{id}/splits
    ↓
POST /transactions/{id}/confirm
```

AI never skips the canonical command path.

---

# 75. MRE Adapter API Responsibilities

The internal MRE adapter should expose capabilities such as:

```text
listRealms()
getProperty()
listProperties()
getTenant()
listTenants()
getTenantRents()
getRentTerm()
recordRentPayment()
getLeaseDefinition()
getDocument()
```

The rest of the DE system should not call arbitrary MRE endpoints directly.

---

# 76. MRE Adapter Anti-Corruption Layer

MRE-specific field names should be translated at the adapter boundary.

Example:

MRE:

```text
Occupant
guaranty
leaseId
properties[]
```

DE integration model:

```text
RentalContractReference
expectedSecurityDeposit
propertyReferences
```

The DE domain must not become polluted with MRE implementation naming.

---

# 77. External System Error Handling

If MRE is unavailable:

- DE canonical data remains accessible
- MRE-dependent operations fail visibly
- errors are marked external
- no partial canonical state should be silently written

Example:

`MRE_UNAVAILABLE`

---

# 78. MRE Write-Back Safety

Any DE command that writes to MRE should:

1. validate DE state
2. verify Realm
3. use idempotency
4. call MRE supported API
5. record result
6. create audit event
7. avoid direct DB write

---

# 79. Bank Adapter Boundary

Future bank APIs should also sit behind an adapter.

The Financial Ledger must not depend on one bank vendor.

Conceptual interface:

```text
listAccounts()
listTransactions()
getTransaction()
```

Initial implementation may be CSV-only.

---

# 80. Import API Semantics

Imported records begin as non-confirmed unless explicitly trusted.

Recommended flow:

```text
Imported
→ Unreviewed
→ Classified
→ Confirmed
→ Reconciled
```

---

# 81. Batch Commands

Batch endpoints are acceptable when they preserve individual validation results.

Example:

```text
POST /api/v1/transactions/batch-confirm
```

Response should report per-item success/failure.

Do not make partial failures invisible.

---

# 82. Pagination

Collection endpoints should support pagination.

Recommended query:

```text
?page=1&pageSize=50
```

Large transaction datasets should additionally support cursor-based pagination later if needed.

---

# 83. Sorting

Use explicit fields:

```text
?sort=bookingDate:desc
```

Only allow approved sortable fields.

---

# 84. Filtering

Prefer semantic query fields over arbitrary database query syntax.

Good:

```text
?status=CONFIRMED&propertyReferenceId=...
```

Avoid exposing raw Mongo operators or SQL fragments.

---

# 85. Date Range Filtering

Use:

```text
?from=2026-01-01&to=2026-12-31
```

Date semantics must be documented per endpoint.

---

# 86. Money Representation

JSON Money should not use binary floating values.

Preferred conceptual shape:

```json
{
  "amount": "1250.00",
  "currency": "EUR"
}
```

Exact serialization may be standardized later.

---

# 87. Percentage Representation

Use one consistent convention.

Recommended API representation:

```json
{
  "share": "0.50"
}
```

for 50%.

Documentation must state this globally.

**Exception: ownership shares** are exact fractions `"n/d"` (P2-D3, §26.1), never decimal strings: `1/3` has no exact decimal.

---

# 88. Dates and Timestamps

Business dates:

```text
YYYY-MM-DD
```

A business date must be a real calendar date with a year from **1900 to 2100**. Other years are refused as `OUT_OF_RANGE` (a typo such as `0202` would otherwise book into the year 202); malformed or impossible dates are `INVALID_FORMAT`.

System timestamps:

```text
RFC 3339 / ISO 8601
```

Avoid locale-formatted dates in DE API contracts.

MRE adapter is responsible for translating MRE-specific date formatting where necessary.

---

# 89. Review Warnings

Responses may include non-blocking warnings.

Example:

```json
{
  "warnings": [
    {
      "code": "TAX_CLASSIFICATION_NEEDS_REVIEW",
      "sourceEntityId": "..."
    }
  ]
}
```

Warnings must not be confused with errors.

---

# 90. Validation Error Detail

Example:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "Validation failed.",
    "details": {
      "fields": [
        {
          "field": "share",
          "code": "OUT_OF_RANGE"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

A rule over existing data is not a field error: a share that would raise a day's sum above 1 is `422 OWNERSHIP_TOTAL_EXCEEDS_ONE` with the day and its sum (§26.1).

---

# 91. Derived Data Traceability

Derived endpoints should expose enough metadata to explain results.

Example metric response:

```json
{
  "metricCode": "LTV",
  "value": "0.68",
  "formulaVersion": "1",
  "inputs": {
    "marketValuationId": "...",
    "loanIds": ["..."]
  }
}
```

---

# 92. Audit API

Read-only audit queries:

```text
GET /api/v1/audit-records
GET /api/v1/entities/{entityType}/{entityId}/audit-records
```

Audit history should not be editable through normal user APIs.

---

# 93. Health APIs

Operational endpoints:

```text
GET /health
GET /ready
```

May expose dependency status such as:

- database
- MRE
- document storage

Do not leak secrets.

---

# 94. Capability Discovery

Optional future endpoint:

```text
GET /api/v1/capabilities
```

May indicate:

- MRE connected
- banking import enabled
- OCR enabled
- AI enabled
- tax rules available

Useful for modular deployments.

---

# 95. API Documentation

The implementation should eventually provide machine-readable OpenAPI documentation.

Every public endpoint should document:

- authorization
- inputs
- outputs
- error codes
- idempotency
- side effects
- domain owner

---

# 96. API Test Strategy

Each business command requires tests for:

- success path
- validation
- authorization
- duplicate/idempotency
- concurrency
- audit creation
- domain invariants

Integration endpoints additionally require MRE contract tests.

---

# 97. Contract Tests Against MRE

At minimum:

- Property retrieval
- Tenant retrieval
- rent retrieval
- payment write-back
- Lease retrieval
- Realm access isolation

MRE version upgrades must run these tests.

---

# 98. API Anti-Patterns

## Anti-Pattern 1 — Generic CRUD Everywhere

Avoid:

```text
PATCH /entity/{id}
```

for domain transitions with important meaning.

---

## Anti-Pattern 2 — Raw Database API

Never expose:

```text
/query?filter={$and:[...]}
```

---

## Anti-Pattern 3 — UI-Owned Business Logic

The API must expose calculated business results rather than require the frontend to reproduce formulas.

---

## Anti-Pattern 4 — Derived Value Update

Never expose:

```text
PATCH /metrics/LTV
```

---

## Anti-Pattern 5 — Direct AI Write

Never expose an AI path that bypasses canonical commands.

---

## Anti-Pattern 6 — Direct MRE DB Write

All MRE mutations use supported adapter/API paths.

---

## Anti-Pattern 7 — Hidden Cross-Domain Mutation

A Tax command must not silently rewrite Financial Ledger data.

---

# 100. Deferred API Surface

Initially defer:

# 101. Recommended API Module Layout

Conceptually:

```text
api/
├── integration/
│   └── mre/
├── parties/
├── properties/
├── ownership/
├── acquisitions/
├── ledger/
├── financing/
├── deposits/
├── weg/
├── maintenance/
├── documents/
├── taxation/
├── depreciation/
├── investment/
├── reporting/
├── automation/
└── ai/
```

This is logical module structure, not necessarily separate services.

---

# 102. Command Naming Rule

Commands should use domain language.

Preferred:

```text
confirmTransaction()
reconcileRentPayment()
closeOwnership()
recalculateDepreciation()
```

Avoid:

```text
updateRecord()
setStatus()
saveData()
```

---

# 103. Query Naming Rule

Queries should describe user intent.

Preferred:

```text
getPropertyDashboard()
getOutstandingRentReconciliations()
getTaxYearSummary()
```

Avoid exposing persistence terminology.

---

# 104. Internal vs External APIs

Not every internal capability must be publicly exposed.

Example:

`recalculateAllDerivedMetrics()` may remain an internal service operation.

Public API should remain intentionally small.

---

# 105. API Evolution Rule

When adding a new endpoint, contributors must verify:

- Which domain owns the operation?
- Is this a query or command?
- Does it duplicate an existing capability?
- Does it expose implementation details?
- Can it violate accepted ADRs?
- Is it idempotent where necessary?
- Is audit behavior defined?
- Are MRE dependencies isolated?

---

# 106. AI Coding Agent Guidance

AI coding agents implementing APIs must:

- follow business command semantics
- avoid generic CRUD shortcuts
- preserve domain ownership
- use FinancialAccount naming
- use RentalContractReference rather than assuming MRE Lease is the full contract
- use MRE adapter interfaces
- implement reconciliation explicitly
- never create Ledger Transactions from MRE payments without provenance
- never expose editable derived metrics
- include tests for invariants
- surface ADR conflicts instead of bypassing them

---

# 107. Open API Decisions

## API-OPEN-001 — Authentication Token Sharing

How exactly should the DE API validate or reuse MRE authentication tokens?

**Direction accepted (ADR-034):** reuse MRE authentication + Realm authority. The exact token validation/propagation mechanism is an implementation spike (per TECH-ADR-005), not a new architecture decision.

---

## API-OPEN-002 — Organization Context Transport

Should Realm context be encoded primarily in:

- token claims
- header
- route
- combination

Implementation-level under ADR-034 (Realm authority reused); Realm membership must be verified server-side regardless of transport.

**Resolved at implementation level (VC-0-08):** the Realm is sent in the `organizationid` request header — the same header the MRE landlord API uses — and verified server-side against MRE on every `/api/v1` request (`mre-integration.md` §47.1). Route scoping may be added later where a resource path naturally carries the Realm.

---

## API-OPEN-003 — MRE Payment ID Limitation

How should reconciliation fingerprints be represented until MRE has stable payment IDs?

---

## API-OPEN-004 — Correction Endpoint Semantics

Should correction create:

- replacement record
- reversal + replacement
- versioned mutation

**Resolved by ADR-037:** reversal + replacement (confirmed transactions are immutable).

---

## API-OPEN-005 — Async Jobs

Large reports, imports and OCR may eventually require job APIs.

The initial MVP should avoid asynchronous infrastructure unless necessary.

---

## API-OPEN-006 — GraphQL

No need exists currently.

REST-like business APIs are preferred for the MVP.

GraphQL may be reconsidered only if composite query requirements justify it.

---

# 108. Final API Principle

The API should expose the business model the user understands.

It should not expose the database model the developer happens to use.

The correct abstraction chain is:

```text
User Intent
   ↓
Business Capability
   ↓
Domain Command / Query
   ↓
Domain Model
   ↓
Persistence / MRE Adapter
```

Never reverse this chain.

---

# Closing Statement

The API of Vermieter Cockpit DE is not intended to be a thin CRUD layer over storage.

It is the executable contract of the domain model.

Its role is to protect:

- financial truth
- domain boundaries
- historical traceability
- MRE compatibility
- human review
- reproducible calculations

The best API endpoint is not the one that exposes the most flexibility.

It is the one that makes the correct business action explicit and the incorrect state difficult or impossible to create.

> Commands express intent.  
> Queries explain state.  
> Adapters isolate external systems.  
> Reconciliation connects realities without merging them.
